result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / ownership / public surface, for `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue` (demo/shell)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-18 — the dock's "certified chrome ink" referent is read off `.glass-dock`, a node that paints nothing under Glass 7 (measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` in both schemes; the paint is on the `.dock-plate` child, measured α 0.5392 light / 0.5776 dark). `resolveLiveTint` therefore returns `undefined` on every call and the static model it exists to distrust (α 0.80/0.88) serves every certification on the dock band, unnoticed since the W44 Glass 7 adoption. The mechanism is a demo feature module (`demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:152`) reaching across two package boundaries into a producer-private DOM class by `document.querySelector` — the weakest coupling the language offers, for a value the producer already computes, serving exactly one consumer (`ProfileSection.vue:28`, the dock).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but three axes were checked and found sound and are recorded as such in the report: (1) no demo file reaches into `src/` or `dist/` — all 50 value.js import sites use published `package.json#exports` subpaths (`grep -rho '@mkbabb/value.js[a-z/]*' demo | sort | uniq -c` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize, 1 bare inside a comment); Dock.vue imports the library not at all, correct for chrome. (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` holds across the whole dock subtree, and it is load-bearing: because `Dock.vue:24`'s `import type { DockActionBar }` is erased, the dock's runtime graph is 65 modules rather than the 195 that `usePaneRouter` itself pulls (measured, L-graph2.mjs). (3) `main` = 1 and `nav` = 1 on 60/60 audit captures and live; the producer's inert/aria-hidden packaging of inactive dock faces is correct (measured `inert:true, visibility:hidden` at rest).

defects.defect: The chrome-tier ink referent probes a node that paints nothing: `resolveLiveTint("chrome")` reads `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.glass-dock')).backgroundColor`, which is fully transparent under Glass 7 — the glass is painted on the `.dock-plate` child. The live probe returns undefined on every call and the static model silently serves.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:150-153 (the querySelector) and :217 (`if (!resolved || resolved.alpha === 0) return undefined`). Measured live (scratchpad L-probe5.mjs, /#/, 1280x900, dock expanded): light {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.931227 0.845921 0.816039 / 0.5392)"} ; dark {"dockBg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","plateBg":"color(srgb 0.390298 0.334077 0.29024 / 0.5776)"}. Producer paint site: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/morph.css `.glass-dock:not(.vertical) .dock-plate { background: color-mix(...) }`. Static fallback now in force: demo/color-session/ink.ts:29-35 RUNG_ALPHA.floating = {light 0.8, dark 0.88}, FLOATING_TINT_L = {light 1, dark 0.345}, applied to chrome at ink.ts:118-122. Sole consumer of the tier: `grep -rn 'useSafeAccentFn("chrome")' demo` -> demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:28.
defects.mechanism: Cross-package boundary violation: a demo feature module reaches a producer's internal paint value through a DOM class-name query instead of a published token/contract. Untyped, unexported, untested — so a producer paint change (Glass 7, adopted whole at V·W44) un-wires it silently.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe5.mjs against the live dev server on localhost:9000 — prints dockBg rgba(0,0,0,0) and the real plateBg with alpha 0.5392/0.5776 in light/dark. Consequence example (labelled: assumed ambient L 0.75): surfaceLightness = a*L + (1-a)*ambient gives 0.95 modelled vs 0.83 measured — ink certified against a surface an eighth of the OKLab range too light. e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:594-635 measures only the outcome at one boot colour and never asserts the live probe returned anything.
defects.proposedCure: The referent is the producer's own composited value, so the producer publishes it: glass-ui exposes `--glass-tint-chrome` (resolved) or `useDockSurfaceTint()` on the existing DockContext, and the demo reads a token, never a node. The `chrome` branch — and the identical `querySelector('[data-surface="veil"]')` idiom at :170-176 — then collapse to token reads with no DOM archaeology. Interim `.glass-dock .dock-plate` is another line of the same wrong kind and will break on the next paint change. Secondary: the selector is document-order dependent — two `.glass-dock` elements exist on /#/atmosphere and /#/blob (demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:164); measured firstIsShell:true today, breakage on re-order is a hypothesis.

defects.defect: `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch defined by two disagreeing predicates. After one visit to a tuning route the dock wears admin identity (gold shimmer glyph + gold `--dock-ring`) on every subsequent non-admin route for the rest of the session.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:32 seeds the ref with a PREFIX test `currentView.startsWith("admin-")`; :55-59 maintains it with a MEMBERSHIP test `adminViews.includes(view)` and has no falsifying arm. The two predicates disagree on `atmosphere`/`blob` (in the array at :27, not prefixed). Reproduced live (scratchpad L-probe6.mjs, headless Chromium 1280x900): `1 fresh picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":false,"ring":"oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.8340"}` / `2 -> atmosphere {"goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `3 back() -> picker {"route":"#/","goldIcon":true,"ring":"light-dark(oklch(0.751 0.147 8"}` / `4 -> palettes {"goldIcon":true,...}`.
defects.mechanism: Duplicated state for a value that is a pure function of the route, with the predicate implemented twice and neither copy owned by the schema that owns views (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe6.mjs — load /#/ (gold false), hash to /#/atmosphere (gold true), page.goBack() to /#/ (gold STILL true), hash to /#/palettes (gold STILL true). With admin credentials the damage is functional, not cosmetic: viewEntries (:34-39) then returns only the seven admin views while on /#/palettes, so the dock's own navigation cannot reach the user views except through the `__admin_toggle__` sentinel row.
defects.proposedCure: Derive, do not latch. Add `group: "user" | "admin"` to `PaneConfig` (viewSchema.ts owns the partition) and reduce the composable to `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[viewManager.currentView.value].group === "admin")`. The ref, both watchers and both hardcoded ViewId arrays die; `toggleAdminMode` keeps its real job (it navigates) and the flag follows the route by construction — the same transposition `useViewManager.ts:51-58` already applied to `mobilePaneIndex`.

defects.defect: The local `useLayerTransition` shim in ActionBarLayer produces no crossfade at all: the producer CSS the template hand-binds declares no opacity transition, so the 260 ms timer window is an instant cut with a transparent inert box held over the live controls.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62-94 (the shim, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260, subLayerProps hand-binding `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer rules: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)` on `.dock-layer`; the opacity overlap lives on `.dock-crossfade[data-crossfading] > .dock-face` via `--dock-t` (crossfade.css), reachable only inside `<DockCrossfade>`. Measured live (scratchpad L-probe2.mjs), both faces at rest / +60ms / +460ms across the actions->input swap: `transitionProperty: "visibility", transitionDuration: "0s"` at every phase; opacity steps 1->0 and 0->1 in one frame; the leaving face holds a 442x45 transparent inert box. The public successor exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:5 `export { default as DockCrossfade } from "./DockCrossfade.vue";` — contradicting the shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:54-61.
defects.mechanism: A local fork of a retired producer concept, styled out of the producer's private stylesheet by class-name convention; the fork reimplements the packaging but cannot reach the animation, which the producer moved behind a component.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe2.mjs — navigate /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], sample getComputedStyle on both children of `.dock-layer-grid` at 60 ms and 460 ms. transition-property is `visibility` and duration `0s` in all four phases.
defects.proposedCure: Replace ActionBarLayer.vue:62-101 with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. The shim, the 260 ms literal, the timer, `subLayerProps`, `subLayerGridEl`, the `void opts.containerEl` parity argument and the hand-bound producer classes all die (~40 lines), and the producer's spring-driven overlap, peak-size reserve and focus transfer from a dissolving face arrive instead of being approximated.

defects.defect: The document heading outline is inverted, not merely missing an h1: the page's most prominent title is an H3 whose own subsections are H2s. No module owns heading level.
defects.evidence: h1 = 0 on 60/60 captures (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md per-capture table) and live. Live outline (scratchpad L-probe.mjs, /#/, 1280x900, document order): ['H3:92.0%,88.8,20.0', 'H3:About the color spaces, La', 'H2:Basic Information', 'H2:Components', 'H2:Key Properties', 'H2:Conversion Graph', 'H2:Usage', 'H2:Detailed Guide', 'H3:Attributes', 'H3:Historical Context']. `grep -rn '<h1' demo --include=*.vue | wc -l` -> 0. The datum exists in the right place with exactly one consumer: demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:104-233 `label` per view, read only by demo/color-picker/router/useDocumentTitle.ts:47-56 (`composeTitle`).
defects.mechanism: Half-owned document identity: the title half declares a canonical owner, the outline half has no owner, so each pane picks a heading level to match a font size.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe.mjs — reads document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,...') in order on the live picker route. A screen-reader outline reads: (no title) -> level 3 'About the color spaces' -> level 2 'Basic Information' — the child outranks its parent.
defects.proposedCure:
Extend the existing owner rather than adding one: `useDocumentTitle` becomes `useDocumentIdentity(route)` returning `{ title, heading }` from the same `viewSchema` row, the shell renders `

{{ heading }}

` as the first child of App.vue's `
`, and panes start at `h2` by rule. Note the fix cannot land in Dock.vue — the dock is the `
` landmark and a nav cannot own the document heading; CARRY-LEDGER W47's 'main/H1/active-subtree = 1' clause is unowned in code, which is why the wave never noticed.

defects.defect: The demo's declared view of the published library surface has drifted from `package.json#exports`: tsconfig.demo.json maps a nonexistent `dist/index.d.ts`, declares two subpaths that are not exported, and omits two that are — while calling itself a mirror of the generated Vite alias set.
defects.evidence: `package.json#exports` keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.' root. tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index*` -> no matches found), plus `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports; no src/subpaths/parsing.ts or units.ts — `ls src/subpaths` -> color, css, easing, math, quantize, transform, value), and omit `/value` and `/css` (both exported; `/css` used 10x in demo and 4x inside glass-ui's dist). The file's header calls this 'the 8 public keys' / 'a CLOSED 8-key set' that 'mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map'; vite.config.ts:41-50 generates one alias per exports entry -> 7 aliases and no bare-root alias.
defects.mechanism: A hand-maintained declaration of a generated surface: the runtime alias set is derived from exports, the type paths are not, so the two views of the public API drift silently.
defects.reproduction: NONE — latent, not live. No demo file imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (`grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js"' demo` -> the only hit is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12), and glass-ui's three specifiers (/color, /css, /easing, measured in its dist) are all covered by the generated alias set, so one instance serves the running app. Were the bare specifier ever written it would resolve to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 — the published copy npm installed for glass-ui's peer dep — a second instance of this library behind an undeclared specifier.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig `paths` from `package.json#exports` exactly as the Vite aliases already are (one loader, one source of truth), or add a real `"."` export plus `dist/index.d.ts`. Either way the two declarations of the public surface cannot drift apart again — this is the axis T.W1's dogfood keystone was fought over.

defects.defect: Inverted dependency: the shell's persistent chrome imports its identity/session port from the palettes FEATURE, putting 23 palettes modules into the dock's runtime graph on every route.
defects.evidence: Five of the six `SESSION_PORT_KEY` consumers are dock files: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13 — the sixth is the definition in demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts. Runtime-only import-graph walk from Dock.vue (scratchpad L-graph2.mjs, `import type` edges correctly excluded as erased): 65 modules total, area histogram {"demo/shell":20,"demo/color-session":6,"demo/ui":7,"demo/platform":9,"demo/palettes":23}. The payload is pure identity (usePalettePorts.ts Port 1: isAdminAuthenticated, userSlug, userLogout, ensureUser, ensureSession, onRegenerateSlug, onSlugSwitch) assembled from demo/platform/auth/{useAdminAuth,useUserAuth,useSession} — which already exist as the proper home.
defects.mechanism: A feature owns a platform concept; the shell must reach down into the feature to render chrome, creating the palettes<->shell module cycle.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-graph2.mjs — 23 of the dock's 65 runtime modules are demo/palettes. The picker, admin and 404 routes all instantiate palette machinery to render a Login button.
defects.proposedCure: Move the port to demo/platform/auth/session.ts exporting `SESSION_KEY: InjectionKey<Session>`, provided at the composition root; usePalettePorts consumes it like every other consumer. `shell -> palettes` goes 5 -> 0 and the cycle dissolves.

defects.id: L-7 (carried, sharpened with a live measurement)
defects.defect: MT-F005 located: the app's single nameless button is a hand-rolled `<button>` inside the dock's ColorInput — the one control in the dock subtree that bypasses the design-system primitive, and therefore the one that lost the accessible name the primitive enforces.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:67-82 — both branches are `<button class="send-btn btn-interactive">` with only an SVG child, no aria-label, no text, no title. It is the only nameless control: all 8 `<DockControl>` uses in the subtree carry aria-label (Dock.vue x3, ActionBarToggle x1, SlugEditLayer x3, ActionBarLayer x1) and the other hand-rolled button, ActionButton.vue:13, carries `:aria-label="title"`. Measured live after two clicks (scratchpad L-probe3.mjs: Toggle action bar -> Open color input): `send-btn: {"visible":true,"ariaLabel":null,"text":"","title":null,"rect":[24,24],"inertAncestor":false,"cs":{"visibility":"visible","opacity":"1"}}`. Nameless-button enumeration at rest, 1280x900 /#/: 1 hit, path `div.dock-face-content > div.flex.items-center.gap-0 > div.dock-layer-grid.flex-1 > ... > button.send-btn.btn-interactive`.
defects.mechanism: Bypassing the design-system primitive loses the affordance the primitive enforces; the dock's own written law (Dock.vue:140-142, 'icon-only controls carry aria-label') is obeyed everywhere it goes through DockControl and violated in the one place it does not.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/L-probe3.mjs — load /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], then read button.send-btn: visible, 24x24, accessible name null, no inert ancestor. Two clicks from cold boot.
defects.proposedCure: Route the send affordance through `DockControl` (or glass-ui `Button`), which carries the aria-label contract; the 24x24 box also sits at the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 floor, and since `compact` is a producer variant the size cure belongs producer-side (edict 5), not as a per-instance override.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the tier explicitly declared at spawn; seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the only focus indicator on the app's primary text-entry control is `border-color: <the user's own selected colour, alpha included>` with the UA outline explicitly suppressed (`focus-visible:outline-none`, ColorInput.vue:16 + :162-166). Measured contrast against the field's own background rgb(251,250,248): #fbfaf8 → 1.00:1; white → 1.04:1; alpha 0 → fully transparent. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 floor is 3:1. There is no forced-colors fallback either — the element matches NONE of foundation.css:702-720's focus-restoration roster (measured el.matches(roster) === false; role="textbox"/[contenteditable] are not in the roster and the element carries no tabindex attribute). And in the error state the destructive branch of `inputStyle` returns first, so the error border erases the focus border entirely. The bitter part: the app's certified contrast-safe accent (SAFE_ACCENT_KEY, computed from cssColorOpaque precisely so alpha cannot destroy contrast) IS injected in this same component at :157 — and is spent on the arrow glyph's stroke while the raw alpha-bearing cssColor takes the focus indicator.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE

defects.defect: Focus indicator is the user's raw alpha-bearing colour with the UA outline suppressed; measured contrast 1.00:1 for reachable colours; no forced-colors fallback; error state overwrites focus state.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:16 (`focus-visible:outline-none`) and :162-166 (`if (inputIsFocused.value) return { borderColor: cssColor.value }`). Live after a real click: `focused: true, outline: "none 1px rgb(0,95,204)", inlineStyle: "border-color: lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827);"`. Measured contrast vs the field's own measured background rgb(251,250,248): `#fbfaf8` → 1.00, `rgb(255 255 255)` → 1.04, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0)` → alpha 0 / invisible. Forced-colors roster membership measured via el.matches() against foundation.css:702-720: colorInput → false, sendBtn → true; colorInput attrs = [data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class] (no tabindex). Error+focus measured inline style: `border-color: var(--destructive)`. Contrast-safe primitive available and unused for this purpose: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:273-292, injected at ColorInput.vue:157 and spent on the arrow stroke at :74/:81.
defects.mechanism: Accessibility-critical state expressed through a user-data-driven decorative channel with no floor, no fallback register, and no separation from a competing state — instead of a design-system focus register.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ at >=1440px viewport → hover the dock → click `Tools` (aria-label="Toggle action bar") → click `Open color input` → drag the alpha channel slider to 0 (or set the colour to white in light mode) → click the field. Focus is undetectable. In WHCM the element matches no outline-restoration selector.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `focus-visible:outline-none` and the focus branch of `inputStyle` entirely. Focus comes from the house register — demo/styles/focus-ring.css / the `.focus-ring` class that four sibling dock controls measurably carry (measured siblingButtonsUsingFocusRing: 4, colorInput.usesFocusRing: false). Architecturally this dissolves by adopting glass-ui `Input`, which owns its own focus register. If the live colour must appear on this control it appears as a swatch, never as the focus boundary.

defects.defect: `.btn-interactive` does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0; the send button therefore has no hover, press, focus or disabled treatment at all — while the source comments and DESIGN.md record that contract as `landed`.
defects.evidence: `grep -ro 'btn-interactive' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | wc -l` → 0 (installed version confirmed 7.0.0). Not defined in demo/**/*.css either — it appears only inside template class strings and prose. Live computed on the rendered button: `transitionProperty: "all", transitionDuration: "0s", scale: "none"`. Claimed contract: ColorInput.vue:61-66 and :327-334 (~15 lines asserting the atom supplies scale on --transition-liquid-spatial @ --spring-smooth-duration, press/hover magnitudes, focus ring, disabled opacity); demo/DESIGN.md:247 records the row as `landed`. Entire disabled treatment: ColorInput.vue:344-346 `.send-btn:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; }`.
defects.mechanism: A remediation (T.W5-R5) deleted a working bespoke recipe and replaced it with a producer atom name that resolves to no CSS rule in the pinned producer version; nobody measured the result, and the design record now asserts a contract that is not in effect.
defects.reproduction: Open propose mode with an empty field (ColorInput.vue:70 sets `:disabled="!proposedName.trim() || proposing"`). The arrow button renders pixel-identical to its enabled self and does nothing on click. Hover and press it in colour mode: no visual change whatsoever (measured transition-duration 0s, scale none).
defects.proposedCure: Consume atoms that measurably exist — `tap-squish focus-ring` (the Login/@mbabb dock buttons carry them live). Better: delete the hand-rolled button and take the trailing action slot of the glass-ui field. Then correct demo/DESIGN.md:247, which is currently a false record of shipped state.

defects.defect: The send button is the one nameless button on the route, is 24x24 CSS px, and defaults to type="submit".
defects.evidence: Live enumeration of all 26 buttons on /#/: every dock control has an aria-label except one — `{ txt: "", aria: null, cls: "send-btn btn-interactive", r: {w:24,h:24} }`, `type: "submit"`, `accessibleTextLen: 0`. This is exactly the `namelessButtons: 1` recorded at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:96 and :103 for safari-desktop-{light,dark} /#/. Both button branches (ColorInput.vue:67-75, :76-82) contain only an icon; the Loader2/ArrowRight swap at :73-74 means the in-flight state also has no name and no aria-busy. 24px contributes to REPORT.md's smallTapTargets: 8 on this route.
defects.mechanism: An icon-only action control with no accessible name, no operable-target/glyph separation, and the wrong default button type.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/ at >=1440px and run `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => !b.getAttribute('aria-label') && !b.innerText.trim())` — the sole result is `.send-btn`. Cross-check REPORT.md namelessButtons row for safari-desktop-light /#/: 1.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label per branch ("Apply color" / "Submit name"), type="button", aria-busy on the in-flight branch, and an invisible >=44px hit seat over the 24px glyph — which is PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-12's exact prescription ("Invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung").

defects.defect: The parse-error affordance carries zero programmatic semantics and physically occludes 83% of the send button and 66% of the field it describes.
defects.evidence: Measured with the badge live on screen (frames/B-error-badge-over-send.png): badge left 682.1 right 783.1 width 101.0; send left 763.1 right 787.1 width 24.0 → overlap 20.0px = 83% of the button; input width 153.0 → badge covers 66% of the field. Both absolutely positioned against the same edge with no z-order: ColorInput.vue:337 `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` vs :350 `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }`; the badge is later in DOM order so it always wins. Semantics measured while the error was displayed: aria-invalid null, aria-describedby null, aria-errormessage null, aria-multiline null; badge role null, aria-live null, pointer-events none.
defects.mechanism: An error rendered as a floating decoration positioned against the same physical edge as the recovery action, instead of as a field state with an associated message region.
defects.reproduction: Open the colour input at >=1440px, focus it, and drive a stream of distinct invalid strings at ~2.6s intervals (e.g. `lab(#)`, `lab(##)`, …) so the 2s auto-clear never fires. The red pill sits over both the send arrow and the user's typed text. Read the ARIA attributes on the field: all null.
defects.proposedCure: The error is a field state, not an ornament: use glass-ui `Input`'s existing `invalid` prop plus a real message node in normal flow wired by `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-errormessage`. It never overlaps the value or the action.

defects.defect: ~2.04s trailing debounce before any feedback, no live preview while typing at human cadence, and complete silence when the same invalid string is retried.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; :62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;`; :57 error auto-clears after 2000ms. Four measured live trials — T1 fresh `lab()` → badge at 2037ms; T2 SAME `lab()` retried → badge NEVER; T3 different `zzz(` → 2048ms; T4 `lab()` again after previousInvalid changed → 2041ms. Separately: driving the field at a 900ms cadence for 4s produced no badge at all, because every keystroke resets the 2000ms trailing timer.
defects.mechanism: A trailing debounce an order of magnitude past the interaction-feedback threshold, combined with a stale-input dedup cache guarding a pure function, and an error truth that lives only on a 2s timer.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input open and focused: type `lab()` and wait — the badge appears at ~2.04s and vanishes 2s later. Now clear and type `lab()` again — nothing ever appears. Separately, type `oklch(0.7 0.1 200)` at roughly one character per second: zero live colour preview for the entire 18-character entry.
defects.proposedCure: Leading-edge debounce at ~120-200ms for the live preview; derive the error state from the current value so it PERSISTS while the value is invalid rather than flashing on a timer; delete `previousInvalid` entirely — it is a cache guarding a pure function and it is the mechanism that silences the natural human retry loop. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 already rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.

defects.defect: MT-F001's shipping TypeError is swallowed by the component's parse try/catch and laundered into the user-blaming copy "not a valid color"; the crash is invisible to console, window.onerror and the audit's own telemetry.
defects.evidence: Reproduced live in the running app via the dev-server module graph — `await import('/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/src/css/index.ts')` then `parseCssColor(s)`: `oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl(  )`, `lab()`, `lch()`, `color()`, `oklab()` all → `THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; `oklch(`, `)`, `not-a-color` → clean failure; `oklch(0.7 0.1 200)` → ok. Throw site src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space")` — the `!` is false because splitTopLevel("", "/") yields an empty array. Swallow site demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:63-89 (`try { parseColor(input) } catch { previousInvalid = input; if (!initialParse) flashParseError(); }`). Measured in the live UI while typing `oklch()`: window.onerror fired 0 times, console clean, user shown the generic "not a valid color" pill. REPORT.md records pageErrors: 0 across all 60 captures for exactly this reason. Also useColorParsing.ts:50/:86 — `initialParse` means the FIRST parse of a session flashes nothing at all.
defects.mechanism: An internal fault (TypeError) is caught by the same handler as a user-authored syntax error and rendered with user-blaming copy, destroying both the user's diagnosis and the product's telemetry.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → open the colour input → type `oklch()` → the field shows "not a valid color" after ~2s with no console output. Direct: in the page console, `(await import('/@fs/<repo>/src/css/index.ts')).parseCssColor('oklch()')` throws TypeError.
defects.proposedCure: The root fix belongs to MT-F001 / V-pi (grammar.ts:181 must return a clean failure, not deref a false non-null assertion). The seat-level cure here: catch the internal fault SEPARATELY from a parse failure, report it once (so telemetry sees it), and show a distinct message — "couldn't parse that; this is our bug" — never render an internal fault as copy that blames the user's input.

defects.evidence:
ColorInput.vue:11-27 builds ``. Meanwhile node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/input/ exists and demo/ui/input/index.ts reads `export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";`. InputProps offers autocomplete, defaultValue, disabled, enterkeyhint, form, inputmode, invalid, maxlength, minlength, modelValue, name, pattern, placeholder, readonly, required, size, type. Measured consequences: (a) placeholder — `el.innerHTML='
'` → `el.matches(':empty')` === false, `el.innerHTML=''` → true, so `.color-input:empty[data-placeholder]::before` (:321-325) never fires after the user types once and clears; (b) markup — `el.innerHTML='rebeccapurple!'` survives verbatim, `querySelectorAll('*').length === 2`; (c) `aria-multiline` measured null on a role="textbox"; (d) no inputmode/enterkeyhint/maxlength/pattern; (e) native undo/redo defeated by programmatic innerText writes at :191, :240, :265, :278.
defects.mechanism: Reaching past the design system to re-implement a native primitive, then re-implementing its affordances badly in CSS and imperative DOM writes. Owner edict 4.
defects.reproduction:
Enter propose mode (Tools → Open color input → Propose color name), type a name, select-all, delete. The field is blank with NO placeholder — browsers leave a
so `:empty` is false. Verified programmatically: `document.querySelector('.color-input').innerHTML='
'; el.matches(':empty')` → false. For markup: paste any styled text into the field and inspect innerHTML.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the span with glass-ui `Input` (`type="text" inputmode="text" enterkeyhint="done" spellcheck="false" :invalid="parseError" :placeholder="…"`) over a local shallowRef (the defineModel async round-trip caveat this codebase already documents). This single substitution retires D-1's outline suppression, D-4's badge, D-7 wholly, most of D-8 and most of D-13.

defects.defect: `mask-image` fades the field's own border and background to transparent over the right 40px, fights the centred text, mismatches the padding by 4px, and snaps off on focus.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:294-306 sets `--input-action-width: 2.5rem` and `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black calc(100% - var(--input-action-width)), transparent 100%)`, with `:303-306` `.color-input:focus { mask-image: none }`. Measured computed: `maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0,0,0) calc(100% - 40px), rgba(0,0,0,0) 100%)`, `paddingRight: 36px`, `textAlign: center`, `borderRadius: 4px`, and `maskImage: "none"` while focused. The element also carries `text-overflow: ellipsis` (:16), so two truncation idioms are stacked.
defects.mechanism: An element-level mask used as a text-fade: it masks the box, so the border and background are destroyed with the ink; the fade is physical-right under a symmetric centre alignment; and the two gutter numbers (40px mask, 36px padding) are unrelated to each other and to the 24px button they claim to clear.
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input visible at rest, read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.color-input')).maskImage` and `.paddingRight` → the 40px/36px pair. Click into the field: maskImage becomes "none" and the right border and corners pop back into existence in one frame.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the mask. A real <input> scrolls its own overflow; `text-overflow: ellipsis` at rest already covers the resting truncation. Align the value to the inline start (see D-13) and let one number — the action button's own measured inline size — drive the gutter.

defects.defect: The Crown indicator: its hover magnification never animates (transition names `transform` while Tailwind v4 writes the `scale` longhand), the hover is desktop-only, and its tooltip hangs off a non-focusable <svg> so keyboard and touch users can never read it.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:35 declares `hover:scale-110 transition-[opacity,transform]`; measured computed `transitionProperty: "opacity, transform"`, `duration 0.2s`, `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`. The compiled utility, pulled from the served stylesheet, is `.hover\:scale-110 { &:hover { @media (hover: hover) { --tw-scale-x: 110%; --tw-scale-y: 110%; --tw-scale-z: 110%; scale: var(--tw-scale-x) var(--tw-scale-y); } } }` — the `scale` longhand, which is not `transform`. So opacity fades over 200ms while the magnification snaps instantly. `@media (hover: hover)` removes the affordance entirely on touch. `TooltipTrigger as-child` at :32 passes to `<Crown>`, which renders an <svg> with no tabindex — not focusable — while the tooltip content (:42-57) carries the colour's approved name, contributor and CSS. Also :37-39 applies `style="animation: crown-appear …"` as an inline per-instance override (owner edict 5).
defects.mechanism: The same F3 'spatial-on-bezier stray' this file's own comment (:327-334) says was retired from `.send-btn`, surviving two elements away — plus meaning gated behind a pointer-only, keyboard-unreachable disclosure.
defects.reproduction: Static and decisive: fetch the served stylesheet in-page and grep for `hover\:scale-110` — it emits `scale:`, not `transform:`. Then read `getComputedStyle(<crown>).transitionProperty` → "opacity, transform". The two do not intersect, so the scale change is untransitioned. For the tooltip: Tab through the dock — focus never lands on the crown; on touch, no hover event exists to open it.
defects.proposedCure: Move the crown's meaning into text the field already owns (or a persistent adjacent label). If the mark stays, it becomes a real focusable named control with a house-token transition on the `scale` longhand — or it becomes aria-hidden decoration and loses `cursor: help` and the tooltip. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 5 and PR-07 both rule it: named, or removed.

defects.defect: The component is absent from the DOM entirely at mobile widths, and behind a two-step disclosure on desktop — so the product's only free-text CSS-colour entry appears in none of the 60 audit captures.

Visually: safari-desktop-{light,dark}/picker.png show the dock as `Home ⌄ │ Tools → │ Login │ @mbabb`; safari-mobile-dark/picker.png shows `⌂ ⌄ │ Picker · About │ ⋮`. At rest on desktop the component sits behind `visibility: hidden` inside an `[inert] aria-hidden="true"` .dock-face (measured ancestor chain), reachable only after expanding the face and cycling `actions → input` (ActionBarLayer.vue:33-45).
defects.mechanism: A primary affordance placed in a collapsed, double-gated dock face on desktop and dropped entirely on mobile — an amputation rather than a responsive adaptation.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ — at 1440x900 `!!document.querySelector('.color-input')` → true; resize to 390x844 → false. Then open any of the four .../visual/shots/*/picker.png and observe the dock contains no colour field.
defects.proposedCure: Reopen the composition question (W18/W19): a control that is invisible at rest on every route, needs two disclosures on desktop, and does not exist on mobile is not a dock control — it is a hidden feature wearing dock chrome. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 requires the dock to be 'fully visible … clipped by neither mask nor card'; this control is neither visible nor unclipped.

defects.defect: Type roles fall outside the constitution's closed matrix at two sites.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 declares the matrix 'closed across all eighteen compositions' with only P019's Picker pair exempt.
defects.mechanism: Ad-hoc sizing instead of role tokens: the field's value is Fira Code at mono-caption's SIZE — a fourth combination belonging to no role — and the badge is text-xs, which appears nowhere in the matrix.
defects.reproduction: In-page, create probe spans with classes `text-mono-small`, `text-small`, `mono-caption`, `text-xs` and read getComputedStyle fontSize/fontFamily; compare against `.color-input` (18.608px Fira Code) and `.error-badge` (12px). Neither matches a matrix row.

Both come free with glass-ui `Input` + a producer field-message slot.

defects.defect: Propose-name success and failure are both invisible: failure goes only to console.warn, success silently repaints the field.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:242-244 `} catch (e: any) { console.warn("[ColorInput] Failed to propose name:", e?.message); }`. Success path :238-241 clears `proposedName` and repaints innerText with no user-visible confirmation. The only operation state is `proposing` (:227), which has no visual treatment because `.btn-interactive` does not exist (D-2). Also `catch (e: any)` in a strict:true codebase.
defects.mechanism: Durable operation truth left in the console. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace'; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-08 rules this family ADD-AFFORDANCE.
defects.reproduction: Enter propose mode, submit a name while the API is unreachable (or submit a duplicate): the spinner stops and the UI is otherwise unchanged. The only trace is a console.warn.
defects.proposedCure: Route both outcomes into the same persistent field-status region introduced for D-4 (aria-errormessage on failure, a polite status on success), and type the catch.

defects.defect: Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue physical offsets: `pr-9` (:18), `right-2` (:35), `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` (:337), `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }` (:350), `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, …)` (:300). No `dir` attribute and no `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the value (measured attribute list: data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class). Combined with measured `textAlign: center`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document' and 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance — render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose.'
defects.mechanism: Physical-axis geometry plus an un-isolated LTR technical value inside a container that may be RTL — under RTL a value beginning with `#` or `/` reorders on screen while the model keeps the original bytes, so what the user reads is not what the parser receives.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the visual reordering (no RTL locale is currently reachable in-app). The physical-offset inventory and the absence of any dir/unicode-bidi attribute are directly verified from source and from the live attribute enumeration.
defects.proposedCure: Logical properties throughout (`pe-9`, `inset-inline-end`), and `dir="ltr"` on the value element — which glass-ui `Input` makes trivial. Drop `text-align: center` for inline-start alignment; a technical LTR value centred in a possibly-RTL container is the worst of both.

defects.defect: Real instrument information — the Parse-Lab AST echo and gamut verdict — is gated behind a 300ms hover-only popover wrapped around the text field itself.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:3-8 `<Popover trigger="hover" :close-delay="0" :open-delay="300">` wrapping the whole field as its PopoverTrigger (:9). Content at :94-110 is not decoration: the serialized current colour plus `<ParseEchoReadout />` — the E4/Q10 Parse-Lab AST + gamut verdict. Hover has no touch equivalent and no keyboard equivalent.
defects.mechanism: Disclosure-by-hover for content that is instrument data, not help — and the trigger is the text field, so approaching the field to click into it summons an overlay near the pointer. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 6: 'Subtraction precedes explanation'; PR-14 condemns the same species elsewhere.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ with the colour input open: hover the field for 300ms — the popover appears with the AST/gamut readout. On a touch device no hover event exists; tabbing to the field does not open it either (the trigger is hover-only).
defects.proposedCure: Decide what the Parse-Lab echo is. If it is instrument data it belongs in the instrument, persistently (the Picker already owns a readout region). If it is help it needs a named, focusable disclosure control — not the field itself as a hover target.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) beneath demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context). Explicitly declared at spawn; the declaration matches the served seat. Not a defect.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 (strongest overall, re-derived and confirmed): the library's failure-explicit Result contract is transposed to exceptions at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts and then caught by a bare `catch {}` in useColorParsing — so MT-F001, a real TypeError from shipping library code, is delivered to the user as the same 2s "not a valid color" string a typo produces, with zero console output. L-12 (strongest NEW, this pass): the `crown-appear` animation is dead by construction — a `<style scoped>` @keyframes, hash-renamed to `crown-appear-55dadc03` by the SFC compiler, referenced from an inline `style` attribute the compiler does not rewrite. Measured live: 54 keyframe rules registered in the document, the unhashed name absent from all of them.
result.negativeProof: NOT APPLICABLE to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded because half the challenge premise does not hold and deserves saying: ColorInput consumes @mkbabb/value.js CORRECTLY. A full transitive cone walk from ColorInput.vue (26 internal modules: 14 color-session, 6 platform, 3 demo/ui barrels, 2 shell, 1 shared) yields exactly two value.js specifiers anywhere in the graph — `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `@mkbabb/value.js/css`, both real keys in package.json#exports, both reached only via demo/color-session/{picker-color,generate-color}.ts. Zero `@src` edges (`grep -rn "@src" demo/ --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` is empty), zero deep paths into src/ or dist/. Every value.js import in this component's graph is one a real npm consumer could write verbatim; vite.config.ts:39-49 generates the runtime alias set FROM package.json#exports, so the demo genuinely dogfoods the published surface at runtime. Import DIRECTION is also clean: shell → color-session / platform / shared on all twelve edges, no shell → feature or component → boot reach. Also confirmed sound: verbatimModuleSyntax (the one type-only import, `EditTarget` at :134, is `import type`); Vue 3.5 idioms in the component itself (useTemplateRef :159, reactive props destructure :138); `npx eslint` clean on ColorInput.vue, useColorParsing.ts and picker-color.ts — the defects found are structural, not lintable. The `input-mode-flash` animation and the T.W5-R5 `btn-interactive` retirement are exemplary executions of the animations edict. Two named historical suspects were verified OUT of this component's cone (demo/palettes/export.ts vs export/serializers.ts; the three parallel useDark stores at useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76 / useMarkdownColors.ts:16) — they exist, they are real, they are another seat's.

defects.defect: The crown entrance animation never runs, on any device, in any browser, and never has. ColorInput.vue:36-39 binds `animation: crown-appear ...` in an INLINE style attribute; ColorInput.vue:369-376 defines `@keyframes crown-appear` inside `<style scoped>`. Vue's SFC compiler hash-suffixes scoped keyframe names and rewrites animation declarations within the same style block, but does NOT process template style attributes. The inline reference resolves to nothing. NEW this pass — it also refutes the first pass's negative proof line 654, 'The animation law is honoured.'
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:38 (inline `animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;`) vs :369 (`@keyframes crown-appear`). Compiled sheet served by the dev server: `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` → contains `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03 {...}` and, for contrast, the class-driven sibling correctly rewritten: `.color-input-mode-flash[data-v-55dadc03] { animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 ... }`. Live document keyframe census (all stylesheets, all CSSKeyframesRule names): {"exactCrownAppear": false, "crownLike": ["crown-appear-55dadc03"], "totalKeyframes": 54}. No global fallback: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly 3 hits — ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose). demo/styles/animations.css does not contain it.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home for a keyframe, forced by a per-instance inline style. A scoped @keyframes is consumable only from a class rule in the same block; an inline style attribute is consumable only against a GLOBAL keyframe. Pairing the two is unsatisfiable by construction — no combination of the two halves can ever resolve. Violates edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).
defects.reproduction: 1) `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` — observe the definition is emitted as `crown-appear-55dadc03`. 2) In any live page at http://localhost:9000, evaluate: `[...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return []}}).filter(r=>r.type===CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE).map(r=>r.name).includes('crown-appear')` → false.
defects.proposedCure: crown-appear is a design-language beat, not seat geometry: promote it to demo/styles/animations.css (which already exists and is the declared home for global keyframes) and drive it from a `.crown-badge` CLASS. The inline style attribute dies with it. Adopt the rule repo-wide: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. No third combination is legal.

defects.defect: The library's public parse surface has ZERO negative-space coverage for the degenerate functional-colour body — the exact input class that crashes it. Neither side of the boundary was watching: the demo masks the throw (L-1), and the library never asserted it could not happen.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'oklch()\|"lab()"\|rgb()' test/` → no matches. Only six test files mention parseCssColor at all (test/v4-c1.test.ts, test/v4-css-public.test.ts, test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts, test/ink.test.ts, test/preview-chips.test.ts, test/view-accents.test.ts).
defects.mechanism: Missing negative-space test on a public, failure-explicit API. The contract (src/css/types.ts:25-27) promises a discriminated ParseResult for every input; nothing asserts that promise for the empty-body case, so a throw could be introduced and shipped invisibly.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'oklch()' test/` returns nothing; `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/css.js').then(m=>{try{m.parseCssColor('oklch()')}catch(e){console.log(e.constructor.name)}})"` prints TypeError.
defects.proposedCure: Four lines in test/v4-css-public.test.ts: `it.each(["oklch()","rgb()","hsl()","lab()","lch()","color()","oklab()","hsl(  )"])("%s fails as a Result, never a throw", s => expect(parseCssColor(s).ok).toBe(false));` — closes the class permanently on the public surface.

defects.defect: The failure-explicit Result contract is destroyed at the demo boundary, so a LIBRARY CRASH and a USER TYPO are the same event. src/css/grammar.ts:181 throws TypeError on eight inputs; demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 is a throwing facade that only handles `result.ok === false` and lets the raw TypeError escape past its own typed PickerColorError; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:80-85 catches everything with a bare `catch {}` and renders the hardcoded literal 'not a valid color'. Re-derived and confirmed this pass; first filed by the prior pass.
defects.evidence: Contract: src/css/types.ts:25-27 (`ParseResult<T> = {ok:true,...} | {ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,...]}`), package.json:4 ('failure-explicit'). Throw site: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` where splitTopLevel("","/") returns [] (grammar.ts:79,85). Measured against the exact dist the dev server serves (dist/subpaths/css.js, Jul 24 14:04, newer than src/css/grammar.ts Jul 17 14:48): all of oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' THROW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while 'oklch(' and 'notacolor' correctly return ok:false. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/ after typing oklch()+Enter: {"inputText":"oklch()","errorBadge":null,"borderColor":"lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)"} and browser_console_messages(level=error) → Errors: 0. Diagnostics loss is total: ParseIssue carries {code,start,end,expected,actual} (src/css/types.ts:10-24) and the only three demo readers of `.diagnostics` are internal-invariant sites with no human present (useGradientCSS.ts:128, useImageSampler.ts:60, useMarkdownColors.ts:33); the one surface where a human types CSS reads it never.
defects.mechanism: Contract transposition, three hops, each lossy: Result → exception (picker-color.ts valueOrThrow/PickerColorError) → bare catch {} (useColorParsing) → a constant string literal (ColorInput.vue:88). The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.
defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts` → 5/5 green. The harness drives the REAL useColorParsing composable and the REAL picker-color facade against the PUBLISHED dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js and proves: (1) all eight throw while 'oklch(' returns ok:false — the crash is narrower than the failure path and therefore invisible beside it; (2) parsePickerColor re-throws a raw TypeError, not PickerColorError; (3) with the initialParse gate burned, all eight leave the model object-identical (toBe) and set the same boolean a typo sets; (4) the first parse of a composable's life leaves parseError===false; (5) a repeat of the same crasher early-returns on previousInvalid — no badge, no console, no model change. Live: the gesture chain above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete valueOrThrow and PickerColorError from picker-color.ts and every bare catch on the parse path. parseCssColor already returns the right shape — let it reach the component: `parsePickerColor(s): ParseResult<CssColor>`; `useColorParsing.commit(source)` returns it; ColorInput renders `diagnostics[0].expected` and marks [start,end] in the field. No try, no catch, no previousInvalid cache. Because it is also the server root, every non-root module is addressable by two different URL forms (/X.vue resolved against demo/color-picker/, and /@fs/<abs>/demo/X.vue), and any tool that picks the wrong one resolves to a path that has never existed.

defects.proposedCure: Rename demo/color-picker/ → demo/app/ and set Vite `root: "./demo"`. /@fs/ then disappears from the demo graph entirely, the HMR path ambiguity becomes structurally impossible, and ARCHITECTURE.md:9-33's declared physical tree becomes true as written. defects.defect: Split ownership of the colour-name registry: the READ half is owned by a composable, the WRITE half (an HTTP POST plus session acquisition) is inlined into this dock leaf SFC, which is the only SFC anywhere under demo/shell/ that imports an API call. The write never invalidates the read cache, and it breaks the error-voice policy the read half established.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:132 imports proposeColorName (POST /colors/propose, demo/color-session/color-names.ts:36-44 over platform/transport/client); ColorInput.vue:230-247 runs session.ensureSession(), the mutation, the optimistic clear and `catch (e: any) { console.warn(...) }` inline. Enumeration: `for f in $(find demo/shell -name '*.vue'); do grep -l "color-names\|/api/\|transport/client" $f; done` → demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue ONLY. The reciprocal read is composable-owned: demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:19 calls getApprovedColorNames() from the same module and owns customNameRegistry/normalizedCustomNames plus findCustomName/getMetadata/reset. That composable's lines 39-52 establish the house rule for this exact API (dev-only console.debug, never warn/error, so the e2e zero-console-error gate holds); ColorInput.vue:243 uses console.warn.
defects.mechanism: Ownership split of one semantic concept across two homes with opposite architectural altitudes — a composable for read, a leaf SFC for write. Unique semantic ownership violated; the write path has no access to the read path's cache, so the crown indicator reads stale data after a proposal.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static enumeration. The stale-cache consequence is a hypothesis (proposals require moderator approval before entering the approved list, so it may be unobservable in practice); the ownership split and the console.warn policy break are facts at the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: proposeColorName moves behind useCustomColorNames as `propose(name, css)` — the composable already owns registry state and the error-voice policy and can invalidate its own cache. ColorInput calls propose() and renders `proposing`/`error`. The SFC then imports zero transport modules, which is what `shell → color-session / platform / shared` (ARCHITECTURE.md:47) actually means. Drop the `any`.

defects.defect: The crown entrance animation is dead by construction: a @keyframes declared inside <style scoped> (hence name-hashed by the SFC compiler) is referenced from an inline style attribute in the template, which the compiler does not rewrite. The animation has never run.

A keyframe consumed from outside the scoped block is by definition a global keyframe; placing it inside <style scoped> hashes its name out from under its only consumer. Owner edict 6 (animations are never deleted, only moved or tokenized) is violated in effect — the four-stop gold shimmer was deleted by a scoping accident, and demo/DESIGN.md now records a false fact.
defects.reproduction: Compile-time: `node -e "import {parse,compileStyle} from '@vue/compiler-sfc'" ...` on demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue with id 'data-v-55dadc03', scoped true — grep the output for @keyframes and animation: references. Runtime: open http://localhost:9000/#/, click Toggle action bar then Open color input, then evaluate — enumerate CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE names across document.styleSheets (crown-appear absent, crown-appear-55dadc03 present) and create a div with style.animation='crown-appear 550ms ease forwards' → getAnimations().length === 0. defects.proposedCure: Move @keyframes crown-appear to demo/styles/ (the global keyframe home per edict 6 and ARCHITECTURE.md:34) and replace the inline style attribute with a class. The keyframe's real scope is global because its consumer is outside the scoped block; making the home match the scope is the whole fix.

defects.defect: God-object injection: COLOR_MODEL_KEY provides the entire 35-member useColorPipeline return; ColorInput destructures 10 and uses 8. Every consumer of the key is type-coupled to the whole spine.

Installer: keyframes.js deps {"@mkbabb/value.js":"4.0.0"} (hard, exact pin); glass-ui declares it peer-only. Falsified comments: vite.config.ts:26-28 "A package does not install itself…" and tsconfig.demo.json header "a package never installs itself…". Byte comparison: dist/subpaths/css.js checkout=6dfbff9f vs node_modules=0cd5611e DIFFERENT; color.js SAME; css.d.ts checkout=72eb3fbe (12,490 B) vs node_modules=66cb49c5 (10,910 B) DIFFERENT — the checkout's dts-rollup emits a duplicated suffixed type set (Alpha_2, Channel_2, ChannelsBySpace_2, Color_2, SpaceId_2) so CssColor is keyed on Color_2<S>. The installed copy throws identically: `node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCssColor} from './node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.js'; parseCssColor('oklch()')"` → THROWS Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace').

defects.proposedCure: Add a package.json#overrides entry pinning @mkbabb/value.js to file:. so the invariant the comments assert becomes actually true; then the four tools (vite, vue-tsc, vitest, node) no longer need to be individually taught to dodge a twin that no longer exists. Separately, fix the dts-rollup de-duplication so the published css.d.ts stops shipping 1,580 bytes of duplicated suffixed declarations. And note that the MT-F001 crash is already distributed to every consumer of keyframes.js@6 — which is the strongest argument for repairing src/css/grammar.ts:181 at the library rather than guarding at the demo.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (third independent pass on demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier declared explicitly at spawn (not inherited, not undeclared).
result.strongestDefect: C-23 — the dock's slug-login error path is dead in three independent places, so a failed login shows the user nothing at all: (a) `SlugEditLayer.vue` writes `slugError` eight times and renders it zero times; (b) `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` at SlugEditLayer.vue:54 is not awaited, so the `catch` at :57-62 is unreachable and `slugSwitching` flips true→false in one tick, making the `<Loader2 v-if="slugSwitching">` spinner at :97 unreachable UI; (c) the real handler reports through `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)` (useSlugMigration.ts:84-87) where `slugBarRef` is never bound to any template ref and `PaletteSlugBar` — the only component with a `setError` and the only one that renders an error — is rendered by nothing in the entire app. A 404/409/429/network failure produces no message, no spinner, no console output. (The component's overall worst defect remains pass-1 C-3, which this pass independently re-confirmed and widened from 1 route to 7 of 15.)
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded so a fourth seat does not re-spend the probes: (1) The boot-time route hijack away from `#/blob` (observed 3/3, looked like C-3 forcing a switchView) is NOT a defect — a history.pushState/replaceState wrapper installed at waitUntil:"commit" pinned it to vue-router's `popStateHandler`, i.e. a back-navigation into my own accumulated MCP session history; in fresh browser contexts `#/blob` is stable 6/6 over 4-9s. Method warning: any dock/router probe reusing one MCP page across navigations manufactures this false positive. (2) Inactive dock layers are NOT focus traps — measured ancestor walk shows glass-ui seals them with inert + aria-hidden="true" + visibility:hidden + pointer-events:none; the visual audit counts them only because capture.mjs:83-85 defines visibility as width>0 && height>0. (3) PRM is honoured for the settle beat — animations.css:184-192 forces animation-duration 0.01ms, which neutralises vj-settle and still fires animationend, so Dock.vue:130 still clears the class. (4) `release()` cannot drive the producer hold count negative — glass-ui@7.0.0 dist/dock.js clamps with `g.value = Math.max(0, g.value - 1)`. (5) The usePopupMutex swap did NOT drop both popups at my sampling granularity (~700ms): view-select open, then @mbabb click yields {listboxes:0, menus:1} immediately and still {menus:1} after 600ms — recorded as "not observed at coarse granularity", explicitly NOT as a negative proof, since a ~150ms double-open would sit inside my sampling interval.

defects.defect: The dock's slug-login error path is dead in three independent places: an unrendered `slugError` ref, an un-awaited async dispatch that makes the local catch AND the loading spinner unreachable, and a `setError` sink routed at a template ref that is never bound to a component that is never rendered. A failed login from the dock produces zero user feedback of any kind.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:13,18,43,49,59,60,61,62 (eight writes to `slugError`) vs zero reads — `grep -rn "slugError" demo/` shows the template at :75-119 contains no binding, while the sibling it was cloned from renders it at demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:124. SlugEditLayer.vue:54 `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` has no `await` while useSlugMigration.ts:51 declares it `async`, so the catch at :57-62 cannot fire and `slugSwitching.value = true` (:41) plus `finally { slugSwitching.value = false }` (:63-65) execute in one tick, making `<Loader2 v-if="slugSwitching">` (:97) unreachable. useSlugMigration.ts:84-87 reports via `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; `grep -rn "slugBarRef" demo/` returns only the declaration (:30), the four uses, and the return (:121) — no `ref="slugBarRef"` binding exists; `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar" demo/ --include="*.vue"` returns NO matches, so the only component with a `setError` is rendered by nothing. The comment at useSlugMigration.ts:78-82 records this path was repaired once at S.W2 W2-6 — the repair fixed the predicate and left the sink unattached.
defects.mechanism: authored error copy that no surface reads — the error sink is dispatched into a ref the producing component does not own, and the async result is discarded at the call site
defects.reproduction: Desktop http://localhost:9000/#/ -> @mbabb -> Switch account -> type `zzzz-zzzz-zzzz-zzzz` (well-formed, non-existent slug) -> Enter. The layer closes; no spinner, no error text, no console output, no state change. Identical for a bad admin token, a 429, and a dropped network.
defects.proposedCure: The dock owns the input, so the dock must own the outcome: make `onSlugSwitch` RETURN its result (a Promise<void> that rejects, or a Result<…, ApiProblem>) instead of dispatching into a foreign ref; `await` it at SlugEditLayer.vue:54; render the message inside the layer with role="status"/aria-live="polite" so it is announced as well as seen. `slugBarRef`, `setError`, and PaletteSlugBar's unreachable 40-line twin then delete themselves.

defects.defect: Independent re-confirmation and widening of pass-1 C-3: the dock's primary navigation control renders with NO label on 7 of the 15 audited routes for any unauthenticated visitor (pass 1 measured one route). The deeper invariant broken is that `viewEntries` is not a superset of the reachable view set, so the reka `<Select>`'s controlled model-value can leave its own option set.
defects.evidence: Cold load into a FRESH browser context per row, 1440x900, unauthenticated, 1.8s settle, reading `document.querySelector('nav.dock-band [aria-label="Select view"]').textContent`: `#/` -> "Home" (gold 0); `#/gradient` -> "Gradient" (gold 0); `#/browse` -> "Browse" (gold 0); `#/blob` -> "" (gold 1); `#/atmosphere` -> "" (gold 1); `#/admin/users` -> "" (gold 1); `#/admin/tags` -> "" (gold 1). Isolated-context control (#/browse, #/blob, #/browse, one fresh context each): ["Browse",0] / ["",1] / ["Browse",0] — deterministic, not state leak. Element screenshots read with vision: on #/blob the control is an orphan droplet glyph + chevron with no name; on #/gradient the same control reads "Gradient". Opening the select on #/blob offers ["Home","Palettes","Browse","Extract","Mix","Generate","Gradient"] — the current view is absent, so nothing carries aria-selected. Mechanism: useDockAdminMode.ts:34-39 returns adminViews only when `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated`; userViews (:26) omits atmosphere, blob and all five admin-*; DockViewSelect.vue:52 feeds that set `:model-value="currentView"`, so `<SelectValue/>` (:87) resolves nothing.
defects.mechanism: a controlled select whose model-value can leave its own option set — the option list is a hand-maintained partition (useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27) rather than a derivation of the route table
defects.reproduction: Open a private window at http://localhost:9000/#/blob (or #/atmosphere, or any #/admin/* route). The dock's view control shows an icon and a chevron and no name; clicking it lists seven views, none of which is the current one.

defects.defect: The dock's keep-open watch is not `{ immediate: true }`, so a `Dock` that mounts with `editTarget` already non-null never takes the hold (the dock can auto-collapse mid-edit) and later fires an unpaired `release()`.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:86-89 — `watch(shouldKeepOpen, (open) => { if (open) dockRef.value?.keepOpen(); else dockRef.value?.release(); })` and `watch(anyEditActive, (active) => { if (active) dockRef.value?.expand?.(); })`, neither immediate. `anyEditActive` is `!!editTarget`, a prop (Dock.vue:31, :73); `:collapse-delay="5000"` at :132. The unpaired release is survivable only because the producer clamps: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dock.js release body reads `g.value = Math.max(0, g.value - 1)`. The comment at Dock.vue:78-85 asserts the one-predicate collapse is 'behaviour-equivalent (held <=> any flag true)' — true only over edges observed AFTER mount, which the code does not say.
defects.mechanism: a ref-counted external hold driven by a non-immediate watch, so the mount-time value of the predicate is never applied to the counter
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis on the mount-time branch — it requires `editTarget` non-null at Dock mount, which the current App shell does not produce). The code-level asymmetry and the clamp dependency are proven by file:line and the pasted producer source.
defects.proposedCure: `{ immediate: true }` on both watches. Structurally, combine with pass-1 C-4's derivation (`activeLayer !== "main" || isAnyOpen`) so the predicate's domain and its edges are both correct by construction, and drop the masking `?.` from `expand?.()` (the producer unconditionally exposes `expand`).

defects.defect: Seven uncancelled rAF/timer handles across the dock subtree, sitting one directory away from the same programme's correct idiom.
defects.evidence: grep over demo/shell/dock/ and demo/shell/: Dock.vue:105 (rAF, fires on EVERY view change), ActionBarToggle.vue:60-61 (double rAF), ColorInput.vue:262 (rAF), ColorInput.vue:256 (setTimeout 300ms), ActionButton.vue:95 (setTimeout 400ms), layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:76 (setTimeout cleared on re-entry at :75 but NOT on unmount) — none store a cancellable handle at unmount. Against: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:95 stores `raf` and cancels at :89 and :108 (`onBeforeUnmount(() => cancelAnimationFrame(raf))`), and demo/shell/dock/composables/usePopupMutex.ts:82 does the timer equivalent (`onUnmounted(clearSwapTimer)`). The idiom is known in this area and simply not applied in the SFCs.
defects.mechanism: the constellation's PRM-RAF pattern — one-shot async work scheduled without an owned handle or a scope-dispose
defects.reproduction: NONE for user-visible harm (a post-unmount ref write is inert in Vue); the sites and the asymmetry are proven by the pasted grep output.
defects.proposedCure: One focused `useOneShotClass(trigger, className)` composable in demo/shell/dock/composables/ owning requestAnimationFrame / cancelAnimationFrame / onScopeDispose once — Dock.vue, ActionBarToggle.vue and ColorInput.vue are the same beat three times. Five leak sites collapse to one audited one, without adding to a god module.

defects.defect: `ActionBarToggle`'s `slotLive` early return makes the watch's re-arm dead code: on a later false->true edge `settled` is never restored by the watch, and the invariant the O-15b oracle asserts is held only by an unacknowledged `transitionend` side channel.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionBarToggle.vue:52-68 — `if (slotLive.value) return;` short-circuits after the first `visible === true`, while `settled.value = false` is set on every false edge at :56; the only restorer is `@transitionend.self="onSlotSettled"` (:69-72, bound at :78) setting `settled.value = visible`. That class is exactly what e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:74-79 asserts (`is-settled`, then `.action-bar-toggle-inner` computes `overflow: visible`). MEASURED, fresh context 1440x900, in-app hash nav: boot `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible; #/browse `is-live`/overflow hidden; #/ `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible; #/admin/users `is-live`/overflow hidden; #/ `is-visible is-live is-settled`/overflow visible — it recovers today.
defects.mechanism: a state machine whose stated owner (the watch) is not its actual owner (a DOM transition event), so the invariant holds by luck
defects.reproduction: Measured and NEGATIVE at HEAD (the transitionend path restores `is-settled` on every re-entry). Filed as a latent structural defect: any change making the `grid-template-columns` transition a no-op (equal endpoints, `transition: none`, a content-visibility skip) silently pins the clip on and O-15b begins failing far from ActionBarToggle.vue:57.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the `slotLive` early return so the watch owns `settled` on both edges, and keep `onSlotSettled` as confirmation rather than as the sole restorer.

defects.defect: A failed login is completely silent: the slug-edit layer closes as if it succeeded, and there are three independent, redundant reasons no error can reach the user. (1) `SlugEditLayer.vue:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` with no `await` inside a `try`, while `useSlugMigration.ts:51` declares it `async` — the `catch` at :57 is unreachable, and :55-56 close the layer synchronously before the network call resolves. (2) It would not matter: the callee catches everything itself (`useSlugMigration.ts:74-88`) and dispatches onto `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`, a permanently-null ref. (3) `slugError` is written at six sites in SlugEditLayer and rendered at zero — the template contains no reference to it. And the substring branches at :59-62 are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6 (`ApiProblem` does `super(title)`, so `e.message` is the server title and can never contain '409'/'404'/'429').
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:54 (un-awaited) · :57 (catch) · :59-62 (substring sniff) · :13,18,43,49,59-62 (slugError writes) · `sed -n '74,119p' SlugEditLayer.vue | grep slugError` → no output (never rendered). demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51 (`async function onSlugSwitch`) · :77-82 (the S.W2 W2-6 ruling comment) · :84-87 (correct typed path, dispatched into null). demo/platform/transport/api-problem.ts:22-33 (`super(title)`). LIVE REPRODUCTION (LDOCK-probe6.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, http://localhost:9000): after filling 'aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd' and clicking button[aria-label="Switch to slug"] — `[after submit] inputValue:"" layerInert:true layerAriaHidden:"true" errorish:[]`, dock still shows 'Login', console tail contains only the two boot lines, no error from the login attempt.
defects.mechanism: error channel swallowed three ways: un-awaited async across a component boundary; callee catches into a null instance ref; error state with no template binding — plus a condemned string-sniff re-authored after its cure was recorded
defects.reproduction: node LDOCK-probe6.mjs (scratchpad) against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — open the dock Login button, fill the slug input, submit; observe layer closes inert+aria-hidden, input cleared, zero error text anywhere in the DOM (`errorish: []`), clean console. The dev server's API is deliberately misconfigured (its own status lamp reads 'dev misconfigured'), so the attempt is guaranteed to fail.
defects.proposedCure: `onSlugSwitch` returns its outcome (`Promise<Result<void, ApiProblem>>`) instead of dispatching it onto a component instance; the layer awaits and renders the failure. One contract change removes all three swallows at once — awaiting makes it observable, returning kills the instance-ref channel, rendering kills the dead state. Rides L-6/L-24's move of the session port to `demo/platform/auth/`, so the login surface becomes a function with a typed result rather than a feature-owned side effect.

Therefore `slugBarRef` (useSlugMigration.ts:30) is permanently null and the four `setError` calls at :84-87 are guaranteed no-ops. The live implementation (`SlugEditLayer.vue`, 119 lines) sits in the SHELL, exposes `{onStartSlugEdit, onCopySlug, slugSwitching}` with no `setError`, so the two do not even share an interface.

result.strongestDefect: L-30 — the silent login failure. It is the only finding in the whole report where a user performs an action, is told nothing, and is wrong about the outcome: the slug-edit layer closes inert+aria-hidden with the input cleared and zero error text anywhere in the DOM (`errorish: []`, reproduced live). Three independent swallows stack — an un-awaited async call across a component boundary makes the dock's catch unreachable; the callee catches into `slugBarRef.value?.setError()` on a permanently-null ref (its component, PaletteSlugBar.vue, is mounted by nothing); and `slugError` has no template binding at all. And the substring branches are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6. It is cheap to fix (four files, no producer change) and it is the purest instance of the challenge's premise: the concept 'sign in' has two homes, the wrong one survived, and the error contract was left wired to the corpse.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the sub-axis ledger of what I checked and found SOUND, with positive evidence. The T.W1 dogfood keystone holds. (Caveat filed as prior-pass L-22 and corroborated by me via `tsc --traceResolution`: `@mkbabb/value.js/css` resolves by package SELF-REFERENCE through the exports map, not through the stale `tsconfig.demo.json` `paths` block — latent config drift, not a live break.) (2) THE DOCK ITSELF IMPORTS THE LIBRARY ZERO TIMES — correct for chrome, though it means the component on screen 100% of sessions proves 0% of the public API. (3) THE THREE-PARALLEL-useDark SUSPECT NAMED IN THE BRIEF IS CURED: all 9 live call sites use glass-ui `useGlobalDark`; the only vueuse `useDark` mention left is the historical comment at useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76-79. (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` HOLDS across the entire dock subtree — every type-only import carries `import type` or an inline `type` modifier (Dock.vue:22-24, ActionBarLayer.vue:2,5,9, ActionButton.vue:49, GenericActionBar.vue:4, status-lamp.ts:31, useDockAdminMode.ts:4-5, usePopupMutex.ts:4, DockViewSelect.vue:9). (6) `main` AND `nav` LANDMARKS ARE CORRECT — main=1, nav=1 on 60/60 captures and live; only the H1 half of W47's `main/H1/active-subtree = 1` gate is red. (7) THE ONE BOUNDARY GUARD THAT STILL MATCHES FILES — inv-K-1 at eslint.config.js:204-218, banning src/ -> glass-ui — protects the one boundary that has never been violated; that correlation is itself the argument for L-23.
