result.strongestDefect: R2-1 — The send button is structurally incapable of submitting what the user typed. `onInputBlur` (ColorInput.vue:191) overwrites the field's `innerText` with the canonical colour; the UA fires `blur` on mousedown and `click` on mouseup; `onSubmitColor` (:215) then reads the already-overwritten DOM. Measured live: model `rgb(255 0 0)` → user types `rebeccapurple` → after blur the field reads `rgb(255 0 0)` → after the send click the model is still `rgb(255 0 0)`, in 292 ms (far inside the 2000 ms debounce). Every press re-submits the colour that was already active, and the still-armed debounce then applies the typed colour ~2 s later, so the control reads as broken and flaky at once. Round 1 reached this mechanism (its C-9) but labelled it "reproduction: NONE" and drew only a display-latency consequence; round 2 supplies the reproduction and escalates it from MAJOR to BLOCKER.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative is claimed for the component as a whole. The following sub-claims WERE proven negative and are recorded so no future seat re-spends the budget: (1) PRM-RAF epidemic — one single-shot optional-chained rAF at :262, no loop; (2) WebGL — none in this component (the `WebGL: context lost.` console error on /#/ in REPORT.json is the HeroBlob); (3) ValueUnit nesting — the component constructs no colour values, only strings; (4) defineModel stale reads — none present; (5) oklch→HSV hue drift — correctly guarded in useColorParsing.ts:39-46,76-83 with an `s*v > 0.01` powerless gate and last-deliberate-hue retention; (6) reka-ui slider pointer-capture — no slider; (7) verbatimModuleSyntax — the sole type-only import `import type { EditTarget }` (:134) is correctly marked; (8) horizontal overflow — `overflowX: 0` on /#/ in all four capture matrices, the mask-image fade + text-ellipsis contain long values and the mask clears on :focus; that part is careful and right. Also WITHDRAWN: my own hypothesis that the visual census cannot see this component. `capture.mjs:83-86` defines visibility purely as `width>0 && height>0`, and I measured the at-rest field at 233.2×45.9 with its 24×24 button laid out despite the layer being `inert` — so round 1's attribution of REPORT.json's nameless button on /#/ to this component is correct, and the button's exact 24×24 correctly escapes the `w<24||h<24` tap-target filter.

defects.defect: The send button can never submit typed text: `onInputBlur` wipes the contenteditable back to the canonical colour, and because the UA moves focus on mousedown but fires click on mouseup, `onSubmitColor` always reads the already-wiped DOM and re-submits the stale colour.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:191 (`inputColorRef.value.innerText = formattedCurrentColor.value`) and :215 (`parseAndSetColor(inputColorRef.value.innerText)`). Live measurement: {"committed":"rgb(255 0 0)","typed":"rebeccapurple","afterBlur":"rgb(255 0 0)","afterSend":"rgb(255 0 0)"} in 292 ms total. Short-circuit that hides it: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:69.
defects.mechanism: DOM-as-source-of-truth: a mutable DOM node is both the draft store and the read-back channel, with two handlers writing and reading it in UA-imposed order.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → dock → 'Toggle action bar' → 'Open color input'. Focus the field, type a new valid colour, click the arrow (send) button within 2 s. Nothing happens; ~2 s later the colour changes anyway.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the contenteditable as the source of truth. Hold the draft in a local `shallowRef<string>` written by @input, render from it, and let blur only decide whether to DISCARD the draft — never rewrite a node a pending click is about to read. `onSubmitColor` then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering is irrelevant. This is edict 7's synchronous-local-cache idiom, and it dissolves round 1's C-16 (six imperative innerText writers over three sources of truth) in the same stroke.

defects.defect: The 2000 ms debounced parse is never cancelled by this component — not on blur, Enter, send, mode switch, or unmount (there is no onUnmounted at all) — so an abandoned edit silently overwrites a later, deliberate colour commit, and can mutate the global model after the component is destroyed.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 (`debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`); demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 (`.cancel()` exists); `grep -rn onUnmounted demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → no matches; the sibling consumer DOES cancel at demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383. Measured with real timers: `C1 committed #abcdef` → `C2 after committing #00ff00 color=rgb(0 255 0)` → `C3 2.3s later, nothing touched color=rgb(255 0 0)`. Unmount path: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:153 `v-if="hasAnyActionBar"` and :156 `v-if="actionBar"`.
defects.mechanism: A hidden timer owns pending state with no lifetime binding; combined with round 1's C-8 (the debounce is an app-wide singleton), the only `.cancel()` in the application belongs to ColorPicker's lifetime — so this component's pending parse is cancelled by the wrong unmount and by nothing else.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node --config vite.config.ts <scratchpad>/parseprobe2.ts — scenario C. In the app: type a colour into the dock input, blur without committing, immediately pick a different colour by slider/swatch; ~2 s later the colour reverts to the abandoned text.
defects.proposedCure: Give the pending commit the component's lifetime and make it visible reactive state rather than a hidden timer: fold the debounce into the draft `shallowRef` of R2-1, cancel on every path that resolves the edit, and add `onBeforeUnmount`. Do not merely add a cancel call — the singleton ownership (C-8) is the same defect seen from the other side.

defects.defect: The field is `contenteditable="true"`, not `plaintext-only`, so a rich paste injects foreign markup and inline styles and physically blows the dock row open; in propose mode it never self-heals because the blur repaint is gated on `!proposeMode`.
defects.evidence: Live: {"contenteditableAttr":"\"\"","insertHTMLAccepted":true,"innerHTML":"red","childElementCount":2,"firstChildFontSize":"32px","inputHeightPx":66}. Resting height measured 45.9 px → 66 px, a 44% blow-out. Gate: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:190.
defects.mechanism: An unconstrained rich-text editing host used as a single-line plain-text field; no sanitisation and no paste handler.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → open the dock colour input → paste a colour value copied from any styled web page (docs table, CSS snippet on a blog). Equivalently, the UA-level operation: select all in the field and run `document.execCommand('insertHTML', false, 'red')`.
defects.proposedCure: `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` — the exact semantic the component wants, supported by Chrome/Safari/Firefox 125+, removing the sanitisation question entirely rather than adding a paste handler.

defects.defect: A successful name proposal desyncs the field from its own model and never signals the parent: `proposedName` is cleared to "" while the visible field is filled with a colour string (programmatic innerText fires no input event), leaving a filled field above a permanently disabled send button; the comment claiming it signals the parent is false — the component declares no emits and the parent's ref is never dereferenced.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:237-240 (`proposedName.value = ""` then `inputColorRef.value.innerText = formattedCurrentColor.value`), the false comment at :238, the disabled binding at :70; no `defineEmits` anywhere in the file; demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:28 declares `colorInputRef` and :116 assigns it, and `grep -rn "copyAndSetInputColor|onSubmitColor|inputIsFocused" demo/ | grep -v ColorInput.vue` returns empty — the whole `defineExpose` (:282-288) has no caller.
defects.mechanism: Two writers for one piece of state (a ref and a DOM node) reconciled by hand, plus a cross-component intent expressed as a comment instead of an emit.
defects.reproduction: NONE end-to-end in this environment — the dev server targets the cross-origin production API and every proposal request is CORS-blocked (console: `[value.js] value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED … every palette request will be blocked`), so the success branch cannot be driven here. The desync itself is deterministic by inspection of :237-240 + :70: setting innerText programmatically cannot fire `input`, therefore `proposedName` cannot be non-empty while the field shows text. The FAILURE branch IS live-reproducible and is silent (only `console.warn` at :243).
defects.proposedCure: `const emit = defineEmits<{ proposed: [] }>()` and let the parent own the mode — it already owns `toolbarMode`. Feed the field's text from the same single reactive source as R2-1 so clearing the model clears the field by construction, and route the failure into the same error surface the parse path uses so this component has ONE error channel instead of one visual and one console-only.

defects.defect: The propose-mode flash timer is a hardcoded 300 ms that contradicts the design token driving the animation it gates (`--duration-slow` = 450 ms), truncating the animation at 66.7%; the handle is discarded so rapid toggles let an earlier timer clear a later flash.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:256 `setTimeout(() => { modeTransition.value = false; }, 300)` gating `.color-input-mode-flash { animation: input-mode-flash var(--duration-slow) … }` (:313). Token value pasted from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css: `--duration-slow: 0.45s`. demo/DESIGN.md:212 names --duration-slow as this animation's token.
defects.mechanism: A JS literal duplicating a CSS design token — a second source of truth that drifted.
defects.reproduction: Static: 300 < 450 by the two pasted values. Behavioural: toggle propose mode twice inside 300 ms; the first timer clears the flag mid-flight of the second flash.
defects.proposedCure: Drive the flash off `animationend`, or read the token via getComputedStyle. Better: express the flash as a CSS transition keyed off a class so no JS timer exists at all.

defects.defect: Three of the file's four component imports route through one-line re-export barrels of the very package the fourth import names directly — migration aliases in violation of the no-legacy edict, with a glass DockSeparator rendered beside a shim-routed Separator in the same dock row.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:117 imports `writeClipboard` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui` directly, while :118-129 import Popover/Tooltip/Separator from `../../ui/*`. `cat demo/ui/popover/index.ts` → `export { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (tooltip and separator identical, one line each). defects.proposedCure: Systemic, not local: delete the 18 barrels and rewrite consumers to import `@mkbabb/glass-ui` directly. Do NOT patch this one file — that would leave 17 aliases and a split idiom. Route as a sweep.

defects.defect: `oklch(0.5 0.1 250 / )` — an empty alpha after the slash — is ACCEPTED as a valid colour by the parser this component feeds, the false-accept mirror of MT-F001's false non-null assertion on the other side of the same split.
defects.evidence: npx vite-node against @mkbabb/value.js/css: `"oklch(0.5 0.1 250 / )" -> OK`. Source: src/css/grammar.ts:180 `const alpha = alphaToken(slash[1]?.trim())` treats "" as absent rather than as a syntax error; :181 is the MT-F001 throw site on `slash[0]`.
defects.mechanism: `splitTopLevel(body, "/")` results are consumed without validating arity: index 0 is asserted non-null (throws) and index 1 is optional-chained into a permissive path (false-accepts).
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node --config vite.config.ts <scratchpad>/probe.ts — last row of the output.
defects.proposedCure: Not this component's defect — route to the library seat. One repair should cover both halves: validate the arity of the `/` split once and return a typed failure for any shape other than exactly one or two non-empty parts, instead of asserting one index and optional-chaining the other.

defects.defect: A bare, unbound `catch {}` over the parse path renders a live library TypeError byte-identical to a user typo — the mechanism by which MT-F001 has survived in the shipping path with zero console output and zero page errors.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:84-86. Live interceptor result: {"afterDebounce":{"badge":true,"badgeText":"not a valid color","pageErrors":[]},"afterEnter":{"badge":true,"pageErrors":[]}}. Library side: `"oklch()" -> THROW TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` at src/css/grammar.ts:181. The discarded typed failure is `PickerColorError` with `diagnostics` at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:112.
defects.mechanism: Masking fallback: an over-broad catch swallows an exception class it was never meant to handle and relabels it as domain-valid user error.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → dock colour input → type `oklch()`. A red 'not a valid color' pill appears for 2 s; window.onerror and unhandledrejection stay empty.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow the catch: `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof PickerColorError)) throw e; … }`. Genuine syntax rejection stays a quiet inline error; anything else reaches window.onerror where MT-F001 would have been caught on day one. Surface the discarded `diagnostics` in the ParseEchoReadout already mounted at ColorInput.vue:109.

defects.defect: `.btn-interactive` is a phantom class: both send buttons declare it and the component's own comment asserts it supplies hover/press/focus/disabled registers, but it is defined nowhere in the repo and in no dependency — so the only submit control has no hover response, no press feedback, no focus ring, and no disabled dimming.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:69 and :78 carry `class="send-btn btn-interactive"`; the comment at :327-334 documents the retirement. Independently re-verified in round 2: `grep -rn "\.btn-interactive" demo/ src/` → empty; `grep -rl "btn-interactive" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → empty (glass-ui 7.0.0). The scoped `.send-btn` block (:335-346) contains only position/right/top/transform/padding/border-radius/cursor plus `:disabled { cursor: not-allowed }`.
defects.mechanism: A working bespoke recipe was deleted in favour of a producer atom the producer had already retired — edict 6 (animations never deleted) violated by the very refactor comment that records it.

Until the producer ships it, the seat must not reference a class it cannot resolve, and the deleted working recipe must be restored rather than left dangling. Blast radius beyond this file: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:75,:78,:100.

defects.defect: The Crown's `crown-appear` animation has never run: it is declared in an inline template `style` attribute, which Vue's scoped-style compiler does not rewrite, while the `@keyframes` it names is renamed by that compiler.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:38 `animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) …` (inline) vs :369 `@keyframes crown-appear` (scoped). Round 2 confirmed by a different instrument than round 1 — a live scan of every same-origin stylesheet returned exactly {"keyframeNames":[{"name":"input-mode-flash-55dadc03"},{"name":"crown-appear-55dadc03"}]}, i.e. no bare `crown-appear` exists. `grep -rn crown-appear demo/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/` finds only the inline reference, the scoped definition, and demo/DESIGN.md:213 documenting it as live. Contrast: `input-mode-flash` is referenced from INSIDE the scoped block (:313) and therefore works.
defects.mechanism: Scoped-keyframe renaming applies only to references within the style block; an inline style attribute escapes the rewrite, leaving an animation-name that matches no @keyframes rule — which per CSS Animations applies no animation (and loses `forwards`).
defects.reproduction: The stylesheet scan above, run in the live page. Static: the two greps.
defects.proposedCure: Move the declaration into the scoped block as a class (`.crown-indicator { animation: … }`) so the compiler rewrites both sides. Adopt the general rule this file violates: never put `animation` in an inline style attribute inside an SFC.

defects.defect: The error channel is provably silent in two ordinary states: the first invalid input after a cold load raises nothing (the `initialParse` grace is spent by the user's own first attempt), and re-entering the SAME invalid string after the 2 s flash times out raises nothing forever (the `previousInvalid` latch).
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:62 (`if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return`), :85-86 (`previousInvalid = input; if (!initialParse) flashParseError()`), :88 (`finally { initialParse = false }`). Measured: `after parseAndSetColor("oklch()") parseError=false` / `after 2nd "oklch()" parseError=false`; and `B1 'nope-1' parseError=true` → `B2 after 2.1s parseError=false` → `B3 retry 'nope-1' parseError=false`.
defects.mechanism: Error presentation modelled as a fire-and-forget 2 s timer plus a memo of the last bad string, instead of being derived from the last parse attempt.
defects.reproduction: npx vite-node --config vite.config.ts <scratchpad>/parseprobe.ts (scenario 1) and <scratchpad>/parseprobe2.ts (scenario B). In the app: type a bad colour, watch the badge time out after 2 s, press Enter again to see what was wrong — absolutely nothing happens.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both suppressors. Derive error state as a computed over the last attempt `{ input, ok }`: idempotent, re-announces correctly on retry, and needs no `initialParse` special case because a boot-time parse simply should not travel the user-attempt path at all.

defects.defect: Accessibility: the only submit control is a nameless 24×24 icon button, and a rejected colour is never announced — no aria-invalid on the field, no role/aria-live on the badge, no aria-describedby linking them; the only help text lives in a hover-triggered popover unreachable by keyboard.
defects.evidence: Live: {"btnAria":{"label":null,"text":"","title":null},"sendBtn":{"w":24,"h":24},"inputAria":{"invalid":null,"describedby":null},"badgeAria":{"role":null,"live":null}}. Source: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:67-82 (both buttons icon-only), :87 (badge), :4-6 (`trigger="hover"` `:open-delay="300"`). WCAG 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value (A) and 3.3.1 Error Identification (A). The house idiom exists and was skipped — ActionBarLayer.vue:131 computes an aria-label for its sibling control.
defects.mechanism: Visual-only state signalling: error is expressed as border colour, box-shadow and a positioned pill, none of which is in the accessibility tree; and the affordance's name is carried only by icon shape.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → dock → 'Toggle action bar' → 'Open color input', then read the measured attribute snapshot above. A screen reader announces 'button' and says nothing when `oklch()` is rejected.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label on both buttons reusing ActionBarLayer.vue:131's label vocabulary; bind `:aria-invalid="parseError"` and `:aria-describedby` to a stable badge id; give the badge `role="status"`; and move the help copy out of a hover-only popover into a persistent describedby target. If the pattern is worth sharing it belongs in glass-ui (edict 4), not in demo/ui.

defects.defect: Vacuous test gate: zero behavioural coverage of this component, plus a docblock asserting unit coverage in a file that does not exist.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "Enter a CSS color" e2e/` → one hit, e2e/smoke/oracles/o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:370, a font-face census that only hovers the field (:367-380). e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts asserts only ActionBarLayer's toggle aria-label. Its docblock at :22-24 claims coverage in `test/parsing/extract.test.ts`; `ls test/parsing/` → `timeline` only, and `grep -rn "submitProposedName|proposeColorName" test/ e2e/` returns only that docblock. defects.reproduction: THE EXACT GREEN-KEEPING MUTATION: delete the entire handler wiring — @keydown, @input, @focus, @blur — and both <button> elements, leaving only the `<span aria-label="Enter a CSS color">` and the Popover. o10d still finds a hoverable span and still reads the popover title; color-propose never touched any of it. A colour input that accepts no input and commits nothing passes the full suite.

And delete the false coverage claim in color-propose.spec.ts:22-24 — a citation to a non-existent file is worse than no comment, because it tells the next reader to stop looking.

defects.defect: Dead API surface: an unused prop, two unused injections, and a five-member defineExpose no caller dereferences — one member of which also discards a producer contract's failure reason.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:139 (`editTarget` prop, passed at ActionBarLayer.vue:118, never referenced), :146 (`cssColorOpaque`), :150 (`canProposeName`), :282-288 (defineExpose). `grep -rn "copyAndSetInputColor|onSubmitColor|inputIsFocused" demo/ | grep -v ColorInput.vue` → empty; ActionBarLayer.vue:28 declares `colorInputRef` and :116 assigns it, but never reads it. defects.defect: The mobile dock action bar is a row of dead buttons: on /#/gradient, /#/generate and /#/mix the Tools trigger opens an action layer whose buttons are named, sized, focusable and clickable, and every handler is a silent no-op on mobile.
defects.evidence:
D-dock-probe6.mjs, clipboard pre-seeded with SENTINEL-NOT-TOUCHED then "Copy CSS" clicked in the dock action bar on /#/gradient:
MOBILE 390x844:   clipboard="SENTINEL-NOT-TOUCHED"                                          pageErrors=[]
DESKTOP 1440x900: clipboard="linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% 0.15 145deg) 0.00%, oklch(7…" pageErrors=[]
Bar renders in full at 390 (D-dock-probe5.mjs): slot opacity:1, trigger tabIndex:0 32x32; Back 44x44, Reset 32x32, Copy CSS 32x32, Seed from palette 32x32.
defects.mechanism: Desktop-only capability wiring masked by optional chaining. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:206-208 (gradient), :193-196 (generate), :217-220 (mix) call `paneRefs.<view>.value?.<cmd>?.()`. demo/color-picker/App.vue:320-327 writes gradientPaneRef/generatePaneRef/mixPaneRef ONLY inside onDesktopLeftMount/onDesktopRightMount — the file's own comment at :314-316 says "Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots". The mobile PaneSlot (App.vue:81-89) passes no :on-mount. Violates owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks) at the highest-cost site.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe6.mjs against the live dev server: newContext 390x844 → goto /#/gradient → seed clipboard → click "Toggle action bar" → click the button named exactly "Copy CSS" → read clipboard. Repeat at 1440x900.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the direction of the dependency: the dock must not hold references to pane instances. The pane provide()s a command object keyed by view; the dock injects it. A view that provides no commands renders no Tools trigger; a provided command is live in whichever slot mounted it, by construction. Delete paneRefs, onDesktopLeftMount, onDesktopRightMount and every `?.` on a handler — an action that can be absent must be ABSENT, never present-and-inert.

defects.defect: The Picker's entire action region does not exist on a phone: Copy color, Reset color, Random color, Palettes, Extract palette and Open color input are in the dock on desktop and absent from the whole document on mobile.

defects.mechanism: demo/color-picker/App.vue:38 — `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`; colorPickerRef is written only at App.vue:322 inside onDesktopLeftMount. The `?? null` masks "the mobile slot never registered" as "this view has no actions". Breaks VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7·Picker ("Copy lives once in the action region") and §3 law 6 (mobile is a stage→inspector→ACTION sequence beneath the same top dock).
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe4.mjs — enumerate every button/[role=button]/a accessible name in the document at 390x844 on /#/ and grep for /copy color|random color|reset color|open color input/i; then repeat at 1440x900.
defects.proposedCure: Same inversion as D2-01. The Picker publishes its command set through provide(); the dock injects. Deletes the `?? null` mask, the desktop-only ref, and the whole desktop/mobile capability fork in App.vue at once.

defects.defect: Two contradictory isDesktop predicates (plus two more Tailwind/media forks) — at 1024x1366 portrait the dock renders the MOBILE pane switcher and the DESKTOP profile block simultaneously, with no ⋮ menu and no Tools.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe3.mjs·A at 1024x1366: dataLayout:"mobile" (App.vue, aspect-aware) / panesDisplay:"block" / profileDisplay:"flex" / mobileMenuDisplay:"none" / toolsLabelPresent:true / selectValuePresent:true. Rendered proof scratchpad/D-tablet-portrait.png shows one pill: [🏠 Home ⌄] [ Picker | About ] | [→] Login | [@mbabb]. Predicates: App.vue:310-312 `(min-width:1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio:1.1)`; Dock.vue:71 `(min-width:1024px)` width-only; ProfileSection.vue:48 / MobileMenuDropdown.vue:38 Tailwind `lg:` width-only; PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46 `@media (max-width:639px)`.
defects.mechanism: demo/styles/shell.css:98-112 documents that the data-layout stamp exists so the two witnesses "can never disagree" and warns that a media wrapper "would re-introduce the width-only disagreement the stamp exists to retire" — Dock.vue:71 re-introduces exactly that predicate. Four authorings of one responsive boundary at three thresholds, so they disagree by construction on portrait tablets. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 7 (no breakpoint pile).
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe3.mjs (matrix A) — newContext 1024x1366 → goto /#/ → read app-layout[data-layout], computed display of .dock-mobile-panes, of the ProfileSection `hidden lg:flex` wrapper and of the MobileMenuDropdown `lg:hidden` wrapper, plus presence of the Tools label and SelectValue.
defects.proposedCure: One predicate, one owner. App.vue already owns the truth; the dock consumes it via a single useLayoutMode() composable (or reads data-layout), and every lg:/sm: utility in the dock subtree is replaced by that one attribute selector at the root. Delete Dock.vue:71 and the 639px media block in PaneSegmentedControl.vue.

defects.defect: CORRECTION TO r1: three operable 22x22 controls and an unlabelled 160x23 input in the slug-edit layer are real WCAG 2.2 failures (SC 2.5.8 target size, SC 3.3.2 labels), not measurement artifacts — r1 ruled MT-F004 'not real' by measuring only the at-rest inert state.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe3.mjs·B2, slug layer ACTIVATED by clicking Login at 1440x900: slug input 160x23 inert:false tabbable:true accessibleName "(NONE — placeholder only)"; "Switch to slug" 22x22 inert:false tabbable:true; "Generate new slug" 22x22 inert:false tabbable:true; "Cancel" 22x22 inert:false tabbable:true. Rendered: scratchpad/D-desk-slugedit.png — the placeholder is clipped mid-word to "enter slug or to".
defects.mechanism: SlugEditLayer.vue:91-118 applies glass-ui's `compact` register (a ~22px sticker seat for secondary glyphs) to primary form controls, and SlugEditLayer.vue:81-87 gives the input a magic w-40 (160px) with a placeholder and no label. Root cause is housing: a login form lives inside the navigation pill, so it must shrink to fit — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7·Account already rules Account is a modal side Dialog opened FROM the dock, not a layer inside it.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe3.mjs (matrix B2) — 1440x900, goto /#/, click the button named "Login", then enumerate nav interactives with rect + `!!el.closest('[inert]')` + tabIndex, and read input.labels/aria-label.
defects.proposedCure: Move the slug/auth flow out of the band into the Account Dialog §7 already specifies. That single move deletes the slug layer, the three 22x22 controls, the unlabelled 160px input and the 162px dock width jump (D2-10) together. If it must stay meanwhile: drop `compact`, add a real label, size from content measure.

defects.defect: MT-F005 root-caused and enumerated: the one nameless desktop button is ColorInput.vue's send-btn, unnamed on BOTH template branches, and its route pattern fits exactly the views whose left pane is color-picker.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe1.mjs nameless[] = [{path: "…div.dock-face > … > button.send-btn.btn-interactive", rect:[24,24], visibility:"hidden", inNav:true, html:"<button class=\"send-btn btn-interactive\"><svg …"}]. Source: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:67-75 (propose branch) and :76-82 (submit branch) — neither carries aria-label. REPORT.md nameless=1 on /, /palettes, /mix, /blob, /does-not-exist and 0 on /browse, /extract, /generate, /atmosphere, /admin/* — exactly the VIEW_MAP entries with left:"color-picker" (viewSchema.ts), /does-not-exist redirecting to picker.
defects.mechanism: Icon-only button with no accessible name, in a face the dock mounts only for color-picker-left routes. The 'zero on mobile' half is not a hidden-layer artifact — on mobile the color-input face is never provided at all (D2-02), so the button is never rendered.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe1.mjs at 1440x900 on /#/ — collect button/[role=button] with rect>0 and no aria-label/aria-labelledby/textContent, print DOM path and outerHTML head. Cross-check REPORT.json namelessButtons per route against VIEW_MAP `left`.
defects.proposedCure: aria-label on both branches ('Apply color' / 'Submit name'), and fold the propose/submit duplication into one button whose label and handler derive from proposeMode — two nearly identical buttons differing by one v-if is the reason one of them got a label review and the other did not. The mobile half closes with D2-02's inversion.

defects.defect: Dark mode annihilates the dock accent — chroma 0.188 → 0.021 (−89%) — destroying both the nine-view hue identity and the only visual distinction between the primary auth action and the vanity wordmark; and on the default route --accent-view IS --accent-live bit-for-bit, so the 'two dock voices' design is degenerate exactly where a first-time user meets it.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe4.mjs computed root values: light --accent-view = oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402) (C 0.188); dark --accent-view = oklch(0.958322 0.0210531 9.83402) (C 0.021, L 0.958). Same probe: --accent-live light = oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg) — identical to --accent-view (viewSchema.ts picker accentHueShift:0). Rendered: scratchpad/D-dock-light.png (Login = crimson bold text in a crimson-bordered pill) vs scratchpad/D-dock-dark.png (Login and @mbabb are two identical dark slabs with white text).
defects.mechanism: useViewAccents resolves each view token through a gamut-map + WCAG-3:1 contrast re-guard; in the dark scheme the guard drives L to 0.958 and collapses C to 0.021, so hue becomes imperceptible. DockViewSelect.vue:40-42 already excised the per-row hue legend for carrying 'near-zero discriminative information' and then kept the identical mechanism on the trigger, ring and seal ('R1 SURVIVES', line 47) — the survivor now carries strictly less information than the deleted one.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe4.mjs — two contexts colorScheme light/dark at 1440x900 on /#/, read getComputedStyle(documentElement) --accent-view/--accent-live and the computed color of .view-select-trigger svg, .dock-tools-btn svg/span and the Login button's color/borderColor.
defects.proposedCure: Stop encoding view identity as hue. Dock.vue:255-262 already argues the glyph is the stronger continuity carrier ('the same view icon exists at both morph endpoints… a stronger continuity read than a 1px rim') — finish that argument, delete accentHueShift and the --accent-view-<id> token family, and give the auth action its primacy through the design system's own primary-button variant, which is scheme-stable.

defects.defect: RTL: the @mbabb wordmark bidi-reorders to `mbabb@`, and the dock's two directional affordances (Tools ArrowRight / Back ArrowLeft) do not mirror, so the enter/exit motif is inverted wholesale.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png — the dock renders `mbabb@ | ← Login | → Tools 🖌 | 🏠 Home ⌄`; shots/rtl-mobile/picker.png shows the same wordmark break. Sources: ProfileSection.vue:140 (@mbabb text, no bidi isolation), ActionBarToggle.vue:103 (ArrowRight), Dock.vue:154 (ArrowLeft, 'Back'). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose'; 'chrome, navigation and layout follow logical inline/block direction'.
defects.mechanism: A handle beginning with '@' is a neutral-then-Latin run; in an RTL paragraph direction the neutral leading '@' resolves to the right of the Latin run. No dir="ltr"/unicode-bidi:isolate wrapper. Separately, the layer-swap affordance is drawn with physical arrow glyphs while its meaning ('forward into the layer' / 'back out') is logical.
defects.reproduction: Open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png and read the dock band; or re-run states.mjs matrix rtl-desktop (documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl') post-load, per its MT-F022 fix #1).
defects.proposedCure: dir="ltr" / unicode-bidi:isolate on @mbabb and on the slug pill (same family — ProfileSection.vue:75, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:50). Replace the two physical arrows with one logical chevron primitive that flips with `direction`: there are exactly two instances and they must always agree, so they should be one component, not two icon imports.

defects.defect: Three visible dividers for four visible seats — a line between every adjacent pair — in a row where every one of those four items already draws its own capsule seat.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe5.mjs·A at 1440x900: separators:7 in the nav subtree, visibleSeparators:3. Rendered scratchpad/D-dock-light.png: [Home ⌄] | [🖌 Tools →] | [Login] | [@mbabb]. Sources: ProfileSection.vue:49 AND :123 (a separator on both sides of the auth block), ActionBarToggle.vue:82. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 terminal verb REMOVE/KEEP and §5 law 4: 'A divider is retained only when grouping would be ambiguous without it. Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative.'
defects.mechanism: Each dock sub-component ships its own DockSeparator as local furniture, so the count is the sum of independent decisions rather than one composition decision. The maximum possible duplication (n−1 lines for n seats) is reached exactly because no one owns the row.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe5.mjs — count nav .dock-separator total vs those with rect>0 and not inside [inert], at 1440x900 on /#/.
defects.proposedCure: Zero dividers in the main layer; the capsule seats already group and the dock's own gap token supplies the rhythm. Separator ownership moves to the layer composition (Dock.vue), never to the leaf components — a leaf cannot know whether its boundary is ambiguous.

defects.defect: Five operable height rungs (22/28/32/40/44) inside one dock, and ActionBarToggle's source comment asserts its box 'lands at the sibling controls' 2.5rem height' when the measured height is 32px and the named siblings are 40px.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe5.mjs·A main layer at 1440: Select view 32 | Toggle action bar 32 | Login 28 | @mbabb 28. D-dock-probe3.mjs other layers: Save edit / Cancel edit / Back / Open color input = 40; action buttons = 32; slug controls = 22; mobile Back = 44. Claim under test: ActionBarToggle.vue:147-153 '…the box lands at the sibling controls' 2.5rem height' (2.5rem = 40px). Measured 32px — 8px wrong.
defects.mechanism: ActionBarToggle.vue:155 sets `--dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem` — a consumer re-deriving the producer's box model from padding instead of consuming a height/density token. Padding-derived sizing cannot land on a target height because it does not know the content box. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7 (glyph size, target size and reservation are separate quantities) and PR-12.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe5.mjs — map every non-inert nav button with rect>0 to its accessible name and rounded height, at 1440x900 on /#/; then node D-dock-probe3.mjs for the other layers' heights.
defects.proposedCure: One dock control rung declared once as a producer token (a `density` prop / --dock-control-size) and consumed by every seat; the compact register is for genuinely secondary glyphs and must still clear 24px. Delete the --dock-compact-control-padding override. And delete the assertion in the comment: a comment that states a measurement must either be true or not exist.

defects.defect: A dock layer swap jolts the pill 81px sideways and shrinks it 162px, unanimated — the persistent chrome jumps on a single click of Login.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe3.mjs at 1440x900: main layer dock {x:484.3, w:471.5, h:62}; slug-edit layer dock {x:565.5, w:309.0, h:62}. Δx = +81.2px, Δw = −162.5px. glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css cross-fades opacity only ('.dock-crossfade > .dock-face {opacity:0} … .is-active {opacity:1}'), so the box change is instantaneous. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 4: the dock owns a reserved band and its expanded/collapsed/mounted states do not move the scene.
defects.mechanism: GlassDock is instantiated with :fit-content="true" (Dock.vue:132) while hosting four DockLayers of very different intrinsic widths as grid-area:1/1 siblings. fit-content therefore tracks whichever layer is active, making the dock's inline size a property of the layer rather than of the dock.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe3.mjs (matrix B) — 1440x900, goto /#/, read .glass-dock rect, click Login, wait, read .glass-dock rect again.
defects.proposedCure: The dock's inline size is a property of the dock. Either size the container to the max of its layers (they are already coincident grid siblings, so `grid-template-columns: max-content` over all faces gives it for free), or drive width on the producer's morph spring so the change is a motion rather than a jump. Drop :fit-content on a multi-layer dock.

defects.defect: The single layout-forcing animation in the dock is the one that fires on boot: the Tools presence slot transitions grid-template-columns, and it uses a duration/ease register while the seal beside it uses a spring register.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:120-128 — `transition: grid-template-columns var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-standard), opacity …`. The component's own header at :12-16 records that it fires on the app's boot composition ('the pane mounts a beat after the dock, so its action-bar context arrives ~170ms in — the slot visibly GREW the pill on EVERY load'). Everything else in the dock is transform/opacity only: vj-settle = scale(1)→1.03→1 at demo/styles/animations.css:170. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: 'Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register.'
defects.mechanism: grid-template-columns is a layout-animated property; the .is-live double-rAF gate suppresses the visible boot growth but not the layout work on every genuine toggle. Two motion registers in one component (duration/ease on the slot, --spring-snappy on the seal and settle).
defects.reproduction: Read ActionBarToggle.vue:115-128 and demo/styles/animations.css:170; observe the slot transition in DevTools Performance while toggling the Tools presence (navigate picker → browse → picker).
defects.proposedCure: Animate the slot with transform: scaleX() + opacity on a fixed-basis box, or do not animate it at all — a dock control appearing is not a spatial-continuity event. If it stays, it moves onto the producer's spring register so the dock speaks one motion language.

defects.defect: CORRECTION TO r1: r1's strongest BLOCKER ('the dock is keyboard-unreachable on Safari; 1 of 4 controls in the tab order') is a known false-signal class the repository's own harness rules out.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs:7-9 — 'keyboard rows are meaningless in WebKit alone — macOS ships Full Keyboard Access OFF, so run ENGINE=chromium before believing any focus gap, and key focus identity by DOM path, never by label (see probes/kbd-reach.mjs)'. Independent Chromium reproduction, D-dock-probe1.mjs at 1440x900: tab order = Select view → Toggle action bar → Login → @mbabb → [page] Select color space → …, all four dock controls present and in visual order.
defects.mechanism: Safari's 'Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage' is a macOS user setting that excludes bare <button> from sequential focus on EVERY site; Playwright's WebKit inherits the OFF default. It is a property of the harness environment, not of this dock.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe1.mjs — Chromium 1440x900, 12 sequential Tab presses from load, logging document.activeElement DOM path + accessible name after each.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the BLOCKER framing so the root does not ship a row no reviewer with FKA enabled can reproduce. KEEP the underlying observation as a MAJOR: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 row 6 specifies a horizontal Dock roving-focus rail (Right/Left movement, Home/End, activation separate from movement) and Dock.vue implements zero keyboard handling — the dock is a loose row of independent buttons where the constitution specifies a rail.

defects.defect: Rendered text from three inactive dock layers is present in the nav's innerText/textContent, including a bare '→' and the full specimen colour string.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe1.mjs at 1440x900: navInnerText = "→ | Home | Tools | Login | @mbabb | dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"; navTextContent = "→lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)HomeToolsPickerAbout Login @mbabb dev misconfigured…". Source of the leading arrow: Dock.vue:137, a bare → in the non-active mobile-edit layer. glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/crossfade.css applies only `opacity:0; pointer-events:none` to inactive .dock-face — not visibility:hidden.
defects.mechanism: innerText excludes display:none but includes opacity:0 content, so inactive-layer text is rendered text. AT is protected because the faces are inert, but every text-based probe, crawler, snapshot test and bodyTextLength metric reads content from three layers the user cannot see — which is how a shell text metric can move with nothing visible changing.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe1.mjs — read document.querySelector('nav').innerText and .textContent at rest on /#/ at 1440x900.
defects.proposedCure: aria-hidden="true" on the connector arrow at minimum; better, it is a ::before/border between the two WatercolorDots, not a text node. Long-term, the layer set should be v-if'd on activation rather than kept mounted — four always-mounted layers is why three of them are always leaking.

defects.defect: A role="alert" node is mounted permanently in the nav band from first paint, and carries an infinite pulse animation in persistent chrome.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:47-52 returns {variant:"misconfigured", role:"alert", label:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"}; DockStatusLamp.vue:12-20 renders it with the band. Measured live (D-dock-probe2.mjs at 390): lamp {x:348, y:43, w:26, h:18, role:"alert", text:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", labelDisplay:"none"}. Rendered at 1440: scratchpad/D-desk-slugedit.png (right edge) and scratchpad/D-tablet-portrait.png. DockStatusLamp.vue:109-122: `lamp-dot-pulse 2.4s … infinite`.
defects.mechanism: role="alert" is an assertive live region intended for dynamic, time-sensitive changes; a node present at first paint fires an interruption on every load. The pulse is correctly wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so PRM users are unaffected, but it is unbounded motion in persistent chrome with no pause control (cf. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6's five-second/pause rule for ambient motion).
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe2.mjs — read .dock-status-lamp rect, role and text at 390x844 on /#/ against the dev server; or read status-lamp.ts:47-52.
defects.proposedCure: role="status" for a lamp that exists from first paint (assertive interruption is for a state that CHANGES). Bound the pulse to a finite count, or drop it — a dev-config error does not become more legible by blinking forever.

defects.defect: Two template-ref idioms fourteen lines apart in one file, and two computed properties that only re-spell `?? null`.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:74 `const dockRef = useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof GlassDock>>('dockRef')` (Vue 3.5, per owner edict 7) alongside Dock.vue:60 `const slugEditRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof SlugEditLayer> | null>(null)` for the same job. Dock.vue:39-40 `const actionBar = computed(() => actionBarProp ?? null)` and `const genericBar = computed(() => genericActionBar ?? null)` where both props are already typed `… | null | undefined` (Dock.vue:31).
defects.mechanism: Incremental modernisation without a sweep: useTemplateRef was adopted for the new ref and the old one was left. The computed wrappers are pure indirection (owner edict 3, KISS) — they exist only so template call sites can write `actionBar` instead of `actionBarProp`.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:39-40, :60, :74.
defects.proposedCure: useTemplateRef for both; delete the two computeds and rename the destructured props. Note the deeper issue the slugEditRef exposes: Dock proxies two child methods (onStartSlugEdit, onCopySlug) from two different menus through a template ref — prop/event/ref triangulation for one action. The Account-Dialog move (D2-04) deletes the ref entirely.

defects.defect: CARRIED AND SHARPENED from r1 D-5: the open view menu has zero visual selected-state marking in either scheme, and the one lawfully coloured row (Palettes) therefore impersonates the selection.
defects.evidence: D-dock-probe7.mjs, both schemes: all 7 options report fontWeight "400", backgroundColor "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" and one <svg> child each (the view icon, not an indicator); only Home carries aria-selected "true". Rendered scratchpad/D-viewmenu-light.png: Home is typographically identical to Browse/Extract/Mix/Generate/Gradient, and the only visually marked row is Palettes (the Q5-sanctioned pastel ramp). Sources: DockViewSelect.vue:97 and :127 set hide-indicator on every SelectItem; :99-109 records that the font-semibold marker was retired.
defects.mechanism: hide-indicator strips the producer's SelectItem indicator gutter and the weight marker was deleted at P4-R4, leaving selection expressed only through aria-selected. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only' — here selection is not even colour, it is nothing; §4.2's ColorSpaceSelector rule ('deletes hide-indicator and consumes the sole producer SelectItem indicator/gutter') is the same mechanism, unapplied here. Menu rows are also Fraunces (DockViewSelect.vue:91), against §4's 'control or label, INCLUDING dropdown options → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'.
defects.reproduction: node D-dock-probe7.mjs — light and dark contexts at 1440x900, click .view-select-trigger, then read every [role=option]'s aria-selected, computed fontWeight, computed backgroundColor and indicator-child count.
defects.proposedCure: Delete hide-indicator from both SelectItem blocks and consume the producer's indicator gutter — it is scheme-, monochrome- and forced-colors-safe by construction, which no consumer-side marker can be. The Palettes ramp then means 'this destination is about colour', not 'this is where you are'.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) of `demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — the component does not exist below `(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)`. Measured absent at 390x844 (mobile) and at 720x450 (= a 1440x900 desktop at 200% browser zoom), present at 1440x900. Cause chain: `demo/color-picker/App.vue:310-312` (breakpoint) -> `:77` mobile pane slot has no `:on-mount` -> `:105` only the desktop-left slot passes `:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"` -> `:323-328` sole writer of `colorPickerRef` -> `:38` `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"` -> `Dock.vue:41,153` `hasAnyActionBar` gates the layer that hosts `ColorInput`. The app's only "type any CSS colour" affordance — whose own help popover reads "Any valid CSS color string is accepted" — is therefore desktop-landscape-only, breaking VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32 (§3 law 6, "the same top dock" on mobile), :99 (§5, "every spatial action has a keyboard/numeric equivalent") and WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (What was checked and found sound is recorded in report §8: `useTemplateRef` + reactive props destructure are correct Vue 3.5; `verbatimModuleSyntax` compliance is clean — the one type-only import is `import type`; MT-F001 does not crash the app (measured `pageErrors: []`); `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured via the global guard at `demo/styles/animations.css:184-193`; the error badge's contrast is 4.70:1 at 12px, passing WCAG AA; `input-mode-flash` is correctly scoped/renamed by the SFC compiler; the U9 blur snap-back does what its comment claims, measured.)

defects.defect: The component is structurally absent below `(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)` — no CSS-colour text entry exists on any phone, portrait tablet, or desktop at 200% browser zoom.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-2.json): 390x844 touch -> {"missing": true}, aria-label inventory contains no "Open color input"; 720x450 -> {"opened":{"present":false}}; 1440x900 -> present, 324.72 x 45.91 px. Frame: frames/G-mobile-dock.png shows Home / Picker-About / ⋮ and no Tools control. Source chain: demo/color-picker/App.vue:310-312, :77, :101-105, :323-328, :38; demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:41,153; demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:115.
defects.mechanism: viewport-gated mount: the dock action-bar context is a side effect of which pane slot the media query happened to mount
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ at 390x844 or 720x450 -> exercise every dock control -> no colour input exists. Same URL at 1440x900 -> Tools -> second toggle -> it appears.
defects.proposedCure: Lift the action-bar context to the route table (usePaneRouter) so it is breakpoint-independent, and host the same field in the dock's mobile layer; if the dock cannot carry it below 1024px, the field belongs in the Picker inspector at all widths. It may not simply vanish.

defects.defect: `btn-interactive` — the class both of the component's long comment blocks credit with hover/press legs, focus register and disabled opacity — matches ZERO CSS rules. The send button has identical computed style at rest, hover, active and focus, and no focus indicator.
defects.evidence: Live CSSOM walk of every stylesheet at http://localhost:9000/#/: selectors containing "btn-interactive" -> {"count": 0, "hits": []}. Static: grep -rn "btn-interactive" finds no CSS in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css (v7.0.0) or demo/styles/*.css. Measured deltas (frames/probe-3.json): rest/hover/active/focus all { opacity:1, scale:none, transform:matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-12), bg:rgba(0,0,0,0), outlineStyle:none, boxShadow:none, filter:none }; hoverDelta:false, focusRing:false; transition computes to `all` (Tailwind preflight default). Claims at ColorInput.vue:61-66 and :327-334.
defects.mechanism: design-system bypass — a local recipe was 'retired onto' a producer atom that does not exist, deleting the states instead of moving them
defects.reproduction: Open the field (desktop >=1024px, Tools -> input toggle), hover the arrow, press it, Tab to it. Nothing changes at any step. Verify with getComputedStyle or the CSSOM walk above.
defects.proposedCure: Stop hand-rolling the control: replace the bare `<button class="send-btn btn-interactive">` with the glass-ui `DockControl`/`Button` its dock siblings already use (ActionBarLayer.vue:129, Dock.vue:143), which carry the house hover/press/focus/disabled registers. Delete the two comment blocks describing motion that never existed.

defects.defect: The parse-error badge paints over both the user's typed value and the send button — 63.8% of the commit control's area — so the user can see neither their mistake nor the affordance that would retry it.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-1.json, B-f001-light.afterEnter): badgeRect {x:682.1,y:31.4,w:101,h:18.4}, sendRect {x:763.1,y:28.5,w:24,h:24}, overlapPx2 367.5 of sendAreaPx2 576 = 63.8%. Frame frames/B-f001-error.png shows the typed `oklch()` surviving only as a sliver. Source: ColorInput.vue:335-343 (.send-btn right:0.25rem top:50%) vs :348-366 (.error-badge right:0.5rem top:50%); both render simultaneously (:76-82 v-else, :87 v-if).
defects.mechanism: two absolutely-positioned siblings competing for one 24px gutter seat
defects.reproduction: Desktop >=1024px -> Tools -> colour input -> select all -> type `oklch()` -> Enter.
defects.proposedCure: Move the commit action out of the text box entirely (a named DockControl sibling of the field), and express the parse verdict as a persistent control state (`aria-invalid` + one inline message below the dock) rather than an overlay slab inside the field.

defects.defect: The failed state carries no programmatic semantics at all and evaporates after 2 s while the invalid text remains.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-1.json): inputAria {invalid:null, describedby:null}; badgeStyles {role:null, ariaLive:null, id:"", pointerEvents:"none"}; after2s {badge:false, text:"oklch()", border:"lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)"}. Timer at demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:57 (setTimeout 2000). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 (§4.1 'failed states are never color-only... error/status are explicit'), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 (PR-08). glass-ui 7.0.0 ships the fix it cannot use: `useUserInvalidAria` (dist/forms.d.ts, dist/composables/dom/useUserInvalidAria.d.ts) binds FORM CONTROLS, which a contenteditable span is not.
defects.mechanism: error rendered as decorative pop-in rather than a control state
defects.reproduction: Type an invalid colour, press Enter, inspect the field: no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby; the badge has no role/aria-live; wait 2 s and all visual trace reverts while the invalid text stays.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt glass-ui `Input` + `useUserInvalidAria` so `aria-invalid` is wired on blur and cleared on correction; the message gets an id and `aria-describedby`, and persists until the input changes rather than until a timer fires.

defects.defect: Every keystroke resizes the dock (137.3 px of travel while typing one 13-character colour name), and because the field grows instead of clipping, the mask/ellipsis/text-center apparatus — the most bespoke CSS in the file — is unreachable dead code.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-3.json, typing `rebeccapurple` char by char): input width 61.5 -> 198.8 px (span 137.3); dock width 179.5 -> 316.8 px (span 137.3, 1:1). Measured (frames/probe-1.json, C-focus-dark.longValue) for a 46-char value: {scrollW:586, clientW:586, overflowing:false}. Dead declarations: ColorInput.vue:16 (overflow-hidden, text-ellipsis, whitespace-nowrap, text-center), :300-301 (mask-image, --input-action-width:2.5rem), :303-306 (:focus mask cancel). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 (§3 law 4 'the dock owns a reserved band... do not move the scene'), :78 (§4 'reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis').
defects.mechanism: unreserved content-sized field inside a reserved band
defects.reproduction: Open the field, select all, type `rebeccapurple` one character at a time and watch the dock pill collapse to ~61 px then inflate 137 px; measure `.dock-face` width per keystroke.
defects.proposedCure: Give the field a reserved `inline-size` sized to the widest legal serialization (`color(display-p3 ...)`) plus `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; the band stops moving and the mask/ellipsis/text-center machinery can then be deleted outright rather than kept as dead ornament.

defects.defect: Re-submitting the same invalid string produces no feedback whatsoever — no error, no success, no change — because a memo short-circuits ahead of the try/catch.
defects.evidence: Source: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:62 `if (!input || input === previousInvalid) return;` returns before flashParseError() (`previousInvalid` set at :85). Measured (scratchpad/DD-probe4.mjs, guarded on aria-label==="Enter a CSS color"): submit1_badge true; badgeGoneAfter2s true; textAfter2s "oklch()"; submit2_badge false; submit2_badge_late false; pageErrors []. Debounce is 2000 ms (useColorParsing.ts:92).
defects.mechanism: transient-only truth plus a memo that suppresses the retry signal
defects.reproduction: Open the field -> select all -> type `oklch()` -> Enter (badge appears) -> wait 2.4 s (badge gone, text still `oklch()`) -> press Enter again -> nothing happens, ever.
defects.proposedCure: The parse verdict must be derived state on the current input, not a one-shot timer with an invalid-input memo. Recompute validity on every commit; clear it on correction, not on a clock.

defects.defect: A hand-rolled `contenteditable` span with `role="textbox"` stands in for a text field, in direct breach of the canon's explicit 'no duplicate contenteditable path', while glass-ui ships `Input` with exactly the props this component lacks.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:11-27. Measured attributes (frames/probe-1.json): contenteditable "" (i.e. "true", not "plaintext-only"), aria-multiline null, aria-invalid null, aria-describedby null, spellcheck null, inputmode null, enterkeyhint null, autocapitalize null, autocorrect null. glass-ui 7.0.0 `dist/components/input/types.d.ts` InputProps includes placeholder, invalid, disabled, enterkeyhint, inputmode, pattern, readonly, size. Canon verbatim, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:75 (§5 law 10): '...commit/cancel/error semantics and no duplicate `contenteditable` path.'
defects.mechanism: design-system bypass — hand-rolled primitive
defects.reproduction: Read ColorInput.vue:11-27 against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/input/types.d.ts and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:75.
defects.proposedCure: Substitute the glass-ui `Input` (v-model + :invalid + :placeholder + enterkeyhint + inputmode). That one move retires D-04, D-08, half of D-11, the value arm of D-13, and D-15, and makes `useUserInvalidAria` usable.

defects.defect: The bare `contenteditable` (not `plaintext-only`) with no paste handler admits arbitrary markup: a formatted paste injects foreign styling into the dock and inflates the band by 43.8%.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-1.json, D-paste): innerHTML 'red', innerText 'red', height 66 px vs 45.91 px at rest (+20.09 px, +43.8%). Frame frames/D-paste.png shows 32 px lime bold text in the dock. No `paste` listener exists in the SFC; the two innerText writers (:191, :265, :278) only repair on blur or model change.
defects.mechanism: uncontrolled rich-text editing surface
defects.reproduction: Focus the field, select all, and insert formatted HTML the way a real paste does (document.execCommand('insertHTML', false, 'red')) — or copy a colour token out of any syntax-highlighted code block and paste. Measure the field's height before and after.
defects.proposedCure: Use a real `<input type="text">` (glass-ui `Input`), which structurally cannot hold markup. If contenteditable were kept, `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` plus a paste handler would be the minimum — but the primitive already exists.

defects.defect: The Crown reveal animation cannot run: the inline `animation: crown-appear ...` in the template names a keyframe that Vue's scoped-style compiler renamed away, so the entire four-stop gold choreography is dead.
defects.evidence: Source: ColorInput.vue:33-40 sets `style="animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) ..."` inline in the TEMPLATE; :369-376 defines `@keyframes crown-appear` inside `<style scoped>`. Compiler: node_modules/@vue/compiler-sfc/dist/compiler-sfc.cjs.js:8053-8080 renames keyframes and rewrites animation declarations only within the same PostCSS root. Served CSS (curl of the Vite style URL, scoped=55dadc03) contains only `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03`. Live CSSOM (frames/probe-1.json): crownKeyframeNames: ["crown-appear-55dadc03"] — no un-suffixed name exists. The `:key="crownKey"` remount (demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:64) exists solely to restart an animation that cannot start.
defects.mechanism: register drift — inline style attribute escapes the scoped-CSS keyframe rename
defects.reproduction: curl 'http://localhost:9000/@fs/<repo>/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css' | grep crown  -> only `crown-appear-55dadc03`. Then in the live page, walk document.styleSheets for KEYFRAMES rules matching /crown/ -> same single suffixed name.
defects.proposedCure: Move the animation declaration into the scoped `<style>` block (a `.crown-appear` class on the element) so the compiler rewrites the name, and delete the inline style attribute — which is also an owner-edict-5 per-instance override.

defects.defect: In forced-colors mode the field has a measured ZERO focus delta, and the mask survives to fade out the field's system-coloured border and ink over the last 40 px.
defects.evidence: Measured with forcedColors:'active' (frames/probe-2.json): rest {borderColor:"rgb(0, 0, 0)", outlineStyle:"none", bg:"rgb(255,255,255)"}; focused {borderColor:"rgb(0, 0, 0)", outlineStyle:"none", boxShadow:"none"}; deltaBorder:false; maskImage still "linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0,0,0) calc(100% - 40px), rgba(0,0,0,0) 100%)". Frame frames/I-forced-colors.png. Source: ColorInput.vue:16 `focus-visible:outline-none`, :162-166 the only focus register is `{borderColor: cssColor.value}`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84 (§4.1 'Focus remains visibly distinct... forced colors and reduced transparency').
defects.mechanism: focus expressed only as an author-coloured border, with the outline suppressed
defects.reproduction: Launch Chromium with forcedColors:'active', open the field, read getComputedStyle at rest and at focus — border rgb(0,0,0) in both, outline-style none in both.
defects.proposedCure: Never suppress the outline; adopt the house `focus-ring` register (which every dock sibling carries) so focus survives forced colors, and drop the mask so the boundary is not erased in high-contrast mode.

defects.defect: The disabled send button is pixel-identical to the enabled one — the only signal is a cursor shape, i.e. hover-only, mouse-only, invisible to touch and to assistive technology.
defects.evidence: Measured in propose mode with an empty field (frames/probe-2.json, K-propose): disabled true, btnOpacity "1", btnRect {w:24,h:24}, btnCursor "not-allowed", svgStroke 'stroke: oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402);' — the same inline accent as the enabled state. Compare frames/K-propose.png with frames/A-rest-light.png: identical arrow. Source: ColorInput.vue:70 (:disabled), :344-346 (the only disabled rule is cursor). No aria-disabled. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 (PR-07).
defects.mechanism: missing state register (consequence of D-02) plus an inline per-instance stroke override that would defeat any producer disabled treatment
defects.reproduction: Open the field -> cycle the toolbar to propose mode -> leave the field empty -> read getComputedStyle on `.send-btn`: opacity 1, same rect, same stroke, while `.disabled === true`.
defects.proposedCure: Use the glass-ui Button/DockControl disabled register and delete the inline `:style="{ stroke: safeAccent }"` so the producer treatment can win.

defects.defect: The send button is nameless — it is, in full, the single `namelessButtons` defect the mega-tranche visual audit recorded for route `/#/` — and its 24 px target shrinks to 22 px when it enters the loading state.
defects.evidence: Measured live on /#/: 26 buttons total, 1 nameless -> `<button data-v-55dadc03 class="send-btn btn-interactive">` with ariaLabel null, title null, textContent "", svg not aria-hidden, rect {w:24,h:24}. Cross-reference docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:96,103 — namelessButtons on safari-desktop-light /#/ = 1 and safari-desktop-dark /#/ = 1. Target shrink: ColorInput.vue:73 Loader2 `w-3.5 h-3.5` (14px) vs :74 ArrowRight `w-4 h-4` (16px). The hosts' own comments enforce the opposite law: Dock.vue:140-142, ActionBarLayer.vue:126-128.
defects.mechanism: icon-only control with no accessible name; glyph box doubling as target box
defects.reproduction: On http://localhost:9000/#/ evaluate [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b => !b.getAttribute('aria-label') && !b.textContent.trim() && !b.getAttribute('title')) -> exactly one hit, `.send-btn`.
defects.proposedCure: Give the action a name and a real seat: a named glass-ui DockControl ('Apply color' / 'Propose name') at the dock's 40 px control scale, sized independently of its glyph (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72, §5 law 7).

defects.defect: The type register is off the closed matrix in four places, measured: the value renders 13.5% larger than every other mono register in the same dock; the popover title uses the palette-identity role; the help prose renders in Fraunces; the error badge uses a raw Tailwind rung.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-2.json, typeRegister): .color-input value 18.608px Fira Code; dock Login button (text-mono-small) 16.4px Fira Code; dock Tools label (text-small) 16.4px Fraunces. Delta +2.208px (+13.5%), not an adjacent golden rung. ColorInput.vue:16 applies only the family class `fira-code` with no size role. ColorInput.vue:97 uses `text-subheading` (reserved for palette identity per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:71) for a popover section heading. ColorInput.vue:94 `font-display` forces Fraunces onto the prose at :98-100 — visible in frames/H-hover-popover.png. ColorInput.vue:353 `@apply text-xs`, compiled to `font-size: var(--text-xs, 0.75rem)` in the served CSS. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:68-78 (§4, closed matrix), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:78 (§5 law 13).
defects.mechanism: register drift — no role token, ambient inheritance
defects.reproduction: Open the field and compare getComputedStyle('.color-input').fontSize (18.608px) with the dock's `.text-mono-small` sibling (16.4px); hover the field and read the popover heading/prose families.
defects.proposedCure: Apply the role tokens the matrix names — `text-mono-small` on the value, `text-heading` on the popover title, `text-prose`/Plus Jakarta Sans on the help copy, `text-small` on the badge — and remove `font-display` from the PopoverContent root so it stops forcing the display family onto prose.

defects.defect: `text-center` sits over a 12 px / 36 px padding pair, so the value is permanently 12.00 px left of the pill's optical centre — and three different numbers (36, 40, 28) describe the same action gutter.
defects.evidence: Measured (frames/probe-1.json): paddingLeft "12px", paddingRight "36px", contentBoxCentreX 714.00, borderBoxCentreX 726.00, delta exactly 12.00 px. Source: ColorInput.vue:16 (px-3 + text-center), :18 ('pr-9': true = 36px), :300 (--input-action-width: 2.5rem = 40px), :336-337 (.send-btn right:0.25rem, 24px box = 28px). Because the field is content-sized (D-05), text-align:center never resolves anything — the real layout is a 1:3 asymmetry. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 (§5 law 8, 'real rendered relation wins over token intent').
defects.mechanism: unreserved geometry — a centring declaration over asymmetric padding, with three uncoordinated gutter constants
defects.reproduction: Open the field and compute (x + paddingLeft + (width - paddingLeft - paddingRight)/2) vs (x + width/2): 714.00 vs 726.00.
defects.proposedCure: Move the action out of the box (see D-03's cure); the field then has symmetric padding, `text-center` becomes either honest or unnecessary, and the three gutter constants collapse to zero.

defects.defect:
The empty state is undesigned in colour mode, and the placeholder mechanism is defeated by the browser's own `
` filler after any type-then-clear cycle.
defects.evidence:
Measured (frames/probe-1.json, C-focus-dark.empty) after select-all + Backspace: text "\n", html "
", dataPlaceholder null, rectH 45.91, badge false. `:empty` therefore stops matching (ColorInput.vue:321-325). Measured on mount (frames/probe-2.json, K-propose): placeholderShows '"propose a name..."' — the mechanism works exactly once, before any interaction. `data-placeholder` is set only in propose mode (:261) and removed on exit (:264), so colour mode has no placeholder at all. Frame frames/C-empty-dark.png: a ~60 px black square with one arrow. parseAndSetColor returns early on empty input (useColorParsing.ts:62), so no error either.
defects.mechanism: `:empty` used as an emptiness test against a contenteditable
defects.reproduction:
Focus the field, Ctrl/Cmd+A, Backspace -> read innerHTML -> `
`; the `:empty` placeholder rule can no longer match. In colour mode the same gesture leaves an unlabelled empty box.
defects.proposedCure: Use a real `<input>` with a native `placeholder` (glass-ui Input exposes it) so emptiness is a value state, not a DOM-shape test — and give colour mode a placeholder (`e.g. oklch(70% 0.15 200)`) it currently lacks entirely.

defects.defect: The only help text, the only canonical serialization, and the only mount of the Parse-Lab echo are gated behind a 300 ms hover popover — with no click, focus or keyboard path — which is simultaneously redundant (the value appears 4x on screen), carries two dividers in a four-line panel, and occludes the route H1 and the Picker headline.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:3-8 `<Popover trigger="hover" :open-delay="300">` wrapping the field; :94-110 is the only mount of `<ParseEchoReadout />`. Measured (frames/probe-2.json, hoverPopover): count 2, texts[1] "Enter a colorAny valid CSS color string is accepted. lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%) lab l 92% a 88.8 b 20 α 0.827 outside srgb gamut". Frame frames/H-hover-popover.png shows the panel covering the route H1 and the Picker's numeric headline, with two Separator rules (:101, :108). Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 (PR-07), :49 (PR-05 REMOVE), :69 (§5 law 4), :71 (§5 law 6 'subtraction precedes explanation').
defects.mechanism: hover-only disclosure carrying non-decorative information; tooltip proliferation (a second Tooltip on the same control at :30-59)
defects.reproduction: Hover the field for >300 ms on desktop and read the panel; then attempt to reach it by click, focus or keyboard — there is no path. On touch (and below 1024px, per D-01) it is unreachable entirely.
defects.proposedCure: Move the Parse-Lab echo into the Picker inspector where it is reachable without a mouse; reduce the popover to a click/focus-triggered hint or delete it, and drop both Separators and the value restatement (the value is already in the field).

defects.defect: Propose-mode success and failure are both silent: failure is a `console.warn`, success emits nothing, and the comment 'Signal parent to exit propose mode' describes an emit that does not exist — the SFC has no defineEmits at all.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:230-247: `await session.ensureSession()` (silently mints an account), `catch (e: any) { console.warn("[ColorInput] Failed to propose name:", e?.message); }`, and the comment at :238 above a line that only rewrites innerText. Repo grep: no `defineEmits` in the file. glass-ui 7.0.0 exports `./toast`. After success the user remains in propose mode with aria-label 'Propose a color name' while the field displays a colour string. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 (§5 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace'); PALETTE-CONTRACT.md:172 states the identical principle absolutely for the sibling export path — 'a visible terminal/retryable operation state — never a partial download or `console.warn`-only result'.
defects.mechanism: transient-only truth — a network operation with no operation state
defects.reproduction: Enter propose mode, type a name, submit with the API unreachable: the only artefact is a console warning. Submit successfully: the field text changes and nothing else; the mode never exits.
defects.proposedCure: Route both outcomes through `@mkbabb/glass-ui/toast` (or a durable inline status), emit a real `proposed` event so the parent can leave propose mode, and drop the `any` in the catch.

defects.defect: Direction is physical throughout — the action gutter, the fade mask and the button stay pinned to the physical right under `dir="rtl"` — and the field declares no LTR isolation for an LTR-only CSS grammar.
defects.evidence: Measured with dir="rtl" (frames/probe-1.json, E-rtl): computed direction "rtl" while paddingLeft "12px" / paddingRight "36px" are unchanged, maskImage still "linear-gradient(to right, ...)", sendRect.x 848.4 inside input 551.6..876.3, sendOnInlineStartSide false. Frame frames/E-rtl.png: the dock chrome mirrors (Back moves right) but the field's internals do not. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150 (§6.1 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document') and :154 ('CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose').
defects.mechanism: physical CSS properties (right, to right, pr-*) where logical properties are required
defects.reproduction: Set document.documentElement.dir = 'rtl', open the field, read computed padding-left/right, mask-image and the send button's x — all unchanged from LTR.
defects.proposedCure: Use logical properties (padding-inline-end, inset-inline-end) and a logical mask direction; add `dir="ltr"` / `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the value so its neutrals cannot reorder under an RTL paragraph direction.

defects.defect: An opaque `bg-background` plate with a 1 px `--input` border is a second, foreign material tier improvised inside the dock's structural glass — and it is clipped by a mask the canon explicitly forbids in the dock band.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:16 (`border ... bg-background rounded-input`); measured backgroundColor rgb(251,250,248) fully opaque, borderColor rgb(198,180,159) = --input, while every dock sibling is `glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover`. Frame frames/A-rest-light.png. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19 ('One surface has one tier. An inner card is not automatically another pane of glass.') and :178 (§7 Shell/dock: 'The dock is its own top band, fully visible, focusable, and clipped by neither mask nor card') vs the mask-image at ColorInput.vue:300.
defects.mechanism: material-hierarchy break — a shadcn form-field recipe transplanted into a glass instrument
defects.reproduction: Open the field and compare getComputedStyle backgroundColor/borderColor against any sibling dock control's glass capsule classes; observe the mask fading the plate's own right border in frames/A-rest-light.png.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the glass-ui field primitive at the dock's own material tier (instrument veil / glass capsule) instead of an opaque shadcn plate, and delete the mask (which D-05 shows is dead code anyway).

defects.defect: The mode-flash JS timer is a hard-coded 300 ms standing in for the 450 ms token the CSS animation uses, truncating the animation at 66.7% and snapping the element from an eased mid-state to rest.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:313 `animation: input-mode-flash var(--duration-slow) var(--ease-decelerate)` vs :256 `setTimeout(() => { modeTransition.value = false; }, 300)`. Measured live tokens: --duration-slow 0.45s (450ms), --ease-decelerate cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1). 300/450 = 66.7% through, leaving approx scaleX 0.998 / opacity 0.972 at the cut. Same ad-hoc pattern one file away: ActionBarLayer.vue:62 SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260. Owner edict 6 (animations tokenized).
defects.mechanism: register drift — a magic number desynchronised from the token it mirrors
defects.reproduction: Read --duration-slow off :root (0.45s) against the 300 ms setTimeout at ColorInput.vue:256.
defects.proposedCure: Drive the class removal off `animationend` (or read the token), so the JS lifetime cannot diverge from the CSS duration.

defects.defect: Dead surface: a declared-and-unused prop (plus the type import that exists only to type it), two unused injections, a five-member defineExpose with zero consumers repo-wide, and a third Copy path the canon explicitly rules must be removed.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:139 prop `editTarget` never referenced; :134 `import type { EditTarget }` exists only for it; :146 `cssColorOpaque` and :150 `canProposeName` destructured and never used; :282-288 defineExpose({focus, inputIsFocused, copyAndSetInputColor, onSubmitColor, submitProposedName}) — ActionBarLayer.vue:28 declares `colorInputRef` and never dereferences it, and grep across demo/ e2e/ test/ finds no consumer of any member; :219-223 `copyAndSetInputColor` is a third Copy implementation (ActionToolbar already owns @copy at ActionBarLayer.vue:110), against PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:57 (PR-13, REMOVE, 'total 2->1'); :117 `import { writeClipboard }` is used only by that dead path.
defects.mechanism: dead surface accumulated behind an unconsumed imperative API
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'copyAndSetInputColor|onSubmitColor|inputIsFocused' demo/ e2e/ test/ excluding ColorInput.vue -> no consumers; grep -n 'editTarget|cssColorOpaque|canProposeName' ColorInput.vue -> declaration sites only.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop, the two injections, the whole defineExpose and the Copy path with its clipboard import; the component's contract is its props and (once D-17 is fixed) its emits, not an imperative handle nobody holds.

defects.defect: A `demo/ui/` alias layer creates a dual import path inside a single import block — one line imports glass-ui directly, the next twelve import one-line re-export barrels of the same package.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:117 `import { writeClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` vs :118-129 importing from "../../ui/popover|tooltip|separator". Those barrels are literally `export { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (demo/ui/popover/index.ts), likewise separator and tooltip. The sibling ActionBarLayer.vue:8 imports "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock" directly. Owner edict 2: no aliases, migration shims, dual paths.
defects.mechanism: legacy alias layer surviving a completed migration

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for `demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context Opus 5 seat), spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the product's primary navigation renders with NO LABEL on 7 of its 14 views, because the Select's model value (router-owned, range 14) and its option set (`useDockAdminMode`-owned, range 7) have different owners and nothing constrains them to agree. Proven by three same-matrix screenshots (`browse.png` reads "Browse"; `atmosphere.png` and `admin-users.png` render icon+chevron only) and by reka-ui source (`SelectValue.js:33-42` falls back to `placeholder`, which defaults to `""` and is not passed).
