result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (One axis did prove sound and is recorded as L-11: the component reaches the library correctly by not reaching it at all. `grep -rn 'from "(\.\./)*\.\./src' demo/` → no matches; `grep -rn '@src/' demo/shell demo/palettes demo/picker` → no matches; `vite.config.ts:37-50` GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` so the seven public specifiers cannot drift; `package.json#exports` declares only the 7 subpaths with no `"."` root and correspondingly `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` returns nothing. defects.defect: The dock view-select trigger renders an EMPTY label on 7 of the demo's 14 views: the Select's model value and its option set are owned by different modules with different ranges, so the selected value routinely matches no SelectItem.
defects.evidence: Screenshots, same matrix (safari-desktop-light, 1440 CSS px, isDesktop true): docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the trigger reading "Browse"; atmosphere.png and admin-users.png show icon+chevron with NO text. Mechanism from source: DockViewSelect.vue:73 renders `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with no placeholder; node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Select/SelectValue.js:33-42 computes `selectedLabel` by looking modelValue up in `rootContext.optionsSet` and falling back to "", and `slotText` returns `props.placeholder` (default "", lines 10-14) when the lookup misses. Ranges: `:model-value="currentView"` (Dock.vue:169) has range 14 (viewSchema.ts:30-44); `viewEntries` (Dock.vue:173) has range 7 at a time (useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27,34-40). All three shots also show the "Login" control, i.e. unauthenticated — capture.mjs has no login step (grep for admin|login|auth returns only the five route literals at lines 32-36).
defects.mechanism: split enumeration / no single owner of the navigation taxonomy — the option set and the model value are computed from two different modules
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob or any /#/admin/*) unauthenticated at viewport width >= 1024px. The dock view-select trigger shows its icon and chevron with no visible label. Compare /#/browse, which reads "Browse". Already captured in the harness shots listed above.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT add a placeholder — that hides it. Make it structurally impossible: derive the option set as `viewsInGroup(activeGroup) ∪ {currentView}` so the model value is an option by construction. Requires the single nav schema of L-2.

defects.defect: Three hand-maintained enumerations of the same 14 view identifiers exist in three directories, and two of them directly contradict each other about what "admin" means.
defects.evidence: (1) demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:30-44 + VIEW_MAP :97-234 — the declared SSOT, 14 ViewIds, and it carries NO grouping field at all. (2) demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:22-37 — 14 routes hand-listed, `meta:{admin:true}` on exactly 5 (:31-35); /atmosphere (:29) and /blob (:30) have no meta. (3) demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27 — `userViews` (7) and `adminViews` (7), where adminViews INCLUDES "atmosphere" and "blob". Router says 5 admin views; the dock says 7. viewSchema.ts's own header claims it exists 'to retire the 4-copy ViewId enumeration'; its accentHueShift comment (:66-79) speaks of 'the nine primary views ... in dock order', a nine the dock has never had.
defects.mechanism: incomplete SSOT — VIEW_MAP lacks the `group` field the dock needs, so the enumeration regrew in a third home
defects.reproduction: grep -n "meta: { admin: true }" demo/color-picker/router/index.ts → 5 hits; sed -n '27p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts → 7 ids including atmosphere and blob. Adding a view today requires three synchronised edits and nothing fails if you make two.
defects.proposedCure: One home: `demo/shell/nav/nav-schema.ts` — VIEW_MAP gains `group: "primary"|"tuning"|"admin"` and `path`; `routes.ts` DERIVES the route table from it (`Object.entries(VIEW_MAP).map(...)`) so a view cannot exist without a route; the dock reads `viewsInGroup(g)` instead of re-listing ids.

defects.defect: Seven of fourteen views have no UI reachability at all (URL-typing only), and five of them render the full admin console to an unauthenticated visitor because `meta: { admin: true }` has zero readers and no route guard exists.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "meta.admin\|beforeEach\|beforeResolve\|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` → NO OUTPUT. router/index.ts:44-48 registers exactly one guard, installDocumentTitle. Screenshot: shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png renders 'Users · Manage accounts and permissions', a search field, 'Prune empty' and 'Refresh' while the dock control still reads 'Login'. REPORT.md:128-132 records main=1 and 244-273 chars of text for all five admin routes in every matrix, unauthenticated. Reachability: atmosphere/blob/admin-* appear only in adminViews (useDockAdminMode.ts:27), returned only when `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated` (:35); isAdminMode rises only via the `__admin_toggle__` row (rendered under `v-if="pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value"`, DockViewSelect.vue:114) or via the watcher at :55-59 that fires on ALREADY landing there. Admin auth itself has no nav entry — it is a hidden mode of the slug field (useSlugMigration.ts:51-56). MobileMenuDropdown.vue:36-113 carries no view navigation, so mobile has the same hole. No switchView/router.push/href anywhere in demo/ targets atmosphere or blob.
defects.mechanism: the authorization concept has three partial homes (dead router meta, a menu filter, a template v-if) and no owner
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "meta.admin|beforeEach|beforeResolve|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → empty. Then open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users in a fresh profile: the admin console renders while the dock offers 'Login'.
defects.proposedCure: `demo/shell/nav/guard.ts` — the ONE reader of `meta.group === "admin"`: `router.beforeEach(to => useAdminAuth().isAuthenticated.value || to.meta.group !== "admin" ? true : { name: "picker" })`. Gives the dead metadata its only consumer and makes the menu filter a presentation detail rather than the de-facto gate.

defects.defect: Wrong direction of dependency: the app shell imports from a feature to read platform auth. `demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue` injects `SESSION_PORT_KEY` from `demo/palettes/usePalettePorts` — a laundering hop to a platform singleton the parent already holds.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:8 `import { SESSION_PORT_KEY } from "../../palettes/usePalettePorts"` and :35 `const pm = inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!`. Five shell files do this: DockViewSelect.vue:8, Dock.vue:18, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14. The key is named for the wrong domain — `Symbol("palette.session")` at usePalettePorts.ts:271. The feature does not own the value: usePalettePorts.ts:57 does `const { isAuthenticated: isAdminAuthenticated } = useAdminAuth()`, and demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:17-24 is a module-level singleton (one lazily created `_adminToken` ref shared by all callers, by design). Worse, Dock.vue:37 injects the SAME key and Dock.vue:44 already passes `pm.isAdminAuthenticated` into useDockAdminMode — the value is one level up and deliberately not passed as a prop.
defects.mechanism: feature-shaped port used as the transport for a platform concern; component is half props-driven, half ambient (dual data path)
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "SESSION_PORT_KEY" demo/ → five demo/shell/** importers of demo/palettes/usePalettePorts. Read DockViewSelect.vue:16-23 (five props) then :35 (a sixth input reached around the prop surface).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the edge. This component takes no auth input at all — Dock.vue passes what the option set needs. Where the shell genuinely needs auth (the future guard), call `useAdminAuth()` from `demo/platform/auth` directly: one hop, correct direction, no inject, no feature dependency. Resulting lattice: platform/auth → shell/nav → shell/dock → glass-ui, with features reading the shell and the shell reading no feature.

defects.defect: Two paths to the same design system inside one file, eight lines apart: `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` at line 3 and `../../ui/select` at lines 4-6, where demo/ui/select is a one-line pure re-export of @mkbabb/glass-ui. All 19 demo/ui/* barrels are pure forwards.

defects.defect: `demo/shell/useViewManager.ts` carries a self-declared back-compat type re-export shim preserving compatibility with an import path (`@composables/useViewManager`) that no longer exists, and it is the MAJORITY path for the ViewId family (6 of 9 importers), keeping a dual path alive.

defects.defect: `ViewEntry` is a type-erased duplicate of `PaneConfig & { id: ViewId }`: it re-declares two fields, downgrades `icon: Component` to `icon: unknown`, and opens an `[k: string]: unknown` index signature that makes the type accept anything — forcing an `as` cast at both construction sites and erasing this component's prop contract.
defects.evidence: useDockAdminMode.ts:7-12 `export interface ViewEntry { id: ViewId; label: string; icon: unknown; [k: string]: unknown; }` vs viewSchema.ts:86-96 where `PaneConfig.icon: Component` (typed via `import type { Component } from "vue"`, :15). Casts required at :36 and :38 — `adminViews.map((id) => ({ id, ...viewManager.viewMap[id] } as ViewEntry))`. Erasure propagates into the public prop surface: DockViewSelect.vue:16 `currentIcon: unknown` and :22 `viewEntries: ViewEntry[]`, both then fed to `<component :is>` at :66 and :97 — a position vue-tsc does not check, so the props assert nothing about the one thing the component renders. `grep -rn "ViewEntry" demo/` → 7 hits, confined to these two files. Ownership inversion in the import itself: DockViewSelect.vue:9 takes its PROP TYPE from a composable rather than the schema.
defects.mechanism: a second, weaker type for a concept the schema already owns — duplicate ownership plus deliberate type erasure
defects.reproduction: sed -n '7,12p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts vs sed -n '86,96p' demo/shell/viewSchema.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `ViewEntry`. Use `PaneConfig & { id: ViewId }` from the nav schema — same shape, fully typed, already exported, no cast at either construction site, and the component's prop type stops depending on a stateful composable.

defects.defect: The view-change channel carries two disjoint meanings — a ViewId and the magic sentinel `"__admin_toggle__"` — and the far end casts unvalidated into `router.push` while the type predicate written for exactly that check is never called on the write path.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:105 `<SelectItem value="__admin_toggle__" ...>`. useDockAdminMode.ts:65-73: `function onViewChange(id: string | number | boolean | Record<string, string> | null) { if (typeof id === "string") { if (id === "__admin_toggle__") { toggleAdminMode(); return; } viewManager.switchView(id as ViewId); } }` — the cast lands in `router.push({ name: id })` at useViewManager.ts:79. viewSchema.ts:236 exports `isViewId`, and `grep -rn "isViewId" demo/` shows it used only on the READ path (useViewManager.ts:45, useDocumentTitle.ts:50). Doubled defensive typing that validates nothing: DockViewSelect.vue:80 already narrows with `emit('update:modelValue', id as string)` and declares the emit `[id: string]` at :26, yet the receiver re-widens to reka's full AcceptableValue union.
defects.mechanism: one channel, two message types (navigate | toggle-mode) plus an unchecked cast at the module boundary
defects.reproduction: sed -n '65,73p' demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts; grep -rn "isViewId" demo/ shows no call site on the write path.
defects.proposedCure: Split the channel: `emits: { navigate: [ViewId]; toggleAdmin: [] }`. Type `switchView(id: ViewId)` and let callers narrow with `isViewId` — no cast, no sentinel, no magic string with no home.

defects.defect: `demo/shell/dock/index.ts` forms a genuine ESM module cycle with `Dock.vue`, and the barrel is a contrivance: it re-exports three glass-ui symbols for exactly one consumer, which is itself a member of the barrel.

defects.defect: One two-way binding is spelled three times: `defineModel("open")`, a redundant explicit `"update:open"` entry in `defineEmits`, and hand-wired `:open` / `@update:open` instead of `v-model:open`.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:24-33 declares `const emit = defineEmits<{ "update:modelValue": [id: string]; "update:open": [open: boolean]; }>();` immediately followed by `const open = defineModel<boolean>("open", { default: false });` — defineModel generates the `update:open` emit itself in Vue 3.4+, so the explicit entry is a duplicate declaration and dead. Then :38-39 hand-wires `:open="open"` and `@update:open="open = $event"`, which is what `v-model:open="open"` means.
defects.mechanism: three spellings of one binding — redundant declaration plus manual re-implementation of a framework idiom
defects.reproduction: sed -n '24,39p' demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue.
defects.proposedCure: Keep `defineModel`, drop the `"update:open"` line from defineEmits, and use `v-model:open="open"` on `<Select>` (idiomatic Vue 3.5, standing edict 7).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue (round 3)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), matching the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: R3-1 — The field's own canonical text is not accepted by its own parser. The moment a colour has an approved custom name, `formattedCurrentColor` returns that NAME (useColorNameResolution.ts:31-46) rather than a CSS string; ColorInput paints it into the contenteditable at five sites (:191, :240, :265, :272, :278) and reads it straight back into `parseAndSetColor` at three (:199, :208, :215). Custom names are demo-side Map entries never registered with `parseCssColor` (only NAMED_COLORS at src/css/grammar.ts:265 exists), so the parse fails. Reproduced end-to-end against the real composables: model `rgb(20 60 200)` → displayed `"babb-blue"` → `parseCssColor(displayed).ok = false` → re-submit → `parseError = true`. The user is shown "not a valid color" for content they never typed — content the application itself authored — and the crown icon is precisely the signal that the field has become unsubmittable.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded negative results, checked and sound, are in Part VII of the report: no PRM-RAF loop — the single rAF at :262 is a one-shot optional-chained focus defer; no WebGL; no ValueUnit accumulation site; no defineModel; stableHue handling in useColorParsing.ts:39-46/:76-83 and useColorPipeline.ts:80-96 is correct; no reka-ui slider; verbatimModuleSyntax passes at :134. Two of my own round-3 hypotheses were tested and WITHDRAWN: `vj-celebrate` IS defined at demo/styles/animations.css:142-165, and `--color-gold` IS inside the @theme block opened at demo/styles/foundation.css:94 so `text-gold` resolves. A third — that R2-1's send-button BLOCKER was a Chromium-only focus artefact — was tested across three engines and REFUTED; see Part IV.)

defects.defect: The custom-name round-trip is broken: `formattedCurrentColor` is a name-or-CSS union, and the component writes it into the contenteditable at five sites and reads it back into `parseAndSetColor` at three. Approved custom names are never registered with the parser, so the app's own canonical display text fails the app's own parser.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:31-46 returns `findCustomName(...)` (an arbitrary user-proposed name) before ever reaching `serializePickerColor`. demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 resolves against a demo-side Map built from GET /colors/approved; `grep -rn registerColorNames src/ demo/ api/src` yields ONE hit, a comment at useCustomColorNames.ts:46. The parser's only name table is the frozen 148-entry NAMED_COLORS (src/css/grammar.ts:31,265; src/css/named-colors.ts:1). Writers: ColorInput.vue:191, :240, :265, :272, :278. Readers: :199, :208, :215. Measured: `model colour: rgb(20 60 200) / formattedCurrentColor: "babb-blue" / parseCssColor(displayed).ok: false / after re-submitting the displayed text -> parseError = true / model colour now: rgb(20 60 200)`.
defects.mechanism: type-confused single value — one computed serves both 'label a human reads' and 'value a machine round-trips', so the DOM node that is the source of truth for submission is seeded with a value from the wrong domain
defects.reproduction: VITE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/api npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts — test B in roundtrip.probe.ts. Drives the real useCustomColorNames + useColorNameResolution + useColorParsing; only globalThis.fetch is stubbed, and the stub name `babb-blue` is legal under the server's own zod schema (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:8-19).
defects.proposedCure: Split the union at the pipeline, not with a guard at the call site. Expose `canonicalCssColor` (always serializePickerColor) alongside `displayLabel`; render the label, seed and submit the canonical. The custom name then becomes what it always should have been — presentation, exactly like the crown tooltip beside it. This also collapses R2-1 and C-16: with one canonical string source there is no reason for six imperative innerText writers or for blur to rewrite a node a pending click is about to read.

defects.defect: An approved name that collides with a CSS keyword silently rewrites the user's colour. ColorInput performs zero validation before proposing, and neither the zod schema nor the uniqueness index checks the 148 CSS keywords.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:236 `await proposeColorName(proposedName.value.trim().toLowerCase(), cssStr)` — the only client guard is `:disabled="!proposedName.trim() || proposing"` at :70 (non-emptiness). api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:8-19 checks shape only (/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/, <=50); api/src/modules/color/service/proposals.ts:38-41 checks uniqueness against other proposals only. Measured with approved name `red` mapped to rgb(0 128 0): `model colour: rgb(0 128 0) / formattedCurrentColor: "red" / after re-submit: rgb(255 0 0) <- was rgb(0 128 0) / parseError: false`.
defects.mechanism: two unreconciled name authorities (NAMED_COLORS in the library, the approved-names Map in the demo) sharing one flat string namespace with no collision check on either side
defects.reproduction: Same harness, test C in roundtrip.probe.ts. Needs no bad actor: a moderator approving `tomato` for a tomato-ish red that is not exactly #FF6347 is doing their job, and the corruption follows automatically.
defects.proposedCure: One line of shared domain truth: reject any proposal whose lowercased name is a key of NAMED_COLORS. Authoritative in the zod schema, mirrored in the component so the user learns before the round-trip rather than after. Route the server half to the API seat.

defects.defect: A 100 ms debounce on the XYZ key leaves the displayed name, the crown (and its tooltip), and `canProposeName` all reporting the PREVIOUS colour after every commit — while the model itself is synchronous.
defects.evidence: useColorNameResolution.ts:25-30 — `const recomputeXYZ = debounce(() => { currentXYZString.value = ... }, 100); watch(() => model.value.color, () => recomputeXYZ(), { immediate: true })`. `currentXYZString` is the sole input to formattedCurrentColor, currentColorMeta and canProposeName. The model is synchronous by design (useColorPipeline.ts:71: 'the ONE ref — synchronous; derivations recompute now'). Measured: `t+0 model: rgb(255 0 0) displayed: "babb-blue" crown: babb-blue canPropose: false <- STALE` / `t+150 model: rgb(255 0 0) displayed: "rgb(255 0 0)" crown: null canPropose: true`.
defects.mechanism: a derived layer desynchronised from its own source by a hidden timer — the same stale-read hazard class as the defineModel round-trip, reached by a debounce instead of an async parent hop
defects.reproduction: Same harness, test D in roundtrip.probe.ts. Live consequences: (1) onInputBlur at ColorInput.vue:191 writes formattedCurrentColor unconditionally, so a blur inside the window paints the previous colour's name — unparseable per R3-1 — and the repair watch at :270 is skipped while focused (:271); (2) the crown tooltip at :30-59 describes the wrong colour; (3) canProposeName gates cycleToolbarMode and the toggle's accessible name at ActionBarLayer.vue:38,45,131.
defects.proposedCure: Make the xyz key a plain computed on model.value.color. It is one matrix conversion, on the same tick the pipeline already recomputes cssColor, cssColorOpaque, HSVCurrentColor and the entire slider-gradient set synchronously. If it ever measures hot, memoise on colour identity — do not desynchronise it. Must be repaired together with R3-9, since the debounce is currently the accidental cap on the linear scan.

defects.defect: The error badge lands on top of the text it is complaining about — the field is text-centred and the badge is centred on the same point, so the user is told their input is invalid and simultaneously prevented from reading it.
defects.evidence: frames/probe-1.json B-f001-light.afterEnter: badgeRect {x:682.1,w:101} spans 682.1->783.1; sendRect {x:763.1,w:24}; overlapPx2 367.5 of sendAreaPx2 576 = 63.8% of the send button. frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles: textAlign center, padding 12px/36px, contentBoxCentreX 714 — inside the badge span. Neither element carries z-index and the badge is later in DOM order (ColorInput.vue:87 vs :67/:76), so paint order is forced. frames/B-f001-error.png read directly: of `oklch()` only the leading `o` survives. Rider from the same capture: badgeStyles {role:null, ariaLive:null, id:""}, inputAria {invalid:null, describedby:null}.
defects.mechanism: an absolutely-positioned feedback chip competing for the same optical centre as the content it annotates, with no stacking or reflow contract between them
defects.reproduction: frames/probe-1.json (controlled capture 2026-07-27 13:30) + frames/B-f001-error.png. Type `oklch()` into the dock colour input and press Enter.
defects.proposedCure: The error is a property of the field, not a floating chip. Move it below the row as a role="status" line wired to aria-describedby, and set aria-invalid on the textbox — which also closes C-5 (WCAG 3.3.1 Level A). The dock row already grows and shrinks (R3-6), so one more line is inside its existing motion budget.

defects.defect: A machine-syntax field with every UA text-assist left at its human-prose default: spellcheck, autocapitalize, autocorrect, inputmode, enterkeyhint and aria-multiline are all unset on a contenteditable whose UA defaults are spellcheck-on / autocapitalize-sentences / autocorrect-on.
defects.evidence: frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.attrs: {"spellcheck":null,"autocapitalize":null,"autocorrect":null,"inputmode":null,"enterkeyhint":null,"ariaMultiline":null,"contenteditable":"","role":"textbox"}. Consequences: the browser red-squiggles oklch/hwb/display-p3 under a field whose only error signal is also red (R3-4); autocorrect smart-dashes the hyphen in `color(display-p3 ...)` and turns a double space into `. ` — neither is recoverable by the lowercasing at useColorParsing.ts:60; Enter is a commit (ColorInput.vue:203-211) but the touch keyboard shows `return`.
defects.mechanism: a code-entry control inheriting prose-entry UA behaviour because none of the opt-out attributes were declared
defects.reproduction: frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.attrs. Mitigating measurement recorded honestly: frames/probe-2.json G-mobile reports the component {"present":false,"missing":true} on the mobile matrix and REPORT.json shows mobile /#/ at 228 elements vs desktop 1738, so the touch-keyboard legs are latent rather than shipping; the desktop spellcheck leg is live today.
defects.proposedCure: contenteditable="plaintext-only" spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" inputmode="text" enterkeyhint="go" aria-multiline="false". The plaintext-only value also closes R2-3 (the rich-paste dock blow-out) in the same attribute, removing the sanitisation question entirely.

defects.defect: The entire dock relayouts on every keystroke: the field declares no intrinsic width bound, so the dock's width tracks the typed string 1:1.
defects.evidence: frames/probe-3.json typingReflow, 13 characters typed one at a time: inputWidths 61.5 -> 198.8, dockWidths 179.5 -> 316.8, inputWidthSpan 137.3, dockWidthSpan 137.3 — identical spans, 11.4px per character. Mechanism read from source: ColorInput.vue:16 `class="color-input w-full block ..."` on a contenteditable inside ColorInput's div.grid.grid-cols-1 (:2), inside ActionBarLayer's div.dock-layer-grid.flex-1 (:98). `w-full` against a shrink-to-fit chain resolves to max-content; the min-w-0 at ActionBarLayer.vue:118 caps the minimum, never the maximum.
defects.mechanism: content-driven intrinsic sizing inside a shrink-to-fit container, so a per-keystroke text change becomes a per-keystroke layout+paint of a backdrop-filter glass surface
defects.reproduction: frames/probe-3.json (controlled capture 2026-07-27 13:30). Attribution stated precisely in the report: the measurement is the D-seat's, the mechanism is read from this component's source — the field is the only element in the chain declaring a content-driven width.
defects.proposedCure: Give the field a fixed inline size in `ch` — its font is already monospace Fira Code (frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles.fontFamily) — and let it scroll internally. The text-ellipsis + mask machinery at :16 and :300-306 already exists to handle overflow and is currently never exercised at rest because the box grows instead. This also fixes the usability half: the send button stops sliding 11.4px right per character.

defects.defect: The resting mask erases the field's right border and both right corner radii, and fades the accent-stroked send arrow into the page ground — a pink glyph on a background dissolving to pink.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:299-302 `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black calc(100% - var(--input-action-width)), transparent 100%)` with --input-action-width: 2.5rem. Resolved live (frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles): `linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0, 0, 0) calc(100% - 40px), rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 100%)` over borderWidth 1px, borderColor rgb(198,180,159); sendStyles.inlineStyle `stroke: oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402)`. A mask applies to the element's whole rendering including border and box-shadow. frames/A-rest-light.png read directly: the white field dissolves into the pink page across its right 40px, the right border and corner radii are gone, the box reads as unclosed, and the pink arrow sits in the middle of the dissolve.
defects.mechanism: a mask intended to fade TEXT applied to the whole border box, taking the border, the radii and the sibling glyph's contrast with it
defects.reproduction: frames/A-rest-light.png + frames/probe-1.json A-rest-light.styles. .color-input:focus clears the mask (:303-306) and frames/C-overflow-dark.png confirms the focused box is whole — so the defect is exclusively in the resting state, which is the state the entire visual census captured.
defects.proposedCure: Scope the fade to the text, not the box: a ::after gradient overlay inside the padding box leaves border, radii and the sibling button untouched. Or drop it — R3-6's fix makes the field a fixed-width scroller where the ellipsis alone carries the same signal. Note round 2 assessed this block as 'careful and right'; the overflow containment is right, its resting collateral is not.

defects.defect: Whether the user's first invalid input reports at all depends on how the page booted — and the dominant boot path is the silent one. `initialParse` survives boot to eat the user's first real error.
defects.evidence: useColorParsing.ts:50,86,88 — initialParse starts true and suppresses the first failure's flash. The only consumer is restoreFromStorage -> parseAndSetColor(storedInput) at useColorPersistence.ts:73, gated twice: demo/color-picker/App.vue:378 `if (!appliedFromUrl && hydration.source !== "url") restoreFromStorage();` and useColorPersistence.ts:68 `if (!hadPersistedColor) return false;`. hydrate.ts:100-127 builds the model directly and never calls parseAndSetColor. So URL-colour boot -> silent; first-ever visit -> silent; returning visit without a URL colour -> flashes. The app writes the colour into its own URL: every observed load landed on `.../#/?color=%23abcdef` or `.../#/?space=lab&color=...` (REPORT.json /#/ probe.url, all four matrices).
defects.mechanism: a boot-scoped suppression latch on app-lifetime state, whose consumption depends on persistence and URL state invisible to the user
defects.reproduction: Code path traced end to end (App.vue:378 -> useColorPersistence.ts:68,73 -> useColorParsing.ts:50,86,88) plus REPORT.json probe.url across all four matrices. Sharpens round-1 C-6 from 'the first invalid input produces no error' to 'whether an error appears at all is a function of state the user cannot see' — two bug reports saying 'nothing happened' and 'it flashed red' can be the same build.
defects.proposedCure: Delete initialParse. Its job — don't flash red at a user who has not typed yet — is already done correctly by the callers: the boot paths that seed the model no longer go through parseAndSetColor at all (hydrate.ts), and the one that does (restoreFromStorage) is restoring a value the user themselves last committed. A latch that survives boot to eat a real error is a masking fallback (edict 2).

defects.defect: `findCustomName` is an O(n) linear scan of a Map keyed the wrong way round, called by three hot computeds and once per palette swatch.
defects.evidence: useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 walks normalizedCustomNames (name -> xyz) comparing values. Callers: formattedCurrentColor, currentColorMeta, canProposeName (three scans per invalidation) and savedColorLabel at useColorNameResolution.ts:48-53 (once per saved swatch). getApprovedColorNames accepts limit up to 500 (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:27) and the demo passes none (color-names.ts:23-31), so the registry is server-sized. Verified live: findCustomName(xyz) = "babb-blue".
defects.mechanism: an inverse lookup performed by linear search because the inverse index was never built alongside the forward one
defects.reproduction: Same harness, test E in roundtrip.probe.ts. Not currently hot only because R3-3's 100 ms debounce caps invalidations at ~10/s — fixing R3-3 as prescribed removes that accidental cap, so the two must be repaired together.
defects.proposedCure: Build the inverse index (xyz -> name) inside the same loop that builds normalizedCustomNames at useCustomColorNames.ts:20-33. One extra Map.set, O(1) lookups, and the collision case of R3-2 becomes visible at registry-build time — which is where it wants to be caught.

defects.defect: MT-F001 is SWALLOWED by this path and mislabelled as a user typo. A shipped-library TypeError is rendered byte-identically to a plain typo, reaches no telemetry, and leaves the field in a final state indistinguishable from working.
defects.evidence: Library leg re-measured against src/css/index: `"oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`. Site: src/css/grammar.ts:178 guards `slash[1]?.trim()` with optional chaining while :180 asserts `slash[0]!.replace(...)` — the two adjacent indices of the same array handled with opposite rigour, one line apart. Path: ColorInput.vue:194 -> :199 -> useColorParsing.ts:60 -> :64 -> picker-color.ts:110 -> parseCssColor. Live (frames/probe-1.json B-f001-light): afterEnter badgeText 'not a valid color', inputBorder rgb(219,36,36), and pageErrors: []. Swallow site: useColorParsing.ts:84-87, a bare `catch` with no binding and no discrimination, so PickerColorError (which carries result.diagnostics per picker-color.ts:96-112) and a library TypeError render identically.
defects.mechanism: an undiscriminated catch converting a defect in a dependency into an accusation of user error, with a latch that then erases even that signal
defects.reproduction: Test A in roundtrip.probe.ts for the library leg; frames/probe-1.json + frames/B-f001-error.png + frames/B-f001-after2s.png for the live leg. The tail nobody had recorded: after2s = {badge:false, text:'oklch()', border:'lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)'} — the invalid text remains, the error styling is gone, and previousInvalid is now latched to 'oklch()' so useColorParsing.ts:61 short-circuits and pressing Enter again produces nothing at all.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow the catch: `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof PickerColorError)) throw e; ... }`. A genuine syntax rejection stays a quiet inline error; anything else reaches window.onerror, where MT-F001 would have surfaced on day one. ParseEchoReadout (ColorInput.vue:109) — already rendering astEcho and gamutVerdict from the same pipeline — is the natural home for the diagnostics the catch discards. The library-side `!` at src/css/grammar.ts:180 is a separate repair; route to the library seat, together with R2-7's adjacent false-accept of `oklch(0.5 0.1 250 / )`.

defects.defect: CARRIED AND STRENGTHENED — the send button is structurally incapable of submitting typed text, in every browser engine. I attempted to refute this as a Chromium-only focus artefact and the refutation FAILED.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:183-193 onInputBlur overwrites the field with formattedCurrentColor; :213-217 onSubmitColor reads that same node back. Cross-engine test of the exact three-part shape: chromium 148.0.7778.96 / webkit 26.4 / firefox 150.0.2 all produced `typed activeEl=ce` -> `mousedown activeEl=ce` -> `BLUR read="typed-value" -> overwrite` -> `CLICK read="CANONICAL"`. WebKit and Firefox indeed do not focus the button on mousedown, but they blur the contenteditable anyway — the distinction the refutation relied on does not exist for this shape.
defects.mechanism: DOM node as source of truth, mutated by an event that the UA guarantees fires before the event that reads it
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/blurorder.html + blurorder.mjs (session scratchpad; a 12-line static page, no app dependency). `node scratchpad/blurorder.mjs`. Round 2's live app measurement stands as the in-situ leg.
defects.proposedCure: Same cure as R3-1 and C-16, one stroke: hold the draft in a local shallowRef written by @input, render from it, and let blur decide only whether to DISCARD the draft — never to rewrite a DOM node a pending click is about to read. onSubmitColor then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering becomes irrelevant. This is the synchronous-local-cache idiom edict 7 already mandates for the defineModel round-trip; the hazard class is identical.

defects.defect: CARRIED — the pending 2000 ms parse is never cancelled, and the component has no teardown of any kind. An abandoned edit overwrites a later, deliberate commit, and can fire from a destroyed component.
defects.evidence: `grep -n "onUnmounted\|onBeforeUnmount\|clearTimeout\|cancel()" demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` returns NO OUTPUT WHATSOEVER — no lifecycle hook, no timer clear, no debounce cancel, despite the file owning a setTimeout at :256, an rAF at :262 and a 2000 ms debounce via :199. debounce exposes .cancel() (demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41) and the sibling consumer uses it (demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383), so the omission is demonstrated, not stylistic. The unmount leg is real: Dock.vue:153 `<DockLayer v-if="hasAnyActionBar">` and :156 `<ActionBarLayer v-if="actionBar" ...>`.
defects.mechanism: broken ownership of pending-commit state — an app-wide singleton debounce (useColorParsing.ts:92 inside the injected pipeline) whose only cancel is owned by a different component's lifetime
defects.reproduction: Round 2's vite-node reproduction stands (C1 committed #abcdef -> C2 committed #00ff00 -> C3 2.3s later the abandoned 'red' won). Round 3 independently confirms both structural preconditions by grep.
defects.proposedCure: One owner for 'there is a pending commit'. Fold the debounce into the draft shallowRef of R2-1/R3-1 so the pending state is visible reactive state rather than a hidden timer, and give it the component's lifetime.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue — round 3
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: R3-01 — the field cannot be edited, only replaced. `onInputFocus` calls `selectAll()` unconditionally (ColorInput.vue:168-182), so a single click anywhere in the value selects the whole value and the next keystroke annihilates it (measured: `wholeValueSelected: true` → type `x` → field content `"x"`), with no undo (`undoRestoredTypedText: false`). The component's own help copy promises "Any valid CSS color string is accepted"; CSS colour strings are 20-30 characters of punctuated grammar that are typed wrong on the first attempt, and this field's only supported operation is destroy-and-retype. Unreported by rounds 1 and 2; not fixable by styling.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but these sub-claims were tested and proved SOUND, so the register is honest: (1) the field IS in the sequential tab order — Shift+Tab from the send button lands on it (`"isColorInput": true`), despite `element.tabIndex` reporting -1, which invited the opposite claim; no keyboard trap. (2) MT-F001 does not crash the app — typing `oklch()` + Enter yields `pageErrors: []`; the only console error on the route is an unrelated dev VITE_API_URL notice. (3) Owner edict 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5) is MET — `useTemplateRef` at :159, reactive props destructure at :138. (4) Owner edict 8 (`verbatimModuleSyntax`) is MET — `import type { EditTarget }` at :134 is the only type-only import and is correct. (5) `input-mode-flash` is a correctly scoped keyframe compiling to `input-mode-flash-55dadc03` — which is why `crown-appear` failing is a defect, not a framework limitation. (6) The error badge's own text contrast passes AA at its rendered size. (7) The U9 blur snap-back does exactly what its comment says.

defects.defect: The field cannot be edited, only replaced: clicking anywhere in the value selects the entire value, so the next keystroke destroys it. No undo.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:168-182 (`selectAll()` on `focus`). Measured, frames/r3probe.json: `"caretAfterClick": {"selectionText":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)","isCollapsed":false,"wholeValueSelected":true}` then `"caretAfterKeystroke":{"text":"x"}`; `"undo":{"undoRestoredTypedText":false}`.
defects.mechanism: Unconditional select-all bound to the focus event of a text-entry surface; the `selection?.toString() === target.innerText` guard at :174 only suppresses re-selection of the state it just created.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 -> click `Tools` -> click `Open color input` -> click at the horizontal midpoint of the displayed value -> press any key. The 24-character value is replaced by that one character. Ctrl/Cmd+Z does not restore it.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `selectAll()` from `onInputFocus`. Select-all belongs to explicit entry (the toggle's own activation, or Ctrl/Cmd+A) only. Architecturally: replace the contenteditable with glass-ui 7.0.0's published `Input`, whose native caret placement makes the whole mechanism unnecessary.

defects.defect: No cancel path exists, and a 2000 ms commit debounce means valid input typed and blurred inside two seconds is silently discarded with zero signal.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; ColorInput.vue:202-211 handles only `Enter`; :183-193 blur repaints from the model. Measured, frames/r3probe2.json: `"cancel":{"typed":"rebeccapurple","afterEsc":{"text":"rebeccapurple","focused":true},"afterBlur":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)","escapeCancels":false,"blurCommitted":false}`.
defects.mechanism: Two sources of truth (contenteditable text vs. model) reconciled only by a long debounce and an unconditional blur repaint, with no cancel gesture and no uncommitted-state affordance.
defects.reproduction: Open the field -> select all -> type `rebeccapurple` (valid CSS) -> press Escape (nothing happens) -> click elsewhere within 2 s. The value reverts to the previous colour with no error, no toast, no 'unsaved' mark.
defects.proposedCure: Escape restores the model value and exits; blur either commits or warns but never silently discards; drop the debounce to a live-preview cadence (~150 ms) once the field is no longer the sole commit path. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:75 already mandates commit/cancel/error semantics for editors — adopt the W21 numeric-field contract instead of inventing a third one.

defects.defect: The field's boundary fails the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast floor in both schemes, and that same boundary is the only mark identifying the element as an input and the only focus register.
defects.evidence: Measured, frames/r3probe2.json: light border `rgb(198,180,159)` on plate `rgb(251,250,248)` = **1.930:1**; dark border `rgb(101,87,73)` on plate `rgb(11,10,9)` = **2.838:1** (WCAG relative-luminance formula computed in-probe). Ink-on-plate is 16.77:1 — an 8.7x mismatch between the two halves of the same object. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 'boundaries meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.'
defects.mechanism: A decorative `--input` hairline carrying three structural jobs (affordance identity, focus register, error register) with no visible label, no placeholder in colour mode, and no glass affordance to fall back on.
defects.reproduction: Open the field at 1440x900 in light, then in dark; read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.color-input')).borderTopColor` and `.backgroundColor` and compute WCAG contrast. Both arms are below 3:1.
defects.proposedCure: Consume glass-ui's `Input` so the boundary comes from the producer at its audited contrast, and stop overloading it: focus gets the producer focus ring, invalid gets `aria-invalid` plus a real message region — three separate registers instead of one 1.93:1 hairline.

defects.defect: The component's own `mask-image` erases the focus indicator on the inline-end edge (17.0% of the border perimeter under the alpha ramp, the entire right edge at alpha 0) and reaches 3 px past the padding into the glyph run.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:294,300-301. Measured, frames/r3probe.json -> maskGeometry: rect 324.72x45.91, `paddingRight: 36`, `contentRightX: 851.36`, `maskFadeStartX: 848.36`, `maskEatsIntoContentPx: 3`, `inkFadedPx: 3`. Perimeter 2*(324.72+45.91)=741.26 px; masked band = right edge 45.91 + 40 top + 40 bottom = 125.91 px = 16.99%. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:178 'The dock is its own top band ... clipped by neither mask nor card.'
defects.mechanism: An element-wide CSS mask used to fake a text fade; a mask clips the whole element, so border and corner go with the ink — and `border-color` is the only focus indicator (:162-166, with `focus-visible:outline-none` at :16).
defects.reproduction: Open the field and focus it; the right border and corner are absent in the render (frames/r3-focus.png). In DevTools read the computed `mask-image` and compare `100% - 40px` against the content-box right edge at `borderBox.right - 1 - 36`.
defects.proposedCure: Move the commit button out of the text box entirely and delete the mask, `pr-9`, `--input-action-width`, `text-center`, `text-ellipsis` and `whitespace-nowrap` with it. This also retires the three mutually inconsistent numbers that currently describe one action gutter (36 px padding / 40 px mask / 28 px button seat).

defects.defect: Assistive technology is told the control is a multi-line rich-text editor, and it exposes no invalid state even while the error badge is on screen.
defects.evidence: Measured via CDP `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, frames/r3probe2.json -> ax: `{"role":"textbox","name":"Enter a CSS color","value":"color(display-p3 0.5 0.2 0.9)","props":["focusable=true","editable=\"richtext\"","settable=true","multiline=true","readonly=false","required=false"]}`. No `invalid` property present. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 'Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.'
defects.mechanism: `contenteditable="true"` (not `plaintext-only`) under `role="textbox"` with no `aria-multiline` — the computed AX role resolves to multiline richtext, while the component hard-prevents Enter at :203-204. Announced affordance and real affordance disagree.
defects.reproduction: Open the field, attach a CDP session, `Accessibility.enable` then `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, filter for name 'Enter a CSS color'. Read `editable` and `multiline`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the contenteditable and consume glass-ui's `Input` — a native single-line `<input type="text">` resolves to a correct textbox role, cannot hold markup, and is the element `useUserInvalidAria` (glass-ui's own `:user-invalid` -> `aria-invalid` bridge) binds to.

defects.defect: Spellcheck is enabled on the field, so every CSS colour token carries UA red wavy underlines — in the same red the component uses for its own error state.
defects.evidence: Measured, frames/r3probe.json -> maskGeometry: `"spellcheckIDL": true, "spellcheckAttr": null, "contentEditable": "true", "autocapitalize": null`. The component's only error signal is `--destructive` (border at :163, badge at :348-366).
defects.mechanism: `contenteditable` inherits spellcheck=true; nothing in the component opts out. An unowned, unstylable red-for-wrong system paints over correct input, competing with the owned red for the same meaning.
defects.reproduction: Open the field and focus it; the tokens `oklch`, `lab`, `display-p3`, `rebeccapurple` are all non-dictionary words and receive red squiggles. Confirm with `document.querySelector('.color-input').spellcheck === true`.
defects.proposedCure: `spellcheck="false"` (plus `autocorrect="off"`, `autocapitalize="off"`, `enterkeyhint="go"`) on a real `<input>` — all of which are declared props on glass-ui's published `InputProps`, and none of which a contenteditable span accepts meaningfully.

defects.defect: Opening the field with its own toggle fires the hover popover as a side effect, and the popover occludes the route's own content.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:3-10 `<Popover trigger="hover" :open-delay="300"><PopoverTrigger as-child>` wraps the whole field. Measured deterministically (probe parks the pointer on the toggle, clicks, never moves the mouse again), frames/r3probe4.json: `{"parkedPointerAt":{"x":851,"y":40.55},"before":{"popoverOpen":false},"after":{"fieldRect":{"x":563.6,"right":888.4},"popoverOpen":true},"pointerInsideFieldAfter":true,"popoverOpenedWithoutMovingPointer":true}`. frames/r3-dark-focus.png shows the panel covering the About card's H1.
defects.mechanism: A hover-triggered disclosure attached to a control that expands under the stationary pointer that just opened it (R3-08 is the motive force). Overlay state becomes a consequence of layout rather than of a user command — against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:115.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 -> click `Tools` -> click `Open color input` and do not move the mouse -> wait 1.6 s. The help panel is open over the route content.
defects.proposedCure: The Parse-Lab echo and the help prose are real information and must not live behind hover: move `<ParseEchoReadout />` into the Picker inspector as a persistent region (reachable by keyboard at every viewport), and if any tooltip survives, bind it to a named control with a click/focus path, not to the field's own bounding box.

defects.defect: Typing translates the dock's sibling controls +/-166 px: the commit arrow recedes from the pointer as the user types toward it.
defects.evidence: Measured per keystroke, frames/r3probe2.json -> dockShift, entering `color(display-p3 0.5 0.2 0.9)`: field width 50.0 -> 382.0 px; send button x 723.0 -> 889.0 (`sendButtonTravel: +166.0`); mode toggle x 764.0 -> 930.0 (`toggleTravel: +166.0`); Back x 636.0 -> 470.0 (`backTravel: -166.0`). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 'The top dock owns a reserved band ... do not move the scene below it'; :78 'reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis'.
defects.mechanism: A content-sized, unreserved text field inside a centre-anchored band, so every `input` event resizes the field and pushes both halves of the dock outward synchronously.
defects.reproduction: Open the field, select all, Backspace, then type one character at a time while sampling `document.querySelector('.send-btn').getBoundingClientRect().x` and the toggle's and Back's rects. 166 px of travel each, in opposite directions.
defects.proposedCure: Give the field `inline-size` reserved to its widest legal serialization (`color(display-p3 ...)`) plus `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so the band stops moving. The deeper cure is to stop hosting a variable-width text editor in the constitution's reserved band at all — move the editor to the Picker inspector and leave a fixed-width named `DockControl` in the dock.

defects.defect: The plate has no tier in the material hierarchy: opaque, 4 px-cornered, 74% of the dock band's height, inside a `border-radius: 9999px` pill — and in dark it is the darkest object on the page.
defects.evidence: Measured: field background light `rgb(251,250,248)`, dark `rgb(11,10,9)`, both fully opaque; field `border-radius: 4px`; host `.glass-dock horizontal shape-pill layout-line` `border-radius: 9999px` at 62 px height (rendered 31 px) — ratio 7.75:1 with every intervening ancestor at `0px` (frames/r3probe3.json chain, frames/r3probe4.json pill). Field height 45.91 / band 62 = 74.0%. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:11-19 material table + 'One surface has one tier'; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:66.
defects.mechanism: A shadcn form surface (`bg-background border rounded-input`) transplanted whole into a glass instrument, inventing an unlabelled extra material tier and a second radius language inside the structural-glass band.
defects.reproduction: Open the field in dark at 1440x900 (frames/r3-dark-focus.png): a near-black opaque rectangle in a warm translucent glass dock, on a page where every other surface is tinted translucent glass. Read `backgroundColor` and `borderTopLeftRadius` on `.color-input` and on the `.glass-dock` ancestor.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the producer's field surface so the plate inherits a real tier (Instrument veil or Specimen well per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:15-16) and the producer's radius rung, rather than improvising `bg-background` + `rounded-input` inside Structural glass.

defects.defect: The failure badge hides 89.9% of the value it is judging and the entire commit button, and carries no programmatic semantics.
defects.evidence: Measured after typing `oklch()` + Enter, frames/r3probe.json -> f001: `badgeRect {x:682.1,w:101}`, `inkRect {x:673.9,w:80.1}`, `badgeCoversInkPx: 72` (= 89.9% of the ink); `sendRect {x:763.1,w:24,h:24}`, `badgeOverSendPx2: 367.5` of `sendAreaPx2: 576` (= 63.8%), and photographically the arrow is 100% invisible (frames/r3-f001.png). `ariaInvalid: null`, `ariaDescribedby: null`, `badgeRole: null`, `badgeAriaLive: null`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 a transient flourish 'never carries the only truth'.
defects.mechanism: Two absolutely-positioned siblings (`.send-btn` at right:0.25rem, `.error-badge` at right:0.5rem, ColorInput.vue:335-366) competing for one 24 px gutter, with the badge later in DOM order so it paints on top; plus `useColorParsing.ts:57` clearing it on a 2 s timer and :62 short-circuiting the repeat so a second Enter is answered with silence.
defects.reproduction: Open the field -> select all -> type `oklch(` then `)` -> Enter. The dock reads `<- | o[not a valid color] | tag`; press Enter again on the same string and nothing at all happens, ever.
defects.proposedCure: The parse verdict becomes a persistent control state on the field (`aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` -> one message region in flow beside the dock, never over the value), cleared on correction rather than on a timer; drop the `input === previousInvalid` short-circuit ahead of the error path so retries are answered. glass-ui already ships `useUserInvalidAria` for exactly this.

defects.defect: The commit button wears the Chromium UA default focus ring — the only control in the dock band that does — instead of the house register.
defects.evidence: Measured, frames/r3probe2.json -> sendFocus: `.send-btn` programmatic AND keyboard both `{"outlineStyle":"auto","outlineColor":"rgb(0, 95, 204)","matchesFocusVisible":true}`; the dock sibling `DockControl` at keyboard focus is `{"outlineStyle":"none"}`. This CORRECTS round-2 D-02's claim of 'No focus indicator ... WCAG 2.4.7 fails outright'.
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled `<button class="send-btn btn-interactive">` where `btn-interactive` matches zero CSS rules (independently re-measured: `btnInteractiveRules: 0`), so the only focus expression left is the UA default — #005FCC, the one colour guaranteed not to belong to the user's palette, inside a dock tinted by the active colour.
defects.reproduction: Open the field, focus it, press Tab. `getComputedStyle(document.activeElement).outlineColor` is `rgb(0, 95, 204)`; do the same on any `DockControl` sibling and it is `none`.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the hand-rolled button for glass-ui's `./button` or `DockControl` — the same primitive every sibling in this dock already uses — which brings the house focus register, hover/press magnitudes, a disabled treatment and an accessible name in one substitution.

defects.defect: The demo's global reduced-motion transition guard is inert app-wide; the producer's rule wins, so this component's PRM behaviour is accidental rather than designed.
defects.evidence: Measured under `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, frames/r3probe3.json: `transitionDuration: "0.1s"`, `animationDuration: "1e-05s"`, with matching rules `{sel: ":not([data-allow-motion])", media: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", td: "0.1s", imp: "important"}` (glass-ui, specificity 0,1,0) and `{sel: "*, ::before, ::after", td: "0.01ms", imp: "important"}` (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193, specificity 0,0,0). The producer rule wins. This CORRECTS round-2 section 5, which credited compliance to the demo guard.
defects.mechanism: A `*`-selector `!important` guard in consumer CSS outranked by a producer `!important` rule at higher specificity — so the consumer's declared PRM policy for transitions has no effect anywhere in the app.
defects.reproduction: Launch with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, open the field, read `getComputedStyle(el).transitionDuration` — 0.1 s, not the 0.01 ms the demo guard declares. Animations still resolve to 1e-05s, so the guard is live for `animation-duration` only.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the consumer's blanket transition arm and defer to the producer's PRM register, or raise the guard's specificity deliberately — but do not ship a rule the codebase believes is authoritative and is not. (Outcome here is benign: a 100 ms colour transition is appropriate under reduced motion.)

defects.defect: The component root is contrivance: three of the five utilities on it can never apply.
defects.evidence: ColorInput.vue:2 `<div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0">`. Measured, frames/r3probe3.json -> chain: the element has exactly one child (`DIV.relative w-full flex items-center`), both 324.7 px wide. A single-child single-column grid can never apply `gap-y-2`; `p-0 m-0` reset properties already at zero.
defects.mechanism: Layout utilities applied speculatively rather than to a measured need. Owner edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance).
defects.reproduction: Inspect `.grid.grid-cols-1.gap-y-2` in the live DOM: `children.length === 1`; removing `gap-y-2 p-0 m-0` produces a pixel-identical render.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the wrapper entirely — the component's single root is the `relative flex` div, which is also where the parent's `class="min-w-0"` and the dock's `dock-layer is-active` need to land by fallthrough.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED (round-2 D-01): the component does not exist below 1024 px landscape, including at 200% browser zoom — so the app's only free-text colour entry is absent on every phone and at the WCAG reflow arm.
defects.evidence: Read as images this round: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/zoom-200-desktop/picker.png renders the dock as `home-chevron | Picker About | ellipsis` with NO Tools control (capture method: 720x450 @2x DPR, per visual/states.mjs:21-22); docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows the resting desktop dock as `Home | Tools | Login | @mbabb` with no field. Source chain: App.vue:310-312 breakpoint -> :323-328 `onDesktopLeftMount` is the sole writer of `colorPickerRef` -> Dock.vue:41,153 -> ActionBarLayer.vue:115.
defects.mechanism: The action-bar context is a side effect of which pane slot the media query happened to mount, rather than route-table state.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/ at 390x844 or at 720x450 and press every dock control — there is no colour input. At 1440x900 -> Tools -> Open color input, it appears.
defects.proposedCure: Lift the action-bar context to the route table (`usePaneRouter`) so it is breakpoint-independent. Per the R3 gestalt cure, the editor itself belongs in the Picker inspector at all widths, with a named DockControl as its dock-side opener.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED (round-2 D-02/D-09): `btn-interactive` matches zero CSS rules, and the Crown reveal animation names a keyframe the scoped compiler renamed away — two animations the file's comments claim were 'retired onto' or tokenized are simply inert.
defects.evidence: Independently re-measured this round by walking every stylesheet in the live document, frames/r3probe.json -> styleFacts: `"btnInteractiveRules": 0`; the only matching rules are `.send-btn[data-v-55dadc03]` and `.send-btn[data-v-55dadc03]:disabled`; `transition` computes to `all` (Tailwind preflight). Live keyframe inventory: `["input-mode-flash-55dadc03", "crown-appear-55dadc03"]` — there is no unsuffixed `crown-appear`, yet ColorInput.vue:37-39 sets it via an inline `style` attribute that PostCSS never sees.
defects.mechanism: (a) A local hover/press recipe deleted with a comment crediting a producer atom that does not exist (ColorInput.vue:61-66, 327-334). (b) An inline template `style` naming a `<style scoped>` keyframe, which @vue/compiler-sfc rewrites only inside the same PostCSS root. Owner edict 6: animations are never deleted, only moved or tokenized.
defects.reproduction: In the live document, walk `document.styleSheets` counting selectors containing `btn-interactive` (0), and collect CSSKeyframesRule names matching /crown/ (only `crown-appear-55dadc03`). Hover, press and Tab to the arrow: nothing changes at any step beyond the UA outline.
defects.proposedCure: Either land the atom in glass-ui and consume it, or — the KISS answer — retire the hand-rolled button for glass-ui's `./button`/`DockControl`. For the Crown, move the `animation` declaration into the scoped `<style>` block (or bind a class) so the compiler rewrites it; the `:key="crownKey"` remount machinery in useColorNameResolution.ts:64 currently exists to restart an animation that cannot start.

defects.defect: CONFIRMED (round-2 D-23): MT-F001 is swallowed by an undiscriminating bare catch, so a shipping parser TypeError is permanently indistinguishable from a user typo.
defects.evidence: Measured live: typing `oklch(` `)` + Enter yields `"f001PageErrors": []` and the badge text 'not a valid color'; the only console error on the route is the unrelated dev VITE_API_URL misconfiguration notice. Source: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(...))` — the non-null assertion is false for an empty function body; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:84 catches it with a bare `catch {}` and calls `flashParseError()`. Owner edict 2 forbids masking fallbacks.
defects.mechanism: One untyped catch renders 'the grammar rejected your string', 'the parser threw a TypeError' and any future RangeError as the same sentence, so the application can never surface, count or report MT-F001.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ -> Tools -> Open color input -> select all -> type `oklch(` then `)` -> Enter. The user sees a red slab covering 89.9% of their text and the whole retry arrow; no crash, no console error, no distinguishable signal.
defects.proposedCure: Discriminate at the boundary: the parse boundary returns a typed result (`{ok:true,value} | {ok:false,reason:'grammar'|'internal'}`) rather than throwing; 'internal' is reported (and countable) rather than rendered as 'not a valid color'. Fixing grammar.ts:181 is necessary but not sufficient — the swallow is the design defect.

defects.defect: Malformed-URL boot path: the tab title asserts a colour the app is not showing, the bad link never heals, and MT-F001's only observable trace in the entire app is emitted at a severity the mega-tranche audit collects but does not grade.
defects.evidence: Live at http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch&color=rgb() settled 2500ms: {"title":"rgb() — Color Picker","colorInputText":"oklch(72% 0.19 25deg)","url":"…?space=oklch&color=rgb()"}. Source demo/color-picker/router/useDocumentTitle.ts:62 `document.title = composeTitle(to.name, to.query.color)` and :43-45 takes the raw query verbatim — no validation, and the afterEach guard fires independently of whether useColorUrl.applyUrlToModel() succeeded. Console (level=warning): `[useColorUrl] Invalid color in URL: rgb() TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') at ae (…/dist/subpaths/css.js:265:17) at parsePickerColor (…/picker-color.ts:157:17) at applyUrlToModel (…/useColorUrl.ts:22:41)`. Graded categories: `grep -n "^### " docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md` → 8 sections (blankOrNearBlank, pageErrors, consoleErrors, horizontalOverflow, darkClassMissing, mainCountNotOne, smallTapTargets, namelessButtons) — consoleWarnings has none.
defects.mechanism: Mechanism A (failure-explicit contract inverted) with a split-brain consequence: two consumers read the same query parameter; useColorUrl validates it and correctly reports failure, useDocumentTitle does not and renders it as fact. useDocumentTitle.ts:18-19 states the broken assumption verbatim ('the exact string the app uses as the colour's shareable identity everywhere').
defects.reproduction: Navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch&color=rgb() ; wait 2.5s; read document.title, the .color-input textContent, and location.href. Title says rgb(), body shows oklch(72% 0.19 25deg), URL unchanged (useColorUrl.ts:52-64 fires only on model change, and the model never moved).
defects.proposedCure: composeTitle must read the MODEL's cssSpelling, not the query — only the model has been through the parser. Separately, applyUrlToModel returning false should REPAIR the URL with one router.replace so a broken share link heals on open rather than propagating. Promote useColorUrl.ts:44 to console.error only AFTER Mechanism A is cured (while the swallow exists, promoting it would turn a real signal into noise on every typo).

defects.defect: `serializePickerColor` answers a different question rather than failing: it suppresses the library's `{ok:false, color_invalid_input}` for the four non-CSS spaces and silently substitutes oklch — and ColorInput.vue:104 renders that substitution two lines beneath the sentence "Any valid CSS color string is accepted."
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:206-211 `const cssColor = CSS_PICKER_SPACES.has(color.space) ? color as CssColor : convertPickerColor(color, "oklch")`. Measured against the published bundle: `serializeCssColor(hsv(25,0.8,0.95,1))` → {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"color_invalid_input"}} while the demo substitute yields "oklch(71.818014636356% 0.164583951889 51.616475581492deg)"; kelvin(3200) → "oklch(83.541309110086% …)". All 17 spaces incl. the 4 non-CSS ones are user-selectable (color-model.ts:75-78 DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES = {...PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, hex}). The sibling consumer GUARDS the identical call: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:161 `if (CSS_PICKER_SPACES.has(converted.space)) return serializePickerColor(converted);` else renders `hsv · 25 · 0.8 · 0.95`.
defects.mechanism: New face of Mechanism A, named A′: failure answered with a plausible wrong answer rather than an error. A throw is at least loud somewhere; a substitution returns a well-formed string that passes every downstream check. This is the masking fallback edict 2 forbids, sitting at the bottom of the funnel every colour readout in the app runs through.
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module against ./dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js: build hsv(25,0.8,0.95,1), call serializeCssColor → {ok:false,color_invalid_input}; then convertColor(...,'oklch') + serializeCssColor → the oklch string the demo returns instead. In-app: select HSV/Kelvin/ICtCp/Jzazbz in the space selector and hover ColorInput — the popover prints an oklch string under the CSS-fidelity promise, while the selector's own specimen row for the same colour prints the honest non-CSS spelling.
defects.proposedCure: serializePickerColor returns Result<string, ColorIssue> and never converts. Callers wanting the oklch projection request it by name (serializeAsOklch), so substitution becomes a request instead of a silent default. ColorInput.vue:104 then renders either the CSS spelling or the honest non-CSS spelling ColorSpaceSelector already implements — one helper, one home, both call sites. Falls out of the standing transposition-1 cure at zero extra cost and retires the third home for the CSS-serializable-space set (pass 3's L-14).

defects.mechanism: Mechanism G (new): a domain write owned by a leaf has no testable seam — there is nothing to call except by mounting a dock leaf inside a dock inside an app. Both stated reasons for the e2e skip are themselves filed defects (the button has no accessible name — L-10/L-23; the crossfade race — L-11).

defects.proposedCure: Move the mutation to `color-session/useColorNaming.ts` as `proposeName(name, css): Promise<Result<ProposedColorName, ApiProblem>>` (merging useCustomColorNames + useColorNameResolution + this write). Give the send button an accessible name so the e2e can actually drive submit.

defects.defect: The JS half of the timing contract has no home: 21+ bare timing literals under demo/, two unnamed 2000s in one file, and ColorInput's own mode-flash JS timer clears the class 150ms before the CSS animation it gates finishes.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:57 `setTimeout(…, 2000)` (badge lifetime) and :92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)` (typing debounce) — two independent unnamed 2000s in one file; useColorPipeline.ts:209 uses 500 for the slider commit, useColorUrl.ts:64 uses 300 for model→URL. defects.mechanism: Mechanism H (generalizes pass 1's L-11 SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS=260): glass-ui owns the design-token half of timing (--duration-fast/slow/panel) and the demo consumes it correctly in CSS, but the JavaScript half has no home at all, so every site that must coordinate with a CSS duration copies a number and hopes. No compiler, lint rule or test links the two.

The pure-behaviour debounces (parse/URL/slider) are a genuinely demo-owned concern and belong in one named table with a rationale per row. Relay to glass-ui: export the duration tokens as a JS map from @mkbabb/glass-ui/tokens so consumers skip the getComputedStyle read.

defects.defect: MAJOR, re-derived at runtime: the Crown entrance animation is dead — a scoped @keyframes referenced from an inline style attribute, which the SFC compiler never rewrites.
defects.evidence: Live keyframe census of the running document: {"keyframeNames":["input-mode-flash-55dadc03","crown-appear-55dadc03"]} — no unhashed crown-appear exists anywhere. Synthesising ColorInput's exact element (data-v-55dadc03 + its exact inline shorthand) against the live page: asAuthored {"name":"crown-appear","dur":"0.55s","running":0} vs control hashedName {"name":"crown-appear-55dadc03","dur":"0.55s","running":1}. Tokens resolve correctly ({durationPanel:0.55s, easeDecelerate:cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1)}), so this is a name miss, not a token miss. ColorInput.vue:37-39 is the inline style; :369-376 is the scoped @keyframes. The working control is .color-input-mode-flash (:312-314), which references its keyframe from INSIDE the scoped block.
defects.mechanism: Vue's scoped-style compiler hash-suffixes @keyframes names and rewrites animation declarations within the same style block, but never processes template style attributes. Pairing a scoped keyframe with an inline reference is unsatisfiable by construction. Edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction, not decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).
defects.reproduction: On the live app, evaluate: create a span with data-v-55dadc03 and style='animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards', read getAnimations().length → 0; repeat with crown-appear-55dadc03 → 1.
defects.proposedCure: Promote crown-appear to demo/styles/animations.css (the declared home, already holding edit-drawer-in / stagger-child-in / vj-settle) and drive it from a .crown-badge class; the inline style attribute dies with it. Better still, relay it to glass-ui alongside the vj-celebrate / vj-morph families this component already consumes. Standing rule the codebase should adopt: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. No third combination is legal.

defects.defect: The slug-login field's programmatic focus is deterministically revoked 0.3 ms after it lands, by glass-ui's own layer focus-repair. On desktop, clicking Login opens a visible, non-inert login layer whose field never holds the caret — every typed keystroke is dropped, and Escape (bound to the input) does nothing either. SlugEditLayer.vue:20-22's nextTick focus is dead code at runtime.
defects.evidence: Instrumented focus()-stack trace (scratchpad/p4-focus2.mjs): `+193.9ms .focus() on input[enter slug or token.] @ ... at /demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:29:25` → `+201.3ms focusin -> input` → `+201.6ms .focus() on div.dock-face.is-active @ ... at w (@mkbabb_glass-ui_dock.js:895:84)` → `+201.6ms focusout <- input`; final `{active:'div.dock-face.is-active', activeTabindex:'-1', inputIsActive:false}`. Producer source, dist/dock.js:892-896: `!n||!r||!n.contains(r)||(await nextTick(),(_(t)??document.body).focus?.())`. Live state of the layer at that moment: `{visibility:'visible',opacity:'1',pointerEvents:'auto',inertAncestor:false,w:160,h:23}`. Typing test: `input value: ""` after typing 'hello-there-friend-x'.
defects.mechanism: Two nextTick-scheduled focus calls race; the producer's runs second, unconditionally, whenever the OUTGOING face contains document.activeElement — and the desktop Login button lives inside that face. The incoming face carries tabindex="-1" so it absorbs focus. (The mobile ⋮→Login path is unaffected and measured working — the trigger is a portaled reka menu item, outside the face, so no repair fires: `input value: "mobile-typed"`.)
defects.reproduction: Desktop ≥1024px, anonymous session, http://localhost:9000/#/ → click Login → type. The field stays empty. Keyboard users can still reach it with exactly one Tab from the parked face (measured: Tab#1 -> input), so it is a silent focus loss, not a total lockout.
defects.proposedCure: Stop hand-focusing from inside the outgoing layer. Gestalt: the layer declares its entry focus and the layer machine honours it — glass-ui's w() should prefer an explicit target ([autofocus]/focusTarget on DockLayer) inside the incoming face over the face itself (glass-ui BH relay; same cure kills C-35). Demo-side interim: drive focus off the layer's own became-active edge, after the producer's repair, and retire the parent→child imperative poke Dock.vue:61 slugEditRef.value?.onStartSlugEdit().
