Source: Dock.vue:132 passes no :background-canvas; dist/dock.js:715-718 always hands the sampler a getter; dist/dock.js:76-89 De() early-returns on the truthy getter so the documented `[data-glass-field-canvas] canvas, canvas[data-glass-field-canvas]` fallback is unreachable, while dist/dock.js:176's is-live predicate DOES use it; dist/dock.js:216 is the source-unavailable branch. Contradicted claim in the record: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:40-48 ('auto-discovers THIS canvas as its backgroundCanvas and samples the live field').
defects.mechanism: A design-system feature wired by CONVENTION (a data-attribute stamp) rather than by a prop, where the producer's resolver stopped honouring the convention across a major — verified once by reading, never by measuring. Live=true with source=null yields an infinite failing retry loop that writes DOM attributes at 3.5 Hz on the persistent chrome.
defects.reproduction: Load any route, wait past boot, read the dock: `document.querySelector('.glass-dock').getAttribute('data-backdrop-sample-state')` === 'unavailable' and `getComputedStyle(dock).getPropertyValue('--glass-backdrop-luma')` === '0' — on 3/3 routes probed, and re-stamped ~14x per 4 s.
defects.proposedCure: Thread the canvas the App already owns: `<GlassDock :background-canvas="atmosphereCanvas">` (App.vue:9 ref, stamped data-glass-field-canvas at App.vue:16). Producer-side BH relay: De() must fall through to the document convention when the getter yields null, otherwise the stamp is decorative for every consumer in the constellation. No demo-local luminance shim — the ladder token is the producer's and the seam exists. Verify the cured state reaches `sampled` (see C-38: the field canvas is a 300x150 WebGL2 backing store; a blank readback would merely trade source-unavailable for sample-unavailable).

defects.defect: MT-F004's mechanism, named: the three login controls are sub-24px because SlugEditLayer passes `compact` to DockControl, which is the producer's explicit opt-out from the coarse-pointer 2.75rem touch floor — and the demo never sets the --dock-compact-control-* token hooks that its own sibling control already uses. The 160x20 slug input additionally has no accessible name (placeholder only, clipped by a fixed w-40).
defects.evidence: Producer rule, dist/components/dock/styles/controls/touch-floor.css: `@media (pointer: coarse){ .dock-icon-button:not(.dock-icon-button--compact):not(:where(.glass-dock *)){ min-block-size: var(--dock-touch-target,2.75rem); min-inline-size: … } }` — the slug controls hit BOTH exclusions. Compact geometry: icon-button.css `.dock-icon-button--compact{ width:var(--dock-compact-control-size,auto); padding:var(--dock-compact-control-padding,0.25rem) }`. Measured live in the OPEN state at 390x844 isMobile+hasTouch (p4-focus4.mjs): `[{"l":"enter slug or token...","w":160,"h":20},{"l":"Switch to slug","w":23,"h":23},{"l":"Generate new slug","w":23,"h":23},{"l":"Cancel","w":23,"h":23}]`. Input name census (p4-focus.mjs): `{ariaLabel:null,id:null,labelFor:false}`. Source: SlugEditLayer.vue:81-87 (input), :91-118 (three compact DockControls).
defects.mechanism: The demo opted into the producer's documented opt-out and then never re-supplied the geometry through the token seam — the same seam the sibling ActionBarToggle.vue:154-158 already uses (T-36's `--dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem`, asserted at o15-dock-register.spec.ts:126-129). It survived because nothing ever renders this layer (C-36).
defects.reproduction: Open the login layer (click Login on desktop, or ⋮→Login on mobile) and measure the three DockControls and the input: 23x23 / 23x23 / 23x23 and 160x20, all < 24 CSS px, under a coarse pointer.
defects.proposedCure: Apply the T-36 idiom to the login controls: set `--dock-compact-control-padding` (and `--dock-compact-control-size: 2.75rem` under `(pointer: coarse)`) at the root of the slug layer's controls — root-level styling through the producer's own hook, not per-instance overrides, no new component. Give the input a real name (a visually-hidden label or aria-label, plus a non-fixed width so the placeholder is not clipped).

defects.defect: The dock's layer machine is silent to assistive tech: every layer change parks focus on an unnamed, role-less div.dock-face[tabindex="-1"], and the entire band contains no live region in production — the only aria-live/status/alert element is the DEV-gated status lamp.
defects.evidence: Focus landings (p4-focus.mjs): Tools→`div.dock-face.is-active[lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)]`, Back→`div.dock-face.is-active[HomeToolsPickerAbout Log]`, Login→`div.dock-face.is-active[]`. Live-region census of nav.dock-band (p4-perf.mjs): `[ 'span[role=alert,live=null] "dev misconfigured — run `npm r"' ]` — DockStatusLamp.vue:13 is `v-if="lamp"` with `const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV`, so production has zero live regions. The face's only accessible text is the run-together textContent of the controls inside it.
defects.mechanism: State changes are expressed purely visually (crossfade + inert toggling); no announcement channel and no named focus target exist, so the layer swap, the linkCopied flip (ProfileSection.vue:156 'Share color'→'Copied!'), the login result and the view switch are all unannounced.
defects.reproduction: Keyboard-activate any dock layer control (Tools, Back, Login) and read document.activeElement: an unnamed div with tabindex=-1, three times out of three. Then query the band for [aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert],[role=log] in a production build: empty.
defects.proposedCure: One polite live region owned by the dock (the layer machine's announcement seam) plus a real entry-focus target per layer — declared, not poked. Same root as C-31/C-35: the dock's layer machine should own focus and announcement together instead of leaving both to the producer's default face-focus.

defects.defect: ActionBarLayer's two template refs are assigned and never read, and ColorInput's exposed focus() has no caller — so activating 'Open color input' leaves focus on the toggle button and the field unfocused; typed text goes nowhere.
defects.evidence: `grep -n "colorInputRef\|actionToolbarRef" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` → 28,29 (declared), 103,116 (bound) — no read sites. ColorInput.vue:282-288 `defineExpose({focus: () => inputColorRef.value?.focus(), …})` has no caller in the repo. Measured (p4-focus4.mjs, fresh context, desktop): `focused: button[Open color input]` → `after activate: button[Propose color name]` (focus never moved) → typing 'red' leaves the contenteditable at `"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"`; forward Tab from there goes to `button[Select color space]`, i.e. past the field.
defects.mechanism: Same family as C-31 — an entry control that opens a text surface and never hands over focus — plus dead code (two write-only refs, one unused defineExpose surface). ColorInput.vue:262 already does the right thing for the propose-mode swap (rAF focus); the actions→input swap never got it.
defects.reproduction: Desktop: Tools → focus 'Open color input' → Enter → type. The colour field's text is unchanged; document.activeElement is still the toggle.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the two write-only refs, and let the sub-layer swap focus its own entry field on the became-active edge (the same declarative cure as C-31), rather than exposing a focus() nobody calls.

defects.defect: Test truth: nothing in the repository ever opens the slug-edit layer — the whole login surface (C-31's dead focus, C-33's four sub-24px targets, C-23's dead error path) sits behind a documented gate exclusion.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "SlugEditLayer\|slugInput\|Switch to slug\|Generate new slug" e2e/ demo/test/ test/` → no output (zero hits). The exclusion is stated in prose inside the dock's own oracle: e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts:149-152 — 'The conditional layers (mobile-edit, slug-edit) and the portaled menus … are retired at the same source pass; the lane record carries the dock-tree grep-zero.'
defects.mechanism: A grep standing in for a render. The oracle asserts a source property (no native title) instead of rendering the surface, so no behavioural property of that layer is under test at all.
defects.reproduction: Named vacuous mutation (distinct from C-9's and C-29's): delete SlugEditLayer.vue:20-22 (the whole `nextTick(() => { slugInputRef.value?.focus(); })`) — typecheck, unit and e2e all stay green, because the deleted behaviour already does not happen at runtime (C-31).
defects.proposedCure: Replace the grep-shaped assertion with a live one: open the layer, assert document.activeElement IS the input, assert the three controls compute ≥24x24, assert the input has an accessible name, and assert a failed login renders its error. One spec closes four findings' regression surface.

defects.defect: Negative proofs — six suspicions raised by the challenge premise that were measured and died. Recorded so a fifth seat does not re-spend the probes.
defects.evidence: (1) R1 parseCssColor crash class does not reach the dock: 8 malformed ?color= values (oklch(), oklch(NaN NaN NaN), rgb(, color(display-p3 1 0), lab(Infinity 0 0), hsl(0 0% -0%), %%%, empty), fresh context each — every row `{"pageErrors":0,"bandChildren":20,"dockPresent":true,"mainPresent":true}`. (2) Action-bar layer v-if teardown while ACTIVE (location.hash → #/admin/users with the Tools layer open) recovers to main, faceCount 4→3, `pageErrors: []`, restores on return. (3) Zero CanvasRenderingContext2D.getImageData calls across 10 discrete colour changes — the useContrastSafeColor ink probe is properly cached (dock-band mutations 310, ≈31/change). (4) DockControl forwards `type` (dist/dock.js `type: { default: "button" }`), so SlugEditLayer.vue:93's type="submit" is a real submit. (5) ActionBarToggle's hand-rolled `.is-active` hits a real producer rule (icon-button.css `&:is(.is-active,.active,[aria-expanded="true"],[aria-pressed="true"])`). (6) App.vue:32-33's subtree-wide @transitionend.capture/@animationend are guarded (useDockArrival.ts:29-45), so the dock-settle beat cannot re-trigger boot work.
defects.mechanism: n/a — these are the measured absences of defects, reported for honesty under a 'the implementation is defective' premise.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/p4-edge.mjs (1,2), p4-perf.mjs (3), source reads (4,5,6).
defects.proposedCure: None required. Keep (1) and (2) as the regression floor if the parser band lands its cure.

defects.defect: Observation (scoped OUT of this component): the atmosphere field canvas that the dock's sampler is meant to read has a 300x150 UA-default backing store while CSS-stretched to the full viewport, on a webgl2 context.
defects.evidence: scratchpad/p4-backdrop.mjs: `{"autoDiscoverWouldFind":true,"canvasSize":"300x150","canvasCtxKind":"webgl2"}` on 3/3 routes; the element is App.vue:11 `class="atmosphere-canvas absolute inset-0 w-full h-full …"`.
defects.mechanism: Unverified whether useAtmosphere resizes the drawing buffer later or renders deliberately at low resolution — I did not trace it, so this is a hypothesis about the atmosphere, not a finding about the dock.
defects.reproduction: NONE (labelled hypothesis; the measurement above is real, the defect interpretation is not established).
defects.proposedCure: Sequence it before C-32's cure: after threading :background-canvas, assert the sampler reaches data-backdrop-sample-state="sampled" rather than trading source-unavailable for sample-unavailable (a WebGL2 surface without preserveDrawingBuffer reads back blank).

result.strongestDefect: C-31 — the desktop login field's focus is deterministically revoked 0.3 ms after it is set by glass-ui's own layer focus-repair (dist/dock.js:892-896), so clicking Login and typing drops every keystroke; the demo's nextTick focus at SlugEditLayer.vue:20-22 is dead code at runtime, no test ever renders the layer (C-36), and the same mechanism silently breaks the colour input (C-35). Runner-up and arguably the more systemic rot: C-32 — the dock's live backdrop sampler has never succeeded on any route since Glass 7, pinning the adaptive-legibility tint at its 4% floor while the repo's own W7-3 note asserts it works.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the ballast rather than the proof: six suspicions were measured and refuted (full detail in C-37 / report §8.8). (a) The live parseCssColor crash class does not reach the dock — 8 malformed ?color= values incl. `oklch()` produce 0 page errors and a fully rendered 20-button band. (b) The action-bar DockLayer's v-if teardown while it is the ACTIVE layer recovers cleanly to `main` with 0 page errors. (c) Zero getImageData calls across 10 colour changes — the chrome's contrast-ink probe is cached, so there is no per-tick colour math in the persistent dock. (d) DockControl forwards `type`, so the login submit button is real. (e) The Tools button's hand-rolled `.is-active` class hits a real producer rule. (f) App.vue's two subtree-wide transition/animation listeners are guarded, so the dock-settle beat cannot re-trigger boot work. Prior passes' §3 negative proofs (inert hidden layers, live `expanded` expose, the hold mechanism, PRM handling) were not re-litigated.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, served not inherited; receipt is the first section of the report.
result.strongestDefect: D3-01 — the constitution-retired `PaneSegmentedControl` (Dock.vue:197-204) is painted directly on top of the Tools/action-bar control, and the Tools control underneath it has already been emptied of its capability. Two separately-filed defects are the same 30px of screen. `document.elementFromPoint()` at the Tools button's own centre returns `DIV.segmented-indicator` at 390x844, 720x900 (=1440 at 200% zoom) and 1024x1366; both boxes are position:static/z-index:auto, so it is two siblings laid out on top of each other, 100% overlap at the tablet arm. Underneath, `.action-bar-toggle-slot` is width 0px / opacity 0 / tabindex -1 at all three, because `App.vue:322-328` writes `colorPickerRef` only from the desktop pane-slot mount callback. Net: the picker's six primary actions (Reset/Copy/Random/Palettes/Extract/Open color input) do not exist below 1024px, including for a desktop user at 200% browser zoom.
result.negativeProof: Confirmed-sound surfaces I attacked and could not break, so a later round need not re-attack them: (1) band reservation — `.dock-band` height is a constant 72px at 390/720/1024/1440 and in BOTH dock geometries, so VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 4 ("expanded/collapsed/mounted states do not move the scene below it") genuinely holds; (2) inert layering — every inactive `.dock-face` subtree reports `inert:true, aria-hidden:true`, so the harness's at-rest smallTapTargets rows (22x22 slug controls, 160x23 input) are geometry-only at rest, and the real failure is in the active state; (3) no phantom tab stops — live desktop tab set inside the dock is exactly {Select view, Toggle action bar, Login, @mbabb}, and the mobile Tools button carries `tabindex="-1"` (I nearly mis-filed it as a phantom stop; it is not); (4) reduced motion — `animations.css:184-192` neutralises animation+transition durations app-wide and `vj-settle` is transform-only (`scale`), so the dock's one motion composites and does not force layout; (5) edict 6 holds — the keyframe lives globally at `animations.css:170`, `Dock.vue:301-303` holds only the class; (6) edict 8 holds — `Dock.vue:22-24` are the only type-only imports and all three use `import type`; (7) landmarks — `main:1, nav:1` on all 60 audit captures and live, band carries `aria-label="Application navigation"`; (8) no horizontal overflow and no page errors in any matrix or probe.

defects.defect: BLOCKER: the retired-by-law PaneSegmentedControl is painted on top of the Tools/action-bar control, which has itself already lost its capability on every mobile-grammar viewport. Below 1024px the picker's entire action region (Reset color, Copy color, Random color, Palettes, Extract palette, Open color input) does not exist — including for a desktop user at 200% browser zoom.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:197-204 (switcher still mounted) vs VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:89 'V retires the global Dock PaneSegmentedControl and left/right view state' + §3 law 6 + CARRY-LEDGER.md:22 W47 gate 'PaneSegmentedControl 1→0'. Measured (dockprobe9.mjs, live WebKit): slot state on /#/ after 6.5s settle — 390x844 {slotClass:'action-bar-toggle-slot', slotW:'0px', opacity:'0', toolsTabindex:'-1'} · 720x900 identical · 1024x1366 identical · 1440x900 {slotClass:'action-bar-toggle-slot is-visible is-live is-settled', slotW:'125.52px', opacity:'1', toolsTabindex:'0'}. Hit-test (dockprobe4/7/9): 390 tools[153,186] switcher[156,260] elementFromPoint→DIV.segmented-indicator toolsReachable=false · 720 tools[298,330] switcher[300,442] same · 1024x1366 tools[409,510] switcher[398,540] same (100% of a 101px control) · 1440 toolsReachable=true. Both boxes position:static, z-index:auto. Root cause demo/color-picker/App.vue:322-328 `function onDesktopLeftMount(el){ colorPickerRef.value = left==="color-picker" ? el : null; }` feeding App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`. Frame: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-dock/collision-1024x1366.png shows no paintbrush glyph anywhere in the band.
defects.mechanism: Capability wired to a desktop-only DOM ref, then the resulting hole covered by a second surface the canon already retired. One collision, two defect IDs.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at any viewport width < 1024px (or 1440px at 200% browser zoom). The pill renders `Home ˅ | Picker About | ⋮` with no Tools control. Run `document.elementFromPoint()` at the centre of `nav.dock-band button[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]` — it returns DIV.segmented-indicator, not the button. Script: dockprobe9.mjs in the session scratchpad.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the action set through the provide/inject seam the dock already uses for four other concerns (VIEW_MANAGER_KEY, SESSION_PORT_KEY, CSS_COLOR_KEY, SAFE_ACCENT_KEY); delete colorPickerRef and both `?? null` prop hops. Then execute W47's `PaneSegmentedControl 1→0`. Both halves of the collision die together — one colliding surface stops existing, the other stops being conditional.

defects.defect: MAJOR (OVERTURNS r2 D-22, carried by two prior rounds as 'the wax seal has never been observed rendering'): the seal does render. Its gate is pointer history, not elapsed time. The dock therefore has two resting geometries for one idle page, and the collapsed rest is a 56px unlabelled circle that hides all four navigation controls.
defects.evidence: Measured (dockprobe2/3/4): fresh load, no pointer, 7s idle → `.glass-dock … expanded`, pill 471x62; same at 20s idle → still expanded 471x62; mouse.move(700,45) then mouse.move(700,700), 7s → `.glass-dock … collapsed`, pill 56x56, `.dock-seal` 40x40, opacity 1; same cycle but with a prior focus() inside the dock → still expanded. Site: Dock.vue:132 `:collapse-delay="5000" :start-collapsed="false"`. Reads against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:178 'The dock is its own top band, fully visible, focusable' and PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-16/PR-07 (terminal verb for hover-only/unlabeled controls = ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE). Note the band floor DOES hold: .dock-band height constant 72px in both geometries at every viewport.
defects.mechanism: A resting state selected by input device rather than by design. The producer's collapse timer is armed by pointerenter/leave, so a keyboard-only, touch-only or never-hovered desktop session sees a different dock than a mouse session.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 WebKit, load http://localhost:9000/#/, wait 20s without moving the pointer — dock stays 471x62 expanded. Reload, move the pointer over the pill then away, wait 7s — dock is 56x56 with `.dock-seal` visible and all navigation gone. Script: dockprobe3.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Pick one resting state and make it unconditional. If the seal is the rest, set start-collapsed=true and capture the π frame the tranche has never had; if the pill is the rest, delete collapse-delay, the #collapsed slot, .dock-seal* and the ~95 lines of essay above them (Dock.vue:229-268, :309-328). Do not leave a magic 5000ms dwell outside the producer's spring register.

defects.defect: MAJOR: the dock implements none of VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's 'horizontal Dock/rail roving focus' law — no arrow traversal, no Home/End, no separation of movement from activation.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:129 names this component: 'horizontal Dock/rail roving focus — Right moves to the visual-right item; Left to visual-left … Home=first semantic item, End=last; activation is separate from movement.' Measured (dockprobe4 · B, 1440x900): focus `Select view` → ArrowRight → activeElement still `Select view`; → Home → activeElement still `Select view`. `Dock.vue` binds no keydown handler anywhere.
defects.mechanism: Rail behaviour never implemented; the dock is four independent tab stops presented as a horizontal rail.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900, focus `nav.dock-band button[aria-label="Select view"]`, press ArrowRight then Home; activeElement is unchanged both times. Script: dockprobe4.mjs section B.
defects.proposedCure: Roving focus is rail behaviour and belongs to the producer's GlassDock/DockLayerGroup, not a keydown handler grafted into Dock.vue (edict 4: glass-ui is the design system). File it as a glass-ui ask and consume it.

defects.defect: MAJOR: three disagreeing responsive predicates inside one component (four counting the child), and the shell's own source comment states that the width-only one was supposed to have been retired. At 1024x1366 the pill renders the mobile and desktop grammars simultaneously.
defects.evidence: Predicates: Dock.vue:71 `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` (width only) · demo/styles/shell.css:111-124 `[data-layout]` (width AND aspect ≥ 1.1) · MobileMenuDropdown.vue:38, ProfileSection.vue:48,127, ActionBarToggle.vue:84,100 `lg:hidden`/`hidden lg:flex` (width only) · PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46-51 `@media (max-width: 639px)`. shell.css:100-110 states the stamp exists precisely because 'a media wrapper would re-introduce the width-only disagreement the stamp exists to retire.' Measured at 1024x1366 (dockprobe2): dataLayout='mobile', .dock-mobile-panes 141x39@398 SHOWN, ProfileSection Login 83x28@563 SHOWN, @mbabb 73x28@669 SHOWN, `dock-separator hidden lg:block` 1x28@398 SHOWN under the mobile switcher. Frame: collision-1024x1366.png.
defects.mechanism: Four thresholds on three different axes, plus pointer history (D3-02), decide what the dock is; no single source of layout truth.
defects.reproduction: WebKit at 1024x1366 (iPad Pro portrait), load http://localhost:9000/#/. The pill shows `Home ˅ | Picker About | Login | @mbabb` — mobile pane switcher and desktop profile section at once, with the desktop separator buried under the switcher. Script: dockprobe2.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: One injected `useLayoutMode()` derived from the `[data-layout]` stamp (width AND aspect); delete Dock.vue:71 and every `lg:`/`sm:` display utility in the dock subtree, including the 639px fork in PaneSegmentedControl.

defects.defect: MAJOR: every operable control in the mobile dock is below the 44px touch floor (26–33px), while the dropdown that dock opens meets it at 44px. The component sets the correct floor on its secondary surface and misses it on its primary one.
defects.evidence: Measured at 390x844 (dockprobe5): dock at rest — Select view 59x33 · Toggle action bar 33x33 · Picker 49x26 · About 49x26 · Menu 43x33. The menu it opens — Login 44 · Share color 44 · GitHub 55 · Dark mode 44. The 26px rung comes from PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46-51 `@media (max-width:639px){ padding: 0.25rem 0.375rem }`. Same mechanism produces the shell-wide 22x22 (desktop) / 23x23 (mobile) slug controls that appear in the tap-target intersection across all 15 routes x 4 matrices in REPORT.json. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7 and PR-12 — 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities … Invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung.'
defects.mechanism: The glass-ui `compact` DockControl register supplies no invisible hit-seat, so every consumer that wants tight optics also gets a sub-floor target.
defects.reproduction: iPhone 14 Pro emulation at http://localhost:9000/#/, measure getBoundingClientRect() on each `nav.dock-band button`; all heights are 26–33. Script: dockprobe5.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Add a producer-side hit-seat token on the compact register (seat at the 44px floor, optics unchanged at the current rung) and consume it everywhere — not a per-site padding bump, which would violate PR-12's 'touch padding bloats/misaligns visual glyphs'.

defects.defect: MAJOR: the mobile overflow menu has a wrapped row and a material that lets the page's own numerals read through the option copy.
defects.evidence: Frame: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-dock/state-mobilemenu.png (390x844, captured live). (a) The `GitHub` row renders its icon on one line and its label on the next; measured height 55px against 44px for Login/Share color/Dark mode (dockprobe5). (b) The picker's `88.8` and `20.0` numerals are legible behind `Share color` and `GitHub` in the same frame. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19 'Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well' and §4.1 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.' Same frame also shows r2 D-20's type-jurisdiction break — options at a display rung, not §4's `text-small`.
defects.mechanism: The menu is composed from the demo-local `demo/ui/dropdown-menu` primitive (MobileMenuDropdown.vue:9-12) rather than the producer's menu tier, so its row layout, type rung and veil/well decision are all re-derived locally and all three land wrong.
defects.reproduction: iPhone 14 Pro emulation, http://localhost:9000/#/, click `nav.dock-band button[aria-label="Menu"]`, screenshot. GitHub's glyph sits above its label; page numerals show through the copy. Script: dockprobe5.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Move the composition onto glass-ui's menu tier (edict 4 — variants/primitives belong in glass-ui, not demo/ui). The row layout, the control type family and the material tier resolve together from one producer decision.

defects.defect: MAJOR: opening the action bar deletes the dock's navigation identity — the persistent chrome stops being persistent.
defects.evidence: Measured 1440x900 (dockprobe5), frame state-tools-desktop.png. Clicking `Toggle action bar` takes the pill 471x62 → 326x62 (−145px) and re-centres it; the live control set becomes Back 40x40 | Reset color 32x32 | Copy color 32x32 | Random color 32x32 | Palettes 32x32 | Extract palette 32x32 | Open color input 40x40. `Select view`, `Login` and `@mbabb` are gone; the only exit is one unlabelled `←`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:178 'Direct route changes keep its full navigation identity.' Two secondary reads on the same frame: seven adjacent icon-only controls with zero visible labels (PR-07 species) at two size rungs in one row, 40px DockControl bookends around 32px ActionButton middles (PR-06 family).
defects.mechanism: A route-local action region implemented as a layer that evicts the global chrome, instead of as a region of the scene the chassis already allocates.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900, http://localhost:9000/#/, click the Tools control; measure `.glass-dock` and enumerate non-inert buttons in `nav.dock-band`. Script: dockprobe5.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Render the action bar in the scene's action region — §3.1 already allocates one for every member composition — and let the dock keep its four navigation seats at all times. This is the same move §7 already ruled for Account ('one modal side Dialog opened from the Dock, not a route chassis').

defects.defect: MINOR: MT-F005's single desktop-only nameless button, enumerated.
defects.evidence: Measured (dockprobe1, 1440x900): the one nameless button inside `nav.dock-band` is `{ cls: "send-btn btn-interactive", rect: 24x24 @916,28, visibility: "hidden" }`. Source: demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:69 and :78 — two `<button class="send-btn btn-interactive">` with no aria-label and no text child. It lives in the dock's `Open color input` layer, which exists only in the desktop action bar; hence 1 on desktop, 0 on mobile, exactly MT-F005's reported pattern.
defects.mechanism: Icon-only submit control in a colocated layer that never got the dock-wide W6-8 aria-label register pass.
defects.reproduction: 1440x900, http://localhost:9000/#/, query `nav.dock-band button` filtered to those with no aria-label/aria-labelledby/textContent — exactly one, `.send-btn`. Script: dockprobe1.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Give both send-btn instances an aria-label in ColorInput.vue, matching the dock-wide register the rest of the component already follows (Dock.vue:140-142 documents that register).

defects.defect: MINOR: one producer package reached by two different import paths on consecutive lines, and the indirect path closes a module cycle.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:4 `import { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "./";` · Dock.vue:5 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";` · demo/shell/dock/index.ts:2 re-exports the first three from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` · index.ts:5 `export { default as Dock } from "./Dock.vue"`. So index.ts → Dock.vue → index.ts is a cycle, for five symbols that all come from the same package.
defects.mechanism: A barrel that both re-exports a producer and exports its own consumer, used by that consumer.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — the declared model for this seat; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the local `useLayerTransition` shim (ActionBarLayer.vue:53-94) is bound to glass-ui 7.0.0's ORPHANED private CSS contract `.dock-layer`/`.is-active`/`.is-leaving`, which NO component in the installed producer emits (`grep -rl '"dock-layer"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist` → no hits; DockLayer.vue renders `.dock-face`), and the motion it claims does not occur — measured `transition-property: visibility`, `0s`, with opacity stepping exactly {0,1} at swap+60ms. The public successor `<DockCrossfade :active reserve="inline">` shipped in the very same 7.0.0 the shim was written against, in the same commit f2c8f565.
result.negativeProof: Three things are genuinely, provably clean and must not be re-litigated. (1) value.js consumption is exemplary and structurally cannot be wrong: ActionBarLayer imports zero value.js symbols, `grep -rn "@src/" demo/` → 0, and vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES the self-alias set from package.json#exports using anchored regexes resolving to dist/subpaths/*.js — the demo can only resolve the seven published specifiers, so a demo import a real consumer could not write is impossible to author. (2) The glass-ui import at :8 is the granular published subpath `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`, not the root barrel; verbatimModuleSyntax is fully satisfied (`type Ref` inline at :2, `import type` at :5 and :9); `vj-morph` is a global tokenized family in demo/styles/animations.css:103-137 with only `--vj-morph-scale/-y` re-parameterization in the scoped block (edicts 4/5/6 satisfied). (3) The focus-loss hypothesis was actively REFUTED, not deferred: probe 2 drove focus into `.color-input`, then triggered the inert swap, and measured `activeElement = BUTTON.dock-icon-button, isBody:false, inertAncestor:false` at +30ms and +430ms — the triggering click moves focus to the toggle first, and no keyboard path reaches the swap while focus is inside the face. Not a defect.

defects.defect: The local `useLayerTransition` reimplementation is bound to glass-ui's orphaned private CSS contract, and produces no motion at all — it is a divergent shim, not an honest one.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:53-94 (shim) and :91 (binds `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer: `grep -rl '"dock-layer"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist` → NO HITS; dist/dock.js class-string count: "dock-face" 1, "dock-layer" 0; DockLayer.vue.d.ts docstring: "renders its content in a `.dock-face` host". The rules survive only in dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css, reached via exports["./styles"] ← demo/styles/foundation.css:56. Only consumer repo-wide: `grep -rn '"dock-layer"' demo/ | wc -l` → 1. Measured live (1440x900, /#/): transition-property `visibility`, transition-duration `0s` in ALL four sampled phases; opacity exactly 1 and exactly 0 at swap+60ms.
defects.mechanism: Consumer adopted a private, untyped, unexported CSS class contract as its integration surface after the producer retired the component that owned it. Invisible to the type system, the build and CI; a glass-ui PATCH that prunes dead CSS silently breaks sub-layer stacking.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/abl-probe.mjs — chromium 1440x900, http://localhost:9000/#/, click [aria-label="Toggle action bar"], click [aria-label="Open color input"], sample getComputedStyle on both .dock-layer-grid children at rest/+60ms/+460ms. Output: {"transitionProperty":"visibility","transitionDuration":"0s"} and opacity in {"0","1"} at every sample.
defects.proposedCure: Delete :53-94 and :88-94 outright and compose the producer: `<DockCrossfade :active="showInput ? 'input' : 'actions'" reserve="inline"><DockLayer id="actions">…</DockLayer><DockLayer id="input">…</DockLayer></DockCrossfade>` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock. Nesting is legal — DOCK_CROSSFADE_KEY is module-local and distinct from DockContext, so nearest-ancestor injection binds the inner faces to the inner crossfade. Clean break: no alias, no wrapper.

defects.defect: The published library @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 declares the entire glass-ui design system as a RUNTIME dependency while src/ imports it zero times — and glass-ui peer-depends back on value.js, a declared dependency cycle.
defects.evidence: package.json:82-84 `"dependencies": {"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0", "@mkbabb/keyframes.js": "^6.0.0"}`. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" src/ | wc -l` → 0. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo/ | wc -l` → 129. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies contains `"@mkbabb/value.js": "^4.0.0"`. package.json#files = ["dist","!dist/gh-pages","!dist/gh-pages/**"] — the demo is never published. Published surface is seven pure subpaths (./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize); none needs a Vue design system. ActionBarLayer.vue:8 is one of the 129 edges.
defects.mechanism: A devDependency of the DEMO was declared in the LIBRARY's runtime `dependencies`, so every consumer of a colour-maths subpath installs a whole design system, and the two packages declare a cycle.
defects.reproduction: npm i @mkbabb/value.js in a clean tree; @mkbabb/glass-ui + its peer graph is installed for a consumer that only imports @mkbabb/value.js/color. Static: the two greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Move both @mkbabb/glass-ui and @mkbabb/keyframes.js from `dependencies` to `devDependencies`. Nothing that ships loses a dependency (files[] excludes the demo), and the declared cycle is broken.

defects.defect: The dock's action-bar contract has TWO declarations in TWO foreign homes, and neither is the dock.

defects.defect: No peak-size reserve: the dock plate width snaps 141 px in a single frame on the actions→input swap.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1/L-13 — the product's primary navigation renders a role=combobox with ZERO selected options on 7 of the app's 14 named routes (atmosphere, blob, and all five admin/*). Live DOM on /#/atmosphere: triggerText "", 7 role=option children all aria-selected="false", aria-activedescendant null; control /#/browse reads "Browse". The cause is purely structural: the option set (viewEntries, from two hand-written arrays in useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27) and the model value (currentView, from viewSchema/router, range 14) have different owners, and no type, assertion or test relates them. A placeholder would hide the blank label and leave anySelected:false and activeDescendant:null untouched — only the membership invariant repairs the widget.

defects.mechanism: Duplicated ownership of one concept (the view taxonomy) across two modules, with no relation expressed in the type system, the schema, or the tests. viewSchema.ts owns label/icon/hue/panes/defaultPaneIndex for all 14 views but carries NO nav-grouping field — so the dock had to re-enumerate, and the re-enumeration can disagree.

The invariant becomes a theorem rather than an untested assumption.

Live probe: dockLayerAncestors == ["dock-layer dock-layer--full is-active"] — the hand-written layers are descendants of a real producer layer. glass selectors are descendant-scoped: `:where(.glass-dock,.dock-layer-group) .dock-layer {display:flex;align-items:center;grid-area:1/1;gap:var(--dock-layer-gap,.375rem)}`, `.glass-dock:not(.vertical) .dock-layer{min-height:var(--dock-layer-height,2.5rem)}`, and `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * {opacity:var(--child-reveal);scale:calc(0.82+0.18*var(--child-reveal))}` — all land on the nested sub-layers unintentionally, including driving opacity/scale on ActionToolbar's and ColorInput's children during any genuine dock morph.
defects.mechanism: Coupling by class name to a producer's private stylesheet. Invisible to package.json, to typecheck, and to every test — a glass release renaming `.dock-layer` or tightening the selector to `>` breaks this component with no compile error and no failing test.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ console: `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid').children[0].closest('.dock-layer--full')` -> non-null, i.e. a `.dock-layer` inside a `.dock-layer`.
defects.proposedCure: D-2. `<DockLayer>` renders its own `.dock-face` host and never asks the consumer to author producer class names — the coupling becomes a typed component contract instead of a string.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: zero unit tests for this component, and the sole e2e touch asserts only the toggle button's aria-label, which no defect in the component can change.
defects.evidence: `ls test/` -> 21 files, none for the dock; `find test -iname "*dock*" -o -iname "*action*"` -> empty. `grep -rln "ActionBarLayer" test/ e2e/ demo/` -> only e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts, whose entire assertion surface is `await expect(page.getByRole("button",{name:"Propose color name"})).toBeVisible()` — a label computed at ActionBarLayer.vue:131 from toolbarMode + canProposeName alone, on a button that lives OUTSIDE .dock-layer-grid and is never inert during the flow.
defects.mechanism: The gate observes the mode state machine, not the layer machinery the mode drives; the crossfade, the class, the inert and the swap are entirely unasserted.
defects.reproduction: Named green-keeping mutations: (1) delete lines 53-95 and replace subLayerProps with `() => ({})` (no crossfade, no inert, both sub-layers rendered on top of each other) — GREEN; (2) set SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS to 0 or 10_000_000 — GREEN; (3) invert the guard to `inert: isActive ? true : undefined`, inerting the VISIBLE layer and leaving the hidden role=textbox + five buttons in the tab order — GREEN; (4) swap the ids so subLayerProps('input') binds ActionToolbar and subLayerProps('actions') binds ColorInput, showing the wrong layer in every mode — GREEN.
defects.proposedCure: Add a component test asserting the real invariants — exactly one sub-layer carries is-active, the other carries inert, and the active id tracks toolbarMode — and, once D-2 lands, delete the spec's five-line comment excusing the crossfade race (see D-13).

defects.defect: No size reserve: the sub-layer swap is an unreserved, uninterpolated layout jump.
defects.evidence: Measured live: active content width goes 184.0px (ActionToolbar) -> 290.4px (ColorInput) on toggle, a +106.4px instantaneous change with no reserved box. The producer documents this as the primitive's job — DockCrossfade.vue.d.ts: "The reserved box is sized to the peak face as a MEASURE-ONCE `min-block-size` (a running max — NOT a per-swap FLIP)", with `reserve: "block"|"inline"` and `inline` documented for "a horizontal control run". The shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:55 concedes glass's version did "the layer size-morph + crossfade", then reimplements only the crossfade bookkeeping.
defects.mechanism: The reimplementation dropped the peak-reserve half of the retired primitive entirely; nothing sizes the container to the larger of the two faces.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ : sample `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid').children[i].getBoundingClientRect().width` before and after clicking `Open color input` -> 184.0 then 290.4.
defects.proposedCure: D-2 with `reserve="inline"` — inherit the producer's measure-once running-max reserve rather than re-deriving it.

defects.defect: The crossfade timer is never cleared on unmount — a setTimeout outlives its component scope.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:70-79 schedules `timer = setTimeout(() => { leavingLayer.value = null; }, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS)` inside a watch; `grep -c "onScopeDispose\|onUnmounted" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` -> 0. The watch is auto-disposed with the setup scope; the pending timeout is not. The component demonstrably unmounts mid-session: during probing `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid')` went from present to null (throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'parentElement')`) once the app routed to #/admin/users; Dock.vue:153,156 gates it behind two v-ifs (hasAnyActionBar, then actionBar).
defects.mechanism: Missing cleanup that the retired producer composable would have owned. Also the reason local toolbarMode (line 30) silently resets — an unmount discards the user's chosen mode and any half-typed color.
defects.reproduction: Toggle the sub-layer, then within 260ms navigate to a route with no action-bar context; the component unmounts (verified: .dock-layer-grid becomes null) while the timeout remains scheduled and later writes to a disposed ref.
defects.proposedCure: D-2 removes the timer entirely (the producer owns the crossfade lifetime). If D-2 is deferred: `onScopeDispose(() => timer && clearTimeout(timer))`.

defects.defect: Two dead template refs, and two competing template-ref idioms in one 158-line file (edict 7).
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:28-29 declare `colorInputRef` and `actionToolbarRef` via the pre-3.5 `ref<InstanceType<typeof X>|null>(null)` idiom, bound at lines 103 and 116 and never read — `grep -rn "colorInputRef\|actionToolbarRef" demo/ e2e/ test/` returns only the declarations and the ref= bindings, no `.value` access anywhere in the repo. Meanwhile line 83 uses `useTemplateRef` for subLayerGridEl, which is itself dead (its only consumer is `void opts.containerEl` at line 67). All three template refs in the component are unread.
defects.mechanism: Accreted ceremony from an earlier shape, never pruned; the file simultaneously demonstrates the Vue 3.5 idiom and the idiom it replaced.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "colorInputRef\|actionToolbarRef" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` -> lines 28, 29, 103, 116 only; no read site exists.
defects.proposedCure: Delete colorInputRef and actionToolbarRef; subLayerGridEl goes with D-2. If the D-12 cure is taken instead, keep actionToolbarRef and convert it to useTemplateRef so the file speaks one idiom.

defects.defect: A parameter preserved for "signature parity" with a function that exists nowhere — back-compat shimming against a void.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:63-67: `function useLayerTransition(opts: { containerEl: Ref<HTMLElement|null>; activeLayer: Ref<string> }) { void opts.containerEl; // signature parity with the retired producer composable`. `grep -rn "useLayerTransition" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` -> zero hits; there is no caller to be compatible with and no second implementation to swap in. The dead chain also drags `Ref` and `useTemplateRef` into the import at line 2, where neither is otherwise needed.
defects.mechanism: Compatibility ceremony maintained against a removed API — owner edict 2 (no legacy shims) and edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance). The whole useTemplateRef -> containerEl -> void path has no effect.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "useLayerTransition" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` -> 0 results, while ActionBarLayer.vue:67 maintains parity with it.
defects.proposedCure: D-2. Interim: delete the parameter, the call-site argument at line 86, the ref="subLayerGridEl" binding at line 101, and the now-unused Ref/useTemplateRef imports.

defects.defect: `defineExpose` publishes three members with zero consumers, one of them a writable ref that bypasses the component's own state machine.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:96 `defineExpose({ currentToggleIcon, toolbarMode, cycleToolbarMode })`. `grep -rn "currentToggleIcon\|cycleToolbarMode" demo/ e2e/ test/` returns hits only inside this file. The sole mount site, Dock.vue:156, passes props and listens to events and holds no template ref to this component.
defects.mechanism: Dead public surface. Worse than inert: exposing a WRITABLE toolbarMode publishes a second, unguarded way to set a mode whose only legal transitions are encoded in cycleToolbarMode (lines 33-45) — a caller writing `toolbarMode.value = "propose"` bypasses the canProposeName gate at line 37 and strands the component in propose mode for a color that cannot be proposed.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "cycleToolbarMode" demo/ e2e/ test/` -> only ActionBarLayer.vue lines 33, 96, 132.
defects.proposedCure: Delete line 96.

defects.defect: A prop is computed, passed, declared, and never used — a reactive dependency that re-renders the toolbar for nothing and misstates its contract.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:106 passes `:can-propose-name="actionBar.canProposeName.value"`. `grep -n "canProposeName" demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue` -> a single hit, line 72, the declaration; it appears nowhere in ActionToolbar's 65-line template.
defects.mechanism: Leftover prop from an earlier ActionToolbar shape; the consumer keeps feeding it.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "canProposeName" demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue` -> `72:    canProposeName: boolean;` and nothing else.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the binding at ActionBarLayer.vue:106 and the declaration at ActionToolbar.vue:72.

defects.defect: ActionToolbar publishes `clearHover()` specifically so its parent can reset hover state when the toolbar is hidden; ActionBarLayer holds the only possible handle and never calls it.
defects.evidence: ActionToolbar.vue:85-91 — `const activeHover = ref<string|null>(null); function clearHover(){ activeHover.value = null; } defineExpose({ clearHover });`. `grep -rn "clearHover" demo/` returns the definition and the expose and no caller. ActionBarLayer.vue:29 declares actionToolbarRef (the only handle from which clearHover could be called) and never reads it (D-8). When activeSubLayer flips to "input" the toolbar is inerted with whatever activeHover was last set, and it is restored on the way back.
defects.mechanism: A producer of state explicitly published the reset and the consumer ignored it; hover survives the layer going inert on any path that generates no pointerleave before the swap.
defects.reproduction: NONE — the pointer/keyboard sequence needed to strand activeHover was not reproduced live. HYPOTHESIS; the unread expose and the absent call site are code-certain.
defects.proposedCure: Preferred (KISS, no cross-component reach-in): move the reset into ActionToolbar via a watch on an `active` prop, so no parent handle is needed and defineExpose can be dropped. Otherwise call `actionToolbarRef.value?.clearHover()` when activeSubLayer leaves "actions".

defects.defect: The toggle is a disclosure control with no aria-expanded, no aria-controls, no aria-live and no focus management — it swaps a role=textbox in and five named buttons out of the a11y tree silently.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:129-142. Measured live over the subtree: toggle == { label:"Open color input", tag:"BUTTON", role:null, ariaExpanded:null, ariaControls:null, ariaPressed:null }; ariaLiveInScope == 0. `grep -c "focus" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` -> 0: focus is never moved into the revealed input and never restored on close, while line 92 applies inert to the outgoing layer in the same tick as the swap. The producer documents the contract the shim dropped — DockCrossfade.vue.d.ts: "A dissolving focus-holding face transfers focus to its successor, else the body (un-inert-before-focus is load-bearing)." The repo already knows: e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts COVERAGE NOTE concedes the propose contenteditable "is not reliably reachable via accessible-name selectors during the cross-fade. Filed as an E.W3-Lane-A finding". The sibling ActionBarToggle.vue:98-101 models the correct idiom in the same directory (aria-label + :aria-pressed + :tabindex).
defects.mechanism: The hand-reimplementation kept the class/inert bookkeeping and left the focus-transfer half behind; a control a test harness cannot reach by accessible name during a state change is one a screen-reader user cannot reach either.
defects.reproduction: MEASURED part: at http://localhost:9000/#/ , `const t=document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid').parentElement.querySelector('button[aria-label]')` -> the toggle; it has none of aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-pressed, and `t.closest('div').querySelectorAll('[aria-live]').length` -> 0. FOCUS-ORPHAN part: NONE — the specific outcome (document.activeElement falling to <body> when focus is inside ColorInput as inert lands) was NOT reproduced; the live session became unstable (a modal scrim intercepted pointer events, then the app navigated out from under the probe). The absence of focus handling is code-certain; the resulting activeElement is a HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: Structurally D-2 — inherit the producer's focus-transfer-on-dissolve rather than re-deriving it. Immediately: add `:aria-expanded="showInput"` plus an :id/aria-controls pair on the sub-layer hosts, following the ActionBarToggle.vue idiom already present in this directory.

defects.defect: An untokenized magic duration (260ms) in a file whose other transition is fully tokenized — same component, two motion regimes, one of them off-system.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:62 `const SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260;`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css defines --duration-instant:0.1s, --duration-control:0.12s, --duration-fast:0.2s, --duration-normal:0.3s, --duration-slow:0.45s, --duration-panel:0.55s — 260ms matches none, and no CSS in the repo consumes it, so it is coupled to nothing and cannot drift into agreement. 72 lines below, the toggle ICON swap uses the canonical family correctly: `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (line 134), whose rules at demo/styles/animations.css:104-116 are fully tokenized (`opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-decelerate)`, `transform var(--spring-snappy-duration) var(--spring-snappy)`), and which demo/DESIGN.md:275 cites as the reference: "PaletteCard.vue's golden-text-shimmer demonstrates the cubic-bezier path, ActionBarLayer.vue the duration-fast path."
defects.mechanism: Owner edict 6 (animations tokenized, not hardcoded). The component animates a 24px icon with the design system's tokenized morph family and animates the entire content region it toggles with a hand-rolled off-system non-functional timer.
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "260" demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue` -> line 62; `grep -rn "260ms\|0.26s" demo/styles/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/` -> no consumer.
defects.proposedCure: D-2. The KISS interim uses vocabulary already in this file and already blessed by DESIGN.md: wrap the sub-layer content in a plain `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` — exactly what the icon 40 lines below already does, and which would actually render.

defects.defect: A re-provide justified in-comment as back-compat, plus an unnamed DI failure mode from a non-null assertion.
defects.evidence: ActionBarLayer.vue:21-22 — `// Re-provide COLOR_MODEL_KEY so ColorInput works unchanged` / `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, actionBar.colorModel);` — a compatibility shim by its own admission (edict 2). ActionBarLayer.vue:24 — `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!;` asserts non-null, so an absent provider surfaces as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')` inside a render function. The producer this file already imports from models the alternative: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dockContext-BUTlGRNJ.js throws "[glass-ui:dock] useDockContext() called outside <GlassDock>; use useOptionalDockContext() if the primitive may render outside a dock."
defects.mechanism: DI boundary framed as back-compat rather than as architecture, and an unnamed crash where the producer demonstrates a named one.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the inject assertion — no path was found that mounts ActionBarLayer outside the SAFE_ACCENT_KEY provider. HYPOTHESIS. The comment at line 21 is quoted verbatim from source.
defects.proposedCure: Reframe the provide as the component's DI boundary (or pass the model to ColorInput as a prop, retiring the re-provide). Replace the `!` with a named-throw accessor in color-session/keys.ts, mirroring glass's useDockContext/useOptionalDockContext pair.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue (the product's primary navigation), incl. its composable useDockAdminMode.ts, its glass-ui producer surface, its e2e/unit coverage, and the committed visual-audit capture set.
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the explicitly declared seat model, not inherited.

defects.defect: Seven of the fourteen named views have NO navigation entry point, and two of them (atmosphere, blob) are misclassified as admin. `viewEntries` returns one hand-maintained partition of ViewId or the other, never a union and never a projection of the route table; the admin list needs `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated`, and admin mode can only be entered via a row that itself needs auth. For a non-admin user those seven views are reachable ONLY by typing a URL.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27 (the two literal arrays; adminViews contains "atmosphere","blob") and :34-39 (one list or the other). Contradicted by demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:28-29 (atmosphere/blob carry NO meta:{admin:true}, unlike :30-34) and demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:177,186 (accentHueShift 280/320 — the primary 40° fan) vs :195,204,213,222,231 (every real admin view pinned to 0, with the schema's own comment saying admin identity is gold, not a hue turn). SHOT docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png — the full Atmosphere pane renders to an unauthenticated visitor with a Login button in the same dock. GREP: `grep -rn "openView(" e2e/` yields Mix/Palettes/Browse/Gradient/Home/Generate only; atmosphere is reached solely by `page.goto("/#/atmosphere")` (e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:929,1164).
defects.mechanism: The option set is a hand-maintained partition of ViewId held in a composable rather than a projection of the route table; nothing structurally forces userViews ∪ adminViews = keys(VIEW_MAP) or respects meta.admin.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/ unauthenticated, click the "Select view" combobox: exactly 7 options (Home/Palettes/Browse/Extract/Mix/Generate/Gradient) — measured live, count:7. No UI path exists to /#/atmosphere, /#/blob, or any /#/admin/* route.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both literal arrays. Derive the menu from the router, which already holds the authority: one computed over router.getRoutes() partitioned by meta.admin, with label+icon from VIEW_MAP. Drift becomes unrepresentable and atmosphere/blob return to the user set the schema already assigns them.

defects.defect: `isAdminMode` is a one-way latch: the route watcher sets it TRUE and has no else-branch, and does not consult authentication. Any visitor landing on the public /#/atmosphere or /#/blob flips the dock into admin mode, and the false gold admin identity persists across every subsequent navigation until a full page reload.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 — `watch(() => viewManager.currentView.value, (view) => { if (adminViews.includes(view)) { isAdminMode.value = true; } })` with no else and no isAdminAuthenticated check. Consumed at DockViewSelect.vue:70 (`--dock-ring: isAdminMode ? var(--color-gold) : var(--accent-view)`) and :80 (`gold-shimmer-icon`). SHOT shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png shows the gold trigger icon beside a Login button.
defects.mechanism: Derived state (is this route an admin route, and is the user an admin) is stored as a ref and mutated by a partial watcher, so it can neither clear nor stay consistent with auth.
defects.reproduction: 1) Load http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere unauthenticated. Live DOM read of .view-select-trigger: {"dockRing":"var(--color-gold)","iconClass":"lucide lucide-sparkles-icon … gold-shimmer-icon"}. 2) Pick "Home" from the menu. Re-read: {"hash":"#/","triggerText":"Home","dockRing":"var(--color-gold)","iconClass":"lucide lucide-house-icon lucide-house w-6 h-6 shrink-0 gold-shimmer-icon","goldShimmer":true} — still gold, still never authenticated.
defects.proposedCure: isAdminMode is not state: `computed(() => isAdminAuthenticated.value && currentRoute.meta.admin === true)`. Derived, it cannot latch, cannot desync from auth, and cannot be entered by an anonymous deep link; the ref, the watcher and one mutator all disappear.

defects.defect: The trigger label goes BLANK on 7 of the 14 routes and the open menu reports "nothing selected": `:model-value="currentView"` (the route) is bound against options drawn from the hand-partitioned list, so on any unmatched route SelectValue — which has no placeholder — renders nothing and every option is aria-selected="false".
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:52 (`:model-value="currentView"`) vs :92-98 (`v-for="entry in viewEntries"`); :87 `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with no placeholder (glass-ui SelectValueProps = {placeholder?, class?}). SHOT comparison, all unauthenticated desktop-light: picker.png shows icon + "Home"; atmosphere.png and admin-users.png show icon only, no label. LIVE at /#/atmosphere: {"role":"combobox","ariaLabel":"Select view","text":"","rect":{"w":60,"h":32}} and with the listbox open all 7 options report aria-selected "false".
defects.mechanism: A controlled Select whose value domain (the route space) is a strict superset of its rendered option set; the unmatched case is silent by construction.
defects.reproduction: Visit http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob, or any /#/admin/*) at ≥1024px width and read the dock trigger: no text. Open it: count 7, zero options with aria-selected="true".
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-1 — if the option set IS the route set, an unmatched value is unrepresentable. A `placeholder` on SelectValue would mask the seam rather than close it and must not be the fix.

defects.defect: The open navigation menu contains NO indication of the current view. `hide-indicator` on every SelectItem removes glass-ui's only selected-state render, P4-R4 retired the font-weight marker, and the "producer's glass-quiet highlighted-on-open row" the component's own comment names as the replacement carrier does not exist anywhere in producer or consumer CSS. There is also no visible keyboard highlight (WCAG 2.4.7).
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:97 `hide-indicator` on every item; the justification comment at :99-109. GREP (contention-free): `grep -c "data-highlighted" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` → 0; `grep -rc "data-highlighted" demo/styles/*.css` → 0 in all six files; `grep -c 'checked' …/glass-ui.css` → 1, and that single rule is `[data-state=checked] .switch__track{...}` (Switch, not Select). Producer source node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/select-BcBAyLXA.js:272 — `hideIndicator ? "none" : "start"`, and the indicator span is the only checked-state render. LIVE measurement of all 7 rows with Home current: distinctBg ["rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"], distinctWeight ["400"], distinctColor ["rgb(28, 25, 23)"], every row opacity 1 / outline none / boxShadow none / data-highlighted null.
defects.mechanism: An affordance was deleted on the strength of a producer behaviour that was assumed rather than verified; the only remaining carrier (data-state=checked) has no paint in any stylesheet.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/ (current view Home), open the "Select view" combobox, and compute styles for every [role=option]: all seven are byte-identical in background, colour, weight, opacity, outline and box-shadow. data-state is "checked" on Home and "unchecked" on the rest, and nothing paints it.
defects.proposedCure: Selection is the menu's only job. Restore the treatment at the ROOT (edict 4) — a [data-state=checked] rule in glass-ui's select stylesheet, which the whole constellation's selects are missing, not just this one. hide-indicator may then stay; it must not stay while nothing else paints selection.

defects.defect: WCAG 2.5.3 "Label in Name" (Level A) failure on the product's primary navigation: a hard-coded aria-label overrides the visible label, so the accessible name is the constant "Select view" on every route and the current view's name is never in it. Voice-control users cannot operate the nav by what they see.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:68 `aria-label="Select view"`. LIVE accessibility tree, closed state: `- combobox "Select view" [ref=f16e42] [cursor=pointer]:` with child `- generic: Home`. Visible text "Home" is not contained in the accessible name "Select view". Also measured aria-activedescendant: null while closed, so the value is exposed by nothing in the a11y layer once D-3 zeroes aria-selected.
defects.mechanism: aria-label wins over element content; a static role hint was written where a dynamic name was required.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/ and read the trigger's a11y node: name "Select view", visible content "Home". Same on every route.
defects.proposedCure: The visible label IS the name — drop aria-label and let reka compose trigger content + SelectValue into the accessible name. If a role hint is wanted, use aria-labelledby that INCLUDES the value. Note the mobile branch (:87, SelectValue v-if=isDesktop) leaves no content at all below 1024px, so mobile needs the value in the name more than desktop does.

defects.defect: Two independent sources of truth for "is this an admin?" in one menu — the forbidden dual path. The parent gates the option list on `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated`; the child re-injects the same port and gates the admin row on `isAdminAuthenticated` alone.
defects.evidence: Dock.vue:37 injects SESSION_PORT_KEY and Dock.vue:44 passes isAdminAuthenticated into useDockAdminMode, which gates at useDockAdminMode.ts:35 on `isAdminMode.value && isAdminAuthenticated.value`. DockViewSelect.vue:35 injects SESSION_PORT_KEY a second time and DockViewSelect.vue:122 gates on `pm.isAdminAuthenticated.value` alone. usePalettePorts.ts:242 is the single provide site.
defects.mechanism: The child re-derives a fact the parent already owns and passes four other props for; the two predicates are free to disagree and do disagree in exactly the D-2/D-3 state (isAdminMode true, isAdminAuthenticated false → list falls back to userViews so the current route vanishes from it).
defects.reproduction: Reach /#/atmosphere unauthenticated: isAdminMode latches true (D-2) while isAdminAuthenticated is false. viewEntries returns the 7 userViews (so the current view is absent → blank trigger, D-3) while the admin row is correctly withheld — the two gates in disagreement, observable as the blank label.
defects.proposedCure: useDockAdminMode returns the whole menu model — rows plus an optional `adminRow: {mode:"enter"|"exit"} | null` — and DockViewSelect renders it. One predicate, one place, one prop; the child's inject and its non-null assertion both disappear.

defects.defect: Every `update:modelValue` reka emits is a committed history-pushing router.push. There is no highlight-vs-commit distinction, because a Select (a value control) is carrying navigation; reka's SelectTrigger implements native-<select> semantics in which arrow keys CYCLE THE VALUE when focus sits on the trigger.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:55 forwards the raw value change (`@update:model-value="(id) => emit('update:modelValue', id as string)"`); Dock.vue:174 binds it to onViewChange; useDockAdminMode.ts:66-74 calls viewManager.switchView(id as ViewId) → useViewManager.ts:78 router.push. LIVE (once): at #/ with the listbox open and activeElement the combobox, aria-selected true on Home, one real ArrowDown produced {"hash":"#/palettes","activeRole":"combobox","selected":["Palettes"],"expanded":"true"} — navigated, listbox still open, destination exactly the next option.
defects.mechanism: A value-change channel wired directly to a destructive commit, with no separation between moving the highlight and choosing a destination — the category error at the root of the component.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED-ONCE, NEEDS RE-VERIFICATION ON AN UNCONTENDED BROWSER. Steps: load http://localhost:9000/#/, mouse-click the "Select view" combobox, confirm document.activeElement is the combobox, press ArrowDown once → location.hash becomes #/palettes while aria-expanded stays "true". The dev server is driven concurrently by other workflow seats (a foreign ?probe=3 query landed in my page mid-run), and a repeat on a fresh load instead left document.activeElement as BODY with the listbox open — focus placement after pointer-open was observed in three states (combobox / option / BODY), which is itself what makes the arrow path hazardous. The MECHANISM above is source-certain regardless.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the architecture: this is a navigation menu, not a form field. Rows become <a href="#/browse"> in a menu/list — arrow keys move focus and commit nothing, Enter/click navigates, ⌘-click and middle-click finally work (today no href exists anywhere in the product's nav), and the current row is aria-current="page" (which HAS paint conventions, curing D-4). glass-ui already ships DropdownMenu primitives, so this is reuse, not a new component.

defects.defect: `update:open` is declared twice — once in defineEmits and again implicitly by defineModel — producing a duplicated runtime emit declaration. The explicitly declared channel is dead: the component never calls emit("update:open", …).
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:29 (`"update:open": [open: boolean]`) and :33 (`defineModel<boolean>("open", …)`); the only write is :54 `open = $event`. Compiled SFC via @vue/compiler-sfc: `emits: /*@__PURE__*/_mergeModels(["update:modelValue", "update:open"], ["update:open"])` — mergeModels concatenates, so the runtime array is ["update:modelValue","update:open","update:open"].
defects.mechanism: A hand-written emit declaration left in place after the channel was migrated to defineModel — a dual declaration under the no-legacy and KISS edicts.
defects.reproduction: node -e with @vue/compiler-sfc compileScript on demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue; grep the output for `emits:` — the duplicate is in the emitted array.
defects.proposedCure: Delete line 29 and its orphaned comment at :27-28. Separately, rename the misnamed `update:modelValue` channel: there is no modelValue prop (the value arrives as `currentView` at :18), so the emit should be `select` or `update:view` — the name currently advertises a v-model contract the component does not implement.

result.strongestDefect: D-1/D-3/D-2 as one family: the selector's option set is not a function of the route space. `viewEntries` is a hand-maintained partition of ViewId (useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27, :34-39) rather than a projection of the router, so (a) seven of the fourteen named views — including atmosphere and blob, which the router leaves un-flagged and the schema hue-shifts as PRIMARY (280°/320°) — have no navigation entry point at all and are reachable only by typing a URL; (b) on those seven routes the controlled Select has no matching option, so the trigger renders NO label (measured text:"" ; SHOT atmosphere.png / admin-users.png vs picker.png) and every option reports aria-selected="false"; and (c) the flag deciding which partition renders is a one-way latch with no else-branch and no auth check (useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59), so an anonymous visitor to /#/atmosphere is put into admin mode and keeps the gold admin identity on every subsequent view until reload (measured: hash "#/", triggerText "Home", dockRing "var(--color-gold)", gold-shimmer-icon on the Home glyph). One derivation — option set = route set partitioned by meta.admin, isAdminMode = computed over route+auth — retires all three.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. For the record, the following hypotheses were tested and DISPROVEN, and are documented in the report's "Passes" section so the negatives are proven rather than assumed: (1) the defineModel stale-read hazard does NOT apply — `open` is a defineModel over the parent's mutex-backed WritableComputedRef and the mutex genuinely defers 180ms (usePopupMutex.ts:46-54), but the component never reads `open` after writing it, so no stale read exists; (2) usePopupMutex leaks no timer — clearSwapTimer runs on every re-open path and on onUnmounted (:82), and the one path leaving a live timer (close-during-swap, :63-68) fires with pending===null and assigns current=null, benign; (3) no PRM-RAF site — this component has no rAF, and the dock's single rAF (Dock.vue:105) is one-shot cleared by @animationend.self (Dock.vue:130); (4) no ValueUnit nesting, no parseCssColor path, no oklch→HSV hue drift — the component parses nothing and receives --accent-view pre-resolved (useViewAccents.ts:144); (5) the --accent-view transition at :159-161 is NOT a no-op — the property is registered with a syntax at demo/styles/foundation.css:192, and accentHueShift is genuinely consumed at useViewAccents.ts:138, so the per-view hue survived the PRIMARY_VIEW_IDS excision intact (checked specifically because the sibling machinery is documented dead at useViewAccents.ts:21-22); (6) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean — `import type { ViewEntry }` at :9, every other import a value import; (7) tap targets are clean — options 174×44px, and REPORT.json shows ZERO dock-select contributions to smallTapTargets across all 60 captures (the 8 on /#/ are slug-edit buttons at 22×22 and four 12×24 channel handles); (8) not a god module — 162 lines, ~100 of code, one job; (9) animations edict satisfied — vj-morph/vj-settle live in demo/styles/animations.css and the one scoped rule here is a transition, not a keyframe.
