result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1+D-2 — the local `useLayerTransition` shim (ActionBarLayer.vue:53-94) is a DEAD transition bound to producer-PRIVATE CSS. Measured live: the only transition on the sub-layer nodes is `visibility` (`transition: "visibility"` / `"visibility 0s linear 0.3s"`); the leaving layer is already at opacity 0 by t=40ms and never shows an intermediate value — so the 260ms `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS` window guards a beat that never plays. The classes it hand-binds (`.dock-layer` / `.is-active` / `.is-leaving`, line 91) are GlassDock's private expanded-vs-collapsed plate classes — in Glass 7 `dist/dock.js` emits `.dock-layer` at exactly two sites, both internal (`dock-layer--full`, `dock-layer--summary`); the PUBLIC face class is `.dock-face`. And the container class they hang from, `.dock-layer-grid` (line 101), is defined NOWHERE (0 hits across demo/, src/, node_modules/@mkbabb) — computed `display: block; position: static`, making the inherited `grid-area: 1/1` inert and resolving the overlap against `.dock-face.is-active` instead. The header's justification ("offers no public composable successor") is materially false: `DockCrossfade` is exported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` — the same specifier line 8 already imports from — and its doc-comment names this exact case ("the controlled-no-rail case (a consumer) consumes this DIRECTLY").
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negatives that WERE proven, and are recorded in §4 of the report so refuted hypotheses do not propagate: (1) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean — line 2 qualifies `type Ref` inline, lines 5/9 are `import type`; (2) the closed action-bar face IS correctly inert, producer-applied — measured `faceInert: true`, `anyInertAncestor: true`, so no hidden-focus tab leak; (3) my `justify-around` end-asymmetry hypothesis is REFUTED by measurement — `leadIn: 0`, `tailOut: 0`, `interGaps: [6,6,6,6]`; the box is exactly content-sized so space-around has no free space, though the 6px arrives only via the illegitimate `.dock-layer` class of D-2, which is a dependency proof; (4) the dock-open HOLD leak I predicted from the un-fired `onHoverOpenChange(false)` is REFUTED — after 7s idle the popover count returned to 0, so `release()` did fire and the dock's continued `expanded` state is explained by `shouldKeepOpen` at Dock.vue:86, correct by design; (5) no vertical band disturbance — pill height 62px in both modes, VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.4 holds; (6) PALETTE-CONTRACT.md read in full and is NOT APPLICABLE — it is the api/wire/export authority and carries no visual or accent law this component could violate.)

defects.defect: The 260ms `SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS` window animates nothing — the crossfade it guards does not exist in Glass 7. `layers.css` gives `.dock-layer` exactly one transition (`visibility`) and animates opacity only under `.glass-dock[data-morphing]` (a dock collapse/expand), never during a content swap.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62,76. Live measurement (WebKit, localhost:9000, 1440x900): computed `transition` on the active sub-layer = "visibility"; on the inactive = "visibility 0s linear 0.3s". Swap timeline: `t=0 ACT op=1 ... / t=0 off op=0` then `t=40 LEAV op=0 vis=visible inert=1 rect=516,18 408x46` — the leaving layer is already at opacity 0 by the first post-swap sample and no intermediate opacity is ever observed. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css.
defects.mechanism: consumer reimplemented a producer mechanism against a producer stylesheet that has since moved the mechanism elsewhere; the JS half survived, the CSS half did not
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900, click [aria-label="Toggle action bar"], wait 800ms, then click [aria-label="Open color input"] and sample getComputedStyle(el).opacity on both `.dock-layer-grid` children at t=0/40/130/280/480ms. Opacity is only ever 1 or 0.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 53-94 and 88-94; replace with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. All four symbols are already public on `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`. The real overlap then rides the producer's `--dock-t` scalar on `useDockSpring` (velocity-continuous, interruptible).

defects.defect: The component hand-applies GlassDock's PRIVATE shell-pane classes (`.dock-layer` + `is-active`/`is-leaving`) to arbitrary consumer components. In Glass 7 the public face class is `.dock-face`; `.dock-layer` is emitted only by GlassDock's own two internal plates. Because every `.dock-layer` rule is scoped `:where(.glass-dock, .dock-layer-group) .dock-layer`, the counterfeit faces match the dock's private plate rules — including two that are actively hostile during a dock morph.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:91. Scan of the producer bundle: `python3 -c "...re.finditer(r'dock-layer(?![-a-z])', open('dist/dock.js').read())..."` returns exactly two emission sites, both internal: `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--full", {...}])` and `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--summary", {...}])`. The public face component emits `class: L(["dock-face", { "is-active": ..., "is-le..." }])`. Hostile rules in layers.css: `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-morph-t)); }` and `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * { opacity: var(--child-reveal); scale: calc(0.82 + 0.18 * var(--child-reveal)); }`.
defects.mechanism: consumer styles itself from producer internals — a silent breakage contract, since no public API ever promised these class names
defects.reproduction: grep the emission sites as above; then on the live page confirm the consumer nodes carry the class: the two `.dock-layer-grid` children report className `"flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active"` and `"grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0 dock-layer min-w-0"`. (The compound swap-during-dock-morph symptom is a HYPOTHESIS — the rules and the class match are both confirmed, but I did not capture a simultaneous frame.)
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as D-1 — `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` carry the producer's own `.dock-face` packaging, so the consumer stops naming producer internals at all.

defects.defect: `.dock-layer-grid` is defined nowhere; the inherited `grid-area: 1/1` is inert and the sub-layer overlap resolves against the wrong box — the inactive layer is 65px left of, 118px wider than, and 3px proud of its nominal box, spanning across the Back control, the separator and the mode toggle.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/` returns ONE hit — the use site, demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:101. Zero definitions. Live: `gridComputed: {display: "block", position: "static", gridTemplateColumns: "none", flexGrow: "1"}`; `inactiveOffsetParent: "dock-face is-active"`; inactive box `516,18 408x46` vs nominal grid box `634,21 184x40`.
defects.mechanism: a layout mechanism named but never implemented; the overlap comes solely from `position:absolute; inset:0` with no positioned ancestor at the intended container
defects.reproduction: Open the action-bar layer, then evaluate `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid'))` and the offsetParent + getBoundingClientRect of its non-`.is-active` child.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the class. `<DockCrossfade>` supplies `.dock-crossfade { position: relative; display: grid; isolation: isolate }` and anchors `.dock-face` at `grid-area: 1/1` inside it — the box the overlap was always meant to resolve against.

defects.defect: The shim's JS duration and the producer's CSS token disagree across a package boundary: 260ms vs `--duration-normal` = 300ms. The shim releases `is-leaving` 40ms before the producer's visibility hand-off elapses.

defects.mechanism: an untokenized magic number required to stay in lockstep with a token in a different package, with no enforcement

defects.defect: The shim is a self-declared legacy shim: it accepts and discards a parameter purely for 'signature parity with the retired producer composable', and its header calls itself a shim preserving a contract to an API that no longer exists. defects.defect: No peak reserve: pressing the mode toggle moves the mode toggle 70.4px out from under the pointer. The interaction is a three-state CYCLE, so the design asks the user to press the same control repeatedly and then moves it away after the first press.

Sub-layer content 184px (actions) vs 324.8px (input) in a `fit-content` dock. Visual: shot-desktop-light-2-actions.png vs shot-desktop-light-3-input.png. Cycle at ActionBarLayer.vue:33-45.
defects.mechanism: the producer's MEASURE-ONCE running-max reserve was dropped when the composable was reimplemented; the dock re-measures to the live face on every swap

Centre moves +70.4px; |dx| exceeds the control's own 40px width.

Visual: shot-mobile-light-1-main.png shows Home / [Picker·About] / ⋮ and no Tools trigger. MobileMenuDropdown.vue:52-101 offers only Copy SLUG, slug edit, logout, regenerate slug, share link, dark toggle. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.6 ('Mobile uses one document-scrolling stage→inspector→ACTION sequence'), §7 Picker ('Copy lives once in the action region'), and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-13 ('action Copy 1→1').
defects.mechanism: presence derived from a sibling template ref that only one breakpoint's slot ever assigns — an entire responsive arm silently evaluates to null
defects.reproduction: Launch WebKit with devices['iPhone 14'], goto http://localhost:9000/#/, wait 2800ms, then evaluate the slot/button geometry and `document.querySelector('[aria-label="Toggle action bar"]').click()` followed by `document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid')` — returns null.
defects.proposedCure: Provide the ActionBarContext through DI (the app already provides the ONE pipeline at App.vue:257) instead of a sibling template ref, so presence is breakpoint-independent; then design the mobile action composition §3.6 requires. A `:on-mount` binding on the mobile PaneSlot is the minimal patch but leaves the sibling-ref coupling intact.

defects.defect: Every mode swap drops keyboard focus to `document.body`. The shim applies `inert` to the outgoing layer with no focus transfer, so the browser evicts focus and the next Tab restarts from the top of the document.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:92 `inert: isActive ? undefined : true`. Live: `{focusBefore: "Copy color", focusImmediate: "Copy color", focusSettled: "BODY"}`. The producer successor documents this as load-bearing (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/DockCrossfade.vue.d.ts): 'A dissolving focus-holding face transfers focus to its successor, else the body (un-inert-before-focus is load-bearing).' Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1 and §4.1.
defects.mechanism: the reimplementation kept the `inert` half of the producer's contract and dropped the focus-transfer half
defects.reproduction: Open the action-bar layer at 1440x900, `grid.querySelector('button[aria-label="Copy color"]').focus()`, click [aria-label="Open color input"], then read document.activeElement at +480ms — it is document.body.
defects.proposedCure: `<DockCrossfade>` performs the transfer itself. No consumer code.

defects.defect: The outgoing layer's hover popover is stranded fully opaque after the swap, and — because the pointer has not moved — the incoming layer opens ITS popover under the same point, producing two overlapping, mutually illegible tooltip slabs over the dock.
defects.evidence: Live: `strandedPopover: [{w:288, h:119, op:"1"}]` while `originButton: {inertAncestor: true, layerOpacity: "0", layerVis: "visible"}`. Screenshot D-02-stranded-popover-after-swap.png shows 'Copy color / Click to copy the current color to the clipboard' interleaved with 'Enter a color / ...ring is accepted / lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)'. The handle exists and is never turned: ActionBarLayer.vue:29 declares `actionToolbarRef` and never reads it; ActionToolbar.vue:87-91 exposes `clearHover()` and `grep -rn clearHover demo/` finds only the definition and the defineExpose — no caller. Breaks the standing register law recorded at SlugEditLayer.vue:88-90 and Dock.vue:140-142 ('the UA tooltip slab is a foreign register on the liquid-glass dock').
defects.mechanism: the swap owner performs no teardown of the outgoing face's transient UI; two halves of one contract wired to nothing
defects.reproduction: Open the action-bar layer at 1440x900, `page.locator('.dock-layer-grid button[aria-label="Copy color"]').hover()`, wait 700ms (300ms open-delay + settle), then `page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector('[aria-label="Open color input"]').click())` WITHOUT moving the mouse, wait 450ms and screenshot.
defects.proposedCure: Once `<DockCrossfade>` owns the swap, dismiss the face's popovers on its inert/unmount hook; failing that, call `actionToolbarRef.clearHover()` on the mode change — the ref already exists for exactly this.

defects.defect: The toolbar mode is sticky across a full close-and-reopen. A control labelled 'Tools' with a paintbrush icon reopens showing a text field; the entry affordance and the entered state disagree permanently after one use.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:30 — `toolbarMode` is never reset and nothing watches `actionBarLayerActive`. Live: `{s1_openedAs: "Open color input", s1_afterToggle: "Propose color name", s1_afterBack: "Propose color name", s1_onReopen: "Propose color name", s1_verdict: "STICKY — reopens in the prior mode"}`. Entry affordance at Dock.vue:186-187 (`genericBar?.icon ?? Paintbrush`, `?? 'Tools'`). Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 (select → tune → commit).
defects.mechanism: sub-mode state with no lifecycle reconciliation against its own container's open/closed state
defects.reproduction: At 1440x900: click [aria-label="Toggle action bar"] (opens in actions — toggle reads 'Open color input'), click the toggle (now 'Propose color name'), click [aria-label="Back"], then click [aria-label="Toggle action bar"] again — the toggle still reads 'Propose color name'.
defects.proposedCure: Reset `toolbarMode = "actions"` when the action-bar layer closes (watch the parent's active-layer, or reset on the component's own deactivation once it is a `<DockLayer>` face).

defects.defect: `toolbarMode === "propose"` is never reconciled when its own precondition `canProposeName` flips false — the layer stays in propose mode with a live submit button for a proposal the pipeline has already ruled out, and the toggle announces 'Close propose'.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:37 reads `actionBar.canProposeName.value` only at the moment of transition; no watcher exists. demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:66-70 — `const canProposeName = computed(() => !findCustomName(currentXYZString.value))` is live and flips as soon as the current colour acquires a custom name. Consumer: ActionBarLayer.vue:119 `:propose-mode="toolbarMode === 'propose'"`.
defects.mechanism: a stateful mode with no reconciliation watcher on the reactive precondition that gates entry to it
defects.reproduction: NONE — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. Reaching it requires a colour that resolves to an approved custom name while propose mode is open; I did not construct that fixture. The mechanism is confirmed by reading only.
defects.proposedCure: `watch(() => actionBar.canProposeName.value, ok => { if (!ok && toolbarMode.value === 'propose') toolbarMode.value = 'actions'; })`.

defects.defect: The shim has no `prefers-reduced-motion` branch: `setTimeout(..., 260)` is unconditional, so under PRM the leaving layer holds `is-leaving` — and `visibility: visible` — for a further 260ms after everything has already settled.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:76. The house PRM guard shortens transitions to 0.01ms but cannot touch a JS timer — recorded at demo/shell/dock/ActionBarToggle.vue:29-30 ('PRM included — the global guard shortens transitions to 0.01ms, never removes them'). Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 ('Reduced motion resolves DIRECTLY to the final geometry and stable chromatic state').
defects.mechanism: motion timing expressed as an imperative JS timer that no media query can reach
defects.reproduction: NONE for the visible symptom — labelled a HYPOTHESIS at the pixel level; the unconditional timer and the documented guard behaviour are both confirmed by reading. (The state matrix at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs never opens this layer, so no PRM capture of it exists.)
defects.proposedCure: Retire with the shim — `<DockCrossfade>` rides `useDockSpring`, which the producer already degrades under PRM.

defects.defect: A second, shadowing `COLOR_MODEL_KEY` provider. The app root already provides the ONE pipeline; ActionBarLayer re-provides a prop-sourced copy for its subtree, with the comment stating the reason outright — 'so ColorInput works unchanged'. One key, two providers, two truths.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/App.vue:257 `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, pipeline);` vs demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:21-22 `// Re-provide COLOR_MODEL_KEY so ColorInput works unchanged` / `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, actionBar.colorModel);`. Seven other consumers inject the app-root one: ColorPicker.vue:172, ColorInput.vue:155, ParseEchoReadout.vue:31, ComponentSliders.vue:115, SpectrumCanvas.vue:50, HeroBlob.vue:56, ConsoleRail.vue:115; AboutPane.vue:9 records it as 'ambient since S.W2'. Owner edict 2 forbids masking fallbacks and compat paths — 'migrate the consumer to the new API at the root'.
defects.mechanism: a compat re-provide so a child need not be migrated, creating a second injection edge for one canonical key
defects.reproduction: NONE for a user-visible symptom — labelled a HYPOTHESIS that the two edges can diverge; the dual provide is confirmed by the grep above (`grep -rn "provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY" demo/` returns exactly these two sites).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the re-provide; migrate ColorInput and ParseEchoReadout to the app-root pipeline at the root, per edict 2.

defects.defect: Per-instance inline styling where the design-system root owns the ink — three separate overrides of colour that `DockControl` already owns (a Tailwind `stroke-foreground` hard-stop, a private one-off custom property injected inline per instance, and a scoped `:hover` rule to consume it). Neither survives forced-colors, and no system-color fallback is declared.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:138-139 `class="toggle-btn w-6 h-6 stroke-foreground" :style="{ '--toggle-hover-color': safeAccent }"` and 149-151 `.toggle-btn:hover { stroke: var(--toggle-hover-color); }`. Measured live: `{toggleHoverColor: "oklch(47.09...% 0.188... 9.83...deg)", stroke: "rgb(28, 25, 23)", inlineStyleAttr: "--toggle-hover-color: oklch(...);"}`. Correct pattern two directories up: ActionBarToggle.vue:154-158 styles through the producer's OWN token hook `--dock-compact-control-padding`, commented 'rides the producer's OWN token hook ... never a specificity fight'. Owner edict 5.
defects.mechanism: consumer-authored ink instead of consuming the producer control's token
defects.reproduction: Open the action-bar layer and read `document.querySelector('.toggle-btn').getAttribute('style')` — the inline custom property is present on the element.
defects.proposedCure: Drop `stroke-foreground` and the inline custom property; take hover ink from DockControl's token, as the sibling ActionBarToggle already does.

defects.defect: Three dead handles: the entire `defineExpose` surface is unreachable because the parent mounts the component with no ref, and both component refs are declared and never read.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:96 `defineExpose({ currentToggleIcon, toolbarMode, cycleToolbarMode })` vs demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:156 `<ActionBarLayer v-if="actionBar" :action-bar="actionBar" ... />` — no `ref=` attribute. Lines 28 (`colorInputRef`) and 29 (`actionToolbarRef`) are declared and never read anywhere in the file.
defects.mechanism: API surface retained after its consumer was removed
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static; the absence of a `ref=` on Dock.vue:156 and of any read of the two refs in the 158-line file are both directly verifiable.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 28, 29 and 96 — except `actionToolbarRef`, which should instead be given its one legitimate job (D-9) or deleted alongside the shim.

defects.defect: Two template-ref idioms in one 158-line SFC: the legacy `ref<InstanceType<typeof X> | null>(null)` pattern at lines 28-29 and Vue 3.5's `useTemplateRef` at line 83. Owner edict 7 mandates `useTemplateRef`.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:28-29 vs :83 (`const subLayerGridEl = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>("subLayerGridEl");`) — 55 lines apart, same file, same wave.
defects.mechanism: idiom drift within a single authoring pass
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static, both lines quoted.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both legacy refs with D-15; if any survives, use `useTemplateRef`.

defects.defect: A dead prop crossing the component seam: `ActionToolbar` declares `canProposeName` as a required prop and its template never references it, while ActionBarLayer dutifully passes it.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue:72 (`canProposeName: boolean;` in defineProps) with no reference anywhere in its template (lines 1-63); demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:106 `:can-propose-name="actionBar.canProposeName.value"`. Confirmed by `grep -rn "canProposeName|can-propose-name" demo/`.
defects.mechanism: prop retained after the logic that consumed it moved to the parent
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static; the grep output enumerates every occurrence.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop from ActionToolbar and the binding at ActionBarLayer.vue:106.

defects.defect: A 176-character three-branch nested ternary computes the toggle's accessible name inline in the template — the only thing distinguishing three otherwise identical states, and made load-bearing by D-10.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:131. The same three-way state is already switched on in a `computed` 80 lines above (`currentToggleIcon`, lines 47-51) — two switches on one state variable, in two languages, in two places.
defects.mechanism: presentation logic split between a computed and a template expression
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static, line quoted.
defects.proposedCure: Lift to a `computed` beside `currentToggleIcon` so icon and name derive from one switch.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for `demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context Opus 5 seat), spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — `DockViewSelect.vue:70` writes a COLOR into glass-ui's `--dock-ring`, which is a box-shadow value token (`sizing.css: --dock-ring: var(--focus-ring-shadow)`) consumed by `.dock-select-trigger:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--dock-ring); outline: none; }`. `box-shadow: oklch(...)` is invalid at computed-value time → `none`; `outline: none` already applied → the product's primary navigation control has NO keyboard focus indicator. Measured in Chromium at Tab press #1 with `:focus-visible` true: `box-shadow: "none"`, `outline-style: "none"`, while the sibling `.dock-icon-button` in the same frame carries the full two-layer producer ring. This is a verbatim recurrence of the tranche's own U-F25 lesson recorded at `demo/styles/focus-ring.css:9-15`.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundly-checked items in the report's "What I checked and found sound" section: verbatimModuleSyntax clean; vj-morph consumed from the shared global animations.css rather than re-declared; reduced-motion measured working (transition-property collapses to opacity/0.15s, --accent-view sweep neutralised); no layout-forcing animated property; every option row measures h=44 meeting the touch floor; overflowX=0 at 1440/720/390 CSS px; Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure correct; exactly one `palettes-ramp-text` coordinate as the constitution requires.)

defects.defect: The keyboard focus ring on the product's primary navigation control renders nothing: line 70 overwrites glass-ui's shadow-valued `--dock-ring` token with a bare color, invalidating the producer's `box-shadow: var(--dock-ring)` at `:focus-visible`, where `outline: none` has already removed the fallback.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:70 `:style="{ '--dock-ring': isAdminMode ? 'var(--color-gold)' : 'var(--accent-view)' }"` vs node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css `--dock-ring: var(--focus-ring-shadow)` and .../components/dock/styles/index.css `.dock-select-trigger:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--dock-ring); outline: none; }`. Chromium measured: {"active":true,"matchesFocusVisible":true,"boxShadow":"none","outlineStyle":"none","dockRing":"oklch(0.471189 0.0962884 89.834)"}. Sibling .dock-icon-button same frame: dockRing = "0 0 0 2px color-mix(...) , 0 0 8px color-mix(...)". In-page substitution test: withConsumerValue -> "none"; withProducerDefault -> the real 2-layer ring. Screenshot scratchpad/D2-focus-chromium.png shows a focused trigger pixel-identical to rest.
defects.mechanism: consumer writes a value of the wrong TYPE into a producer value-token (retyping a producer contract); invalid-at-computed-value-time collapses box-shadow to initial `none`
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/browse in Chrome; press Tab once; DevTools > Computed on button.view-select-trigger => box-shadow: none, outline-style: none. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe2.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `--dock-ring` arm on line 70 outright — the producer default ring is correct and complete. The hue-on-focus intent needs a producer seam that separates ring GEOMETRY from ring HUE (`--dock-ring-color` / `--focus-ring-hue`) composed inside glass-ui; file it as a BJ ask. Standing rule: a consumer never assigns a producer token a value of a different type.

defects.defect: The trigger renders an EMPTY label on 7 of 14 routes and simultaneously wears the admin gold identity on /atmosphere and /blob, which are not admin surfaces; the open menu reports `aria-selected=false` on every option, i.e. "no selection", while the app is on a route.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit 1440x900 (isDesktop true), scratchpad/D-probe3.json: labels `Home|Palettes|Browse|Extract|Mix|Generate|Gradient` for the 7 user routes; label="" and goldIcon=true for /atmosphere, /blob, /admin/users, /admin/names, /admin/audit, /admin/flagged, /admin/tags, while document.title reads e.g. "Atmosphere — Color Picker". Menu open on /#/atmosphere: all 7 options aria-selected="false". Corroborated by the tracked real-Safari shot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png. Mechanism: useDockAdminMode.ts:34-40 gates the option set on `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated` while :56-60 flips `isAdminMode` on route alone; DockViewSelect.vue:70,80 consume `isAdminMode` alone. No route guard exists (`grep -rn beforeEach demo/` = no matches) and router/index.ts:30-34 `meta:{admin:true}` is never read.
defects.mechanism: one identity derived twice from two different predicates; the model value and the option set have different owners, so a state exists where the value has no matching option
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere unauthenticated -> dock shows gold sparkle + chevron, no text; open the menu -> 7 options, none selected. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe3.mjs
defects.proposedCure: One enumeration, one predicate. Add `audience: "public" | "admin"` to `demo/shell/viewSchema.ts` (which already types every view) and derive BOTH the option set and the mode flag from it, so no state can exist where the value has no option. Promote /atmosphere and /blob to public member routes, as VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:58 already declares them, and delete the route-shaped admin guess.

defects.defect: The open menu marks the current destination with zero pixels: the selected row's computed styles are byte-identical to every unselected row, in light, dark AND forced-colors. Selection and focus/highlight collapse onto one channel, which is the highlight channel.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit /#/browse menu open (scratchpad/D-probe.json): all 7 rows background-color rgba(0,0,0,0), color rgb(28,25,23) (light) / rgb(233,230,226) (dark), font-weight 400, padding-left 10px, box-shadow none, outline none — including the row with aria-selected=true / data-state=checked. Chromium forcedColors:active (D-probe2.json): all 7 rows bg rgba(255,255,255,0), color rgb(0,0,0), boxShadow none, fw 400. Cause: DockViewSelect.vue:97 and :127 pass `hide-indicator`, deleting glass-ui's only selected-state affordance (select-BcBAyLXA.js: `hideIndicator ? "none" : "start"` -> the pl-7 gutter dot); menuRowClass-Nh7CtMON.js + components/_shared/menu.css style only :hover/:focus/[data-highlighted]/[data-state=open]. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83-84 ("never color-only"; "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency"). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:79 already ruled the identical species for ColorSpaceSelector.
defects.mechanism: the consumer deleted the producer's sole selection marker and re-pointed selection at the transient highlight channel, merging two orthogonal states
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, click the dock view trigger, inspect all [role=option] computed styles — the checked row differs in no visual property. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Delete both `hide-indicator` props and consume the producer indicator gutter, exactly as PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:79 required of ColorSpaceSelector. Widen that register row from one component to EVERY dock Select rather than re-litigating it per instance: one marker agreeing with aria-selected, independent of [data-highlighted].

defects.defect: At 200% browser zoom the primary navigation loses its text label entirely, because label presence is keyed to a device-class media query rather than the control's own available space.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit at 720x450 CSS px (= 200% zoom on a 1440x900 display), scratchpad/D-probe5.json: {"label":"","w":56,"h":32,"overflowX":0}; the same control at 100% reads "Gradient" at 128.1px. Source: DockViewSelect.vue:87 `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with Dock.vue:71 `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")`. Hits open register row PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:60 (PR-16, "labels remain perceptible in both schemes") and the constitution's mandated actual-400%-zoom evidence arms (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:62,64,78).
defects.mechanism: a global viewport breakpoint standing in for a local fit decision; browser zoom shrinks the CSS viewport so a desktop/mobile predicate fires on a desktop
defects.reproduction: Chrome at 1440x900, http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, Cmd-+ to 200% -> the dock trigger shows icon+chevron only. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe5.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Keep the label unconditionally and let it earn its space — a container query on the dock band, or a flexible label with text-overflow (the widest label is 94.3px of ink, measured). Remove `isDesktop` from this component's prop surface entirely: a navigation control should not know what a desktop is.

defects.defect: The constitution's closed type matrix is violated: a display serif (Fraunces) is applied to a control label and to every dropdown option, where the matrix mandates Plus Jakarta Sans text-small non-bold.
defects.evidence: Measured computed font-family on trigger, trigger label span and all 7 option rows: `Fraunces, "Fraunces Fallback", serif` at 16.4px/400 (scratchpad/D-probe.json). Source: DockViewSelect.vue:69 `class="... text-small font-display font-normal ..."` and :91 `<SelectGroup class="text-small font-display">`. Spec quoted: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 "| control or label, including dropdown options | text-small | Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold |"; :78 "Fraunces owns display/identity, Plus Jakarta Sans owns headings/prose/controls ... P019's ... pair is the sole exception"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15 "Dropdown options remain Plus Jakarta Sans text-small control copy and non-bold." Visible in scratchpad/D-dock-open-light.png and the tracked shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png.
defects.mechanism: a per-instance family class overriding a closed role matrix; internally self-contradictory, since the file's own comment (lines 99-109) fights to keep option WEIGHT at 400 for that same law while setting the forbidden family
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, open the dock view menu, inspect any [role=option] -> font-family: Fraunces. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Delete `font-display` from lines 69 and 91. The role matrix already resolves control/label typography; no class is needed at all at these two sites.

defects.defect: The mobile trigger is a 33.34 CSS px tap target against a 44px floor that the producer already ships and already applies to the menu rows in the same frame; it is also label-free at that size.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit 390x844 isMobile/hasTouch: trigger rect {w:58.72, h:33.34}, innerText "" (scratchpad/D-probe.json). Producer floor exists and works elsewhere: glass-ui components/_shared/menu.css `.glass-menu-row { min-block-size: max(2rem, var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)) }` -> every measured option row h=44. Tracked audit corroborates: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md counts smallTapTargets 4 on safari-mobile-light /#/browse, a route whose only chrome is the dock. Governing law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:56 (PR-12) and :72 (§5.7) — "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities."
defects.mechanism: the producer's --touch-target token is consumed by menu rows but not by the dock trigger; the consumer never reconciles glyph size with operable size
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse at 390x844 with touch emulation; measure button.view-select-trigger -> 58.72 x 33.34. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe.mjs
defects.proposedCure: An invisible seat, not bigger chrome: give the trigger the producer's `--touch-target` min-block-size with the visible pill geometry unchanged (PR-12's stated cure). Restoring the label (D-4) fixes the second half, and removes the house-glyph "you are here" vs "go home" ambiguity PR-16 names.

defects.defect: The per-view accent — the design's explicitly declared "one counterweight" after the menu legend was excised — carries near-zero discriminative information: in dark mode all seven views collapse to near-white, and in light mode the chroma is unmatched by 2.31x.
defects.evidence: Measured --accent-view on all 7 user routes, both schemes (scratchpad/D-probe4.json). Light: L constant 0.470927, C 0.0814-0.1883, adjacent OKLab separation min 0.0608 / max 0.1226, global max pair 0.2794. Dark: L constant 0.958322, C 0.0206-0.0800, adjacent separation min 0.0152 (Home->Palettes, ~1 JND) / max 0.0522, global max pair 0.0923 — the entire dark gamut is smaller than light mode's smallest adjacent step. /browse resolves to oklch(0.47 0.096 89.8), a dark olive on a hot-pink ambient field (scratchpad/D2-focus-chromium.png). The file's own comment DockViewSelect.vue:37-47 killed the per-row legend because "seven simultaneous 40-degree-fan hues at matched L/C carried near-zero discriminative information"; the survivor is the same fan shown SEQUENTIALLY, which is strictly harder to identify. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:14 puts the dock in the neutral structural-glass tier; :178 "every other Dock label is neutral in both schemes."
defects.mechanism: colour promoted to carry an identity load it cannot carry once the WCAG/gamut guard equalises lightness; the argument that retired the legend was not applied to the trigger
defects.reproduction: walk /#/, /#/palettes, /#/browse, /#/extract, /#/mix, /#/generate, /#/gradient in light and dark reading getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)['--accent-view']. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe4.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Finish the W6-4 subtraction: retire the per-view hue from the dock entirely. Route identity is the WORD, which this design keeps deleting (D-2/D-4/D-6); restore the word everywhere and the hue has no job left. Chromatic identity stays where the constitution sanctions it — the ambient field and the single Palettes coordinate.

defects.defect: The product's primary navigation is a direction island: the trigger and every menu row compute `direction: ltr` inside an `rtl` document, so contents never mirror while the surrounding dock does.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit with document.documentElement.dir='rtl' on /#/gradient: trigDir "ltr", parentDir (.dock-face-content) "rtl"; full ancestor walk (.dock-layer-group, .dock-layer, .dock-layers, .dock-controls, .glass-dock, nav.dock-band, .app-layout, body, html) all "rtl". Child x-positions stay physical LTR: icon 834.2, label 862.2, chevron 934.3. Menu rows also direction "ltr" with symmetric padding 10px/10px, while panel PLACEMENT is RTL-aware (alignedTo "trigger-right") — placement and contents disagree. Corroborated by tracked shots/rtl-desktop/picker.png: the dock's outer order mirrors and the sibling ActionBarToggle mirrors its contents, while the view-select alone keeps icon-label-chevron in LTR order. Nothing in demo/ sets this; reka-ui's Select supplies dir defaulting to "ltr" and DockViewSelect.vue:51-56 never passes :dir. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150 — "chrome, navigation and layout | logical inline/block direction follows the document".
defects.mechanism: a physical direction pinned by a third-party default because no app-level direction provider exists; per-instance dir props would be the wrong cure
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, then document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl'); getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.view-select-trigger')).direction === 'ltr' while the parent is 'rtl'. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe5.mjs
defects.proposedCure: One app-level reka `ConfigProvider :dir` bound to the document direction, set once at the shell root — not a `:dir` prop on this instance, which would be a per-instance override needing repetition on every reka overlay in the app.

defects.defect: The view menu is a translucent glass surface over arbitrary route content, so the page beneath cuts a visible seam across the option list and half the options sit on a different value than the other half.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit /#/browse menu open: panelSurfaceAttr "glass", panelMaterialAttr "overlay", panelBg oklab(0.955861 0.009528 0.029646 / 0.7488), panelBackdrop blur(11px) saturate(1.6). Visible in scratchpad/D-dock-open-light.png: the Browse card's top edge runs straight across the panel so Home/Palettes/Browse/Extract sit on a visibly different value than Mix/Generate/Gradient. glass-ui SelectContent accepts a `surface` prop (select-BcBAyLXA.js props: surface, fieldHue, side, sideOffset, align, alignOffset); DockViewSelect.vue:90 passes only class="min-w-[12rem]". Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19 "Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well"; :82 "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."
defects.mechanism: the consumer never chose a material tier, so an overlay inherits a see-through default whose effective contrast is whatever route content happens to be underneath
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse, open the dock view menu, observe the horizontal seam across the option list where the Browse card's top edge passes behind it (scratchpad/D-dock-open-light.png).
defects.proposedCure: `surface="opaque"` on SelectContent. A menu is a specimen well (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:16), not a pane of glass; the producer already offers the correct rung and the consumer simply never selected it.

defects.defect: The admin mode toggle is a command wearing `role="option"` inside a route-selection listbox, keyed by a magic sentinel string in the ViewId namespace, with a label that flips from a destination noun to an action phrase in the same slot.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:124-141 `<SelectItem value="__admin_toggle__" ... hide-indicator>` rendering `Admin` or `Back to app`; demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:70-77 `if (id === "__admin_toggle__") { toggleAdminMode(); return; }`. Its aria-selected is permanently false-by-construction because the choice never becomes the combobox value. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:96-98, the global grammar select -> tune -> commit, where "Selection changes the active specimen without committing it"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:71 "Subtraction precedes explanation."
defects.mechanism: a command placed inside a selection model, guarded by string equality against a sentinel that shares a type with real route names
defects.reproduction: open the dock view menu while admin-authenticated; the last row is a verb inside a list of destinations and selecting it never updates the combobox value.
defects.proposedCure: The mode switch is not a destination. Once D-2's `audience` field exists on viewSchema, admin routes become ordinary rows gated by authority and the toggle row — together with its sentinel, its divider and its dual label — is deleted outright.

defects.defect: The separator is hand-rolled with a different recipe while the producer's `SelectSeparator` sits unused in the same import barrel; it is also a role-less bare div inside a listbox subtree, and PR-05 rules the divider REMOVE regardless.
defects.evidence:
demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:123 `
`; demo/ui/select/index.ts:1 re-exports `SelectSeparator`; producer recipe (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/select-BcBAyLXA.js) is `-mx-1 my-1 h-px bg-[color-mix(in_srgb,var(--foreground)_12%,transparent)]` — three differences including the missing `-mx-1`, so the hand-rolled line stops short of the panel's --overlay-pad-inline. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:69 (§5.4) and :49 (PR-05 REMOVE).
defects.mechanism: reaching past the design system for a primitive the design system already exports into the same file's scope
defects.reproduction: read DockViewSelect.vue:123 against demo/ui/select/index.ts:1 and the producer class string; the rendered rule is inset differently from every other glass-ui separator.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the divider (PR-05 REMOVE — the admin row already carries gold ink and a Shield glyph, so material already states the boundary). If a separator ever is needed here, use the exported `SelectSeparator`, never a hand-rolled div.

defects.defect: Three per-instance overrides reach into producer internals: an arbitrary-variant selector into glass-ui's own DOM, a duplicated-plus-drifted row padding, and a magic min-width.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:69 `[&>span]:line-clamp-none` cancels glass-ui's internal line-clamp-1 (self-documented at :57-59 as awaiting a `clampLabel` producer prop); :96 and :126 `class="py-1.5 px-2.5"` where `py-1.5` duplicates the producer value verbatim (menuRowClass-Nh7CtMON.js: "... items-center py-1.5") and `px-2.5` overrides the producer's `px-2` — measured padding-left 10px vs the producer's 8px; :90 `min-w-[12rem]` overrides --overlay-min-width / min-w-(--reka-select-trigger-width). Owner edict 5: style at the root component level, never per-instance overrides.
defects.mechanism: consumer-side correction of producer defaults instead of producer-side props; a filed ask shipped as a permanent hack
defects.reproduction: inspect any [role=option] in the open menu -> padding-left 10px (producer default 8px); inspect the trigger label span -> the producer's line-clamp is cancelled with no replacement constraint.
defects.proposedCure: Land the filed `clampLabel` prop in glass-ui and delete the arbitrary-variant selector; delete the duplicate `py-1.5` and the `px-2.5` drift so rows use the producer ladder; replace `min-w-[12rem]` with the producer's overlay min-width token (see D-13 for why 12rem is wrong on the measurements anyway).

defects.defect: The menu panel is 2.04x wider than its widest row's ink, and the in-file comment justifying the hand-set floor is contradicted by measurement.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:89-90 comment "kept wider than --menu-min-w — long view-option labels need the space" over `min-w-[12rem]`. Measured webkit /#/browse menu open: panel 192.0px, row 174.0px, widest row content 94.3px (Generate); Home 70.9, Palettes 85.0, Browse 81.2, Extract 79.7, Mix 52.3, Gradient 92.1. Every row carries 79.7px of empty inline space = 46% of the row. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:5 "they do not excuse a mechanically large gap"; :73 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent."
defects.mechanism: a magic number preserved by a comment that was never re-measured
defects.reproduction: open the dock view menu and measure the panel against each row's inner flex span width. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe2.mjs (geometry block).
defects.proposedCure: Delete `min-w-[12rem]` and let the panel hug its content against the producer's overlay min-width; if a floor is genuinely wanted it is the trigger width, which the producer already supplies as `min-w-(--reka-select-trigger-width)`.

defects.defect: The open menu panel overlaps the dock's reserved band by 10.9px, so a card clips the band the constitution declares must be clipped by neither mask nor card.
defects.evidence: Measured webkit /#/browse menu open: .glass-dock y 9.4 -> bottom 71.4; select-content y 60.5 -> bottom 388.7; overlap 10.9px. Mechanism: glass-ui SelectContent defaults sideOffset: 0 (select-BcBAyLXA.js) and DockViewSelect.vue:90 never sets it, while the trigger's bottom (56.4) sits inside the dock's own padding. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:178 "The dock is its own top band, fully visible, focusable, and clipped by neither mask nor card"; :30 "The top dock owns a reserved band."
defects.mechanism: a zero side offset measured from the trigger rather than from the band, inside a container with its own padding
defects.reproduction: open the dock view menu at 1440x900 and compare .glass-dock bottom (71.4) to [data-slot=select-content] y (60.5).
defects.proposedCure: The offset must be measured from the dock band, not the trigger: expose the band's bottom as the anchor (a producer `collisionBoundary`/offset seam) so any dock popover clears the reserved band by construction, rather than each consumer guessing a sideOffset.

defects.defect: Icon and label are on two different clocks: the glyph plays a `mode="out-in"` morph while SelectValue swaps instantly, so every route change shows a hole where the glyph was while the label already reads the new destination.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:75-87 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` around the icon; :87 `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with no transition. demo/styles/animations.css:104-121 — leave-active runs --duration-fast before enter-active's spring begins. Two halves of one 128px control desynchronised by construction.
defects.mechanism: out-in sequencing applied to one child of a composite control whose sibling is untransitioned
defects.reproduction: switch views from the dock at 1440px with motion enabled and watch the trigger: the word changes first, the glyph slot empties, then the new glyph springs in.
defects.proposedCure: Treat the trigger as one morph unit: key the whole icon+label group on currentView with a single transition, or drop mode="out-in" for a crossfade so the two halves share one timeline. Motion is already correctly tokenized via the shared vj-morph family — the fix is choreography, not new keyframes.

defects.defect: The icon is typed `unknown` in both the prop surface and the ViewEntry interface, widening a schema field that viewSchema already types as `Component`, and ViewEntry carries an open `[k: string]: unknown` index signature.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:73 `icon: Component;` vs demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:8-12 `export interface ViewEntry { id: ViewId; label: string; icon: unknown; [k: string]: unknown; }` and demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:19 `currentIcon: unknown;`. `<component :is="unknown">` type-checks against nothing and can only fail at render.
defects.mechanism: a well-typed schema field widened to `unknown` at the composable boundary, plus an index signature that turns a shape into a bag
defects.reproduction: pass any non-component value as `currentIcon` — it type-checks and fails only at render time.
defects.proposedCure: Import `Component` from vue and use it in both places; delete the `[k: string]: unknown` index signature so ViewEntry is a shape (`{ id: ViewId; label: string; icon: Component }`) derived from PaneConfig rather than a bag.

defects.defect: Two v-model idioms coexist in one 162-line component and `update:open` is declared twice.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:25-33: defineEmits declares both `update:modelValue` and `update:open`, then `const open = defineModel<boolean>("open", { default: false })` registers the `open` prop and the `update:open` emit again. Meanwhile modelValue uses a manual `emit(...)` with a hand-written `as string` cast at :55.
defects.mechanism: redundant declaration plus two conventions for the same job in one file
defects.reproduction: read lines 25-33 and 55 together.
defects.proposedCure: Pick one idiom. Convert modelValue to `defineModel<string>()` and delete the manual emit, the `as string` cast, and the now-redundant `update:open` entry in defineEmits.

defects.defect: Eight of fifteen enumerated states are unhandled or visually broken: empty, loading, error, disabled, focused, selected, overflow/truncation, RTL, forced-colors and 200% zoom.
defects.evidence: Template read plus measurement. empty: `v-for="entry in viewEntries"` (line 92) with no v-else. loading: `pm.isAdminAuthenticated` resolves async so the admin row pops in untransitioned. error: `inject(SESSION_PORT_KEY)!` (line 35) is a non-null assertion with no fallback — a missing provider is a render crash. disabled: never passed although the producer supports and styles it (`data-[disabled]:opacity-disabled`). focused: D-1 measured box-shadow none / outline none. selected: D-3 measured zero delta. overflow/truncation: line 69 removes the producer clamp and supplies nothing. RTL: D-8 measured direction ltr inside dir=rtl. forced-colors: selection delta 0 and the trigger glyph keeps its custom olive instead of adopting the system palette (scratchpad/D2-forced-colors.png). zoom 200%: D-4 measured label "".
defects.mechanism: the component was designed for one state (populated, desktop, LTR, pointer, light) and the remainder were never composed
defects.reproduction: per-state repros are given in D-1, D-3, D-4, D-8; empty/loading/error/disabled are source reads with no rendered branch to observe.
defects.proposedCure: Compose the missing states before restyling the handled one: an empty branch, a disabled pass-through to the producer, an injected-port failure path instead of `!`, and a truncation rule to replace the clamp that line 69 deletes. The seat brief's own rule applies — a state that was never designed is a design defect, and this component has eight.

defects.defect: The `Palettes` pastel-rainbow identity coordinate renders as a dark, 80-degree, near-two-tone magenta wash rather than the pastel rainbow the constitution names.
defects.evidence: DockViewSelect.vue:116 applies `.palettes-ramp-text` (demo/styles/utils.css:192). Measured live resolution: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.470927 0.188343 329.834), oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834), oklch(0.470927 0.188343 49.834))` with background-clip:text, color:transparent — L 0.4709 across an 85px word spanning 80 degrees of hue. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:17 files it under "Watercolor/data ... pastel Palettes identity" and :23 calls it "the pastel-rainbow identity" with W19 owning the Dock witness. Rendered result in scratchpad/D-dock-open-light.png reads as one magenta-to-purple gradient.
defects.mechanism: upstream: the WCAG 4.5:1 text floor in the palettes-ramp resolver pushes L to 0.47, which is a dark tone, not a pastel; the 3 stops span only 80 degrees so no rainbow reads at 85px
defects.reproduction: open the dock view menu and read getComputedStyle on span.palettes-ramp-text -> the three-stop gradient above. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe2.mjs (geometry.ramp).
defects.proposedCure: Owner is upstream (demo/color-session/palettes-ramp.ts + useViewAccents), not this file. Either widen the arc and lift lightness so the coordinate actually reads as the pastel rainbow the constitution names, or amend the constitution's wording to match what the contrast floor permits — the two must not disagree while W19 owns this witness.
